     economic journey its strengths, challenges and emerging opportunities. In a rapidly
     evolving economic environment, sound policy must be guided by credible analysis
     and a clear understanding of ground realities. This publication provides that essential
     foundation.

            I am pleased to note that the Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Assam is bringing out
      the annual publication Economic Survey, Assam 2025-26, which presents a comprehensive and
      up-to-date overview of the economic scenario of the State. The publication reflects the evolving
      economic landscape of Assam and highlights recent trends, achievements, and challenges across
      various sectors.
            The Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Assam serves as the nodal agency for the
      systematic collection, compilation, and analysis of statistical data relating to the State's economy.
      The Economic Survey, Assam 2025-26 provides an in-depth assessment of the performance of
      all major sectors, supported by empirical evidence, analytical insights, and reliable data. It offers a
      factual basis for understanding the growth trajectory and developmental priorities of the State.

      planners, administrators, researchers, and other stakeholders. By facilitating informed decision-
      making and effective policy formulation, the Survey will contribute meaningfully to the pursuit of
      sustainable and inclusive development in Assam.

                                     FOREWORD

          The Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Assam publishes the Economic
    Survey, Assam annually to present a factual and objective overview of the State's
    economic performance. This survey provides an in-depth analysis of Government
    initiatives, including departmental activities, schemes and programmes aimed at
    fostering development. Additionally, it captures key economic trends and
    movements, offering stakeholders a valuable resource for informed decision-
    making and policy formulation.
         In the current edition of Economic Survey, Assam '2025-26 efforts have been
    made to present and review the latest developments and trends in the sectoral
    performance of the State's economy. The information for this publication has been
    meticulously collected from various State Govt. Departments/Ministries and
    Departments of the Government of India. The Directorate sincerely acknowledges

CHAPTER-I
                      ASSAM ECONOMY – AN OVERVIEW

AREA AND POPULATION:




A
        ssam, a state situated between in the North-East region of India- bordering seven
        states namely - Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland,
        Tripura and West Bengal and two countries, namely Bhutan and Bangladesh. The
geographical area of the state is 78,438 sq. km of which 98.4 percent area is rural. Assam
shares about 2.4% of the country’s landmass, providing shelter to 2.6% of India’s
population as per census, 2011. For administration and revenue purposes, the State has
presently 35 districts, including six newly created districts namely Biswanath, Charaideo,
Hojai, South Salmara, West Karbi Anglong, Bajali, Tamulpur and Majuli.

   Assam is a state of heterogeneous population with socio-cultural and ethnic diversity.
According to the Census of India, 2011 the population of Assam was 312.05 lakh of which
159.39 lakh were male and 152.66 lakh were female. The decadal growth rate of the state
population during 2001-2011 was 17.07% against 17.68% growth for the country as a
whole. Out of the total population, 86% population lived in rural areas and 14% population
in urban areas of the state, while the percentage of rural population of the state was higher
than all India average (69%).However, the urban population in the state had increased
from 12.9% in 2001 to 14% in 2011.The density of the population of Assam in 2011 was
398 person per sq.km. as compare to 340 person in 2001. The sex ratio (number of female
per thousand male) of Assam had increased to 958 in 2011 from 935 in 2001.

STATE INCOME:

   The estimates of the State Domestic Product provide a clear picture of the magnitude
and direction of change in the level of economic development of the state over time. Assam
has emerged as one of the potential states in the country, registering robust growth in
terms of Gross Value Added (GVA) and Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP).

   Economic performance is generally assessed by the pace at which economic activity
expands. By this measure, Assam ranks among the high-performing states in India.
Sustained economic growth contributes significantly to improving the quality of life of the
people, and Assam has consistently demonstrated better performance on this front.

   According to the advance estimates, the nominal GSDP of Assam for FY 2025-26 (AE)
is expected to reach ₹7,45,293 crore, as compared to ₹6,43,383 crore in FY 2024-25 (QE),
reflecting a growth of 15.84 percent. The real GSDP for FY 2025-26 is estimated at
₹3,84,433 crore, against ₹3,49,100 crore in FY 2024-25 (QE), registering a growth of
10.12 percent. As per the projected estimates, the GSDP at current prices for FY 2026-27
is expected to reach ₹8.71 lakh crore reflecting a growth of 16.93 percent over the
preceding year.

   Assam has also improved its share in India’s GDP at current prices from 1.65 percent
in FY 2016-17 to 2.09 percent in FY 2025-26 (AE). At constant (2011-12) prices, its
contribution has increased from 1.64 percent to 1.90 percent during the same period.




    4
                           Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



   Further, the Per Capita Income of Assam at current prices for FY 2025 26(AE) is
estimated at ₹1,85,429, compared to ₹1,60,417 in FY 2024 25(QE), showing an increase
of 15.59 percent. The Per Capita Income of Assam at constant prices for the FY 2025-26
is estimated to be ₹93,351 compared to ₹85,503 for the FY 2024-25 (QE), registering an
increase of 9.2 percent.

STATE FINANCE:

   The state expects to earn revenue receipts of around Rs. 117225.97 Crore in FY 2025-
26 (BE) against Rs. 96907.91 crore in FY- 2024-25 (RE) with a positive growth of 20.97
percent. Rs 43184.28 crore is expected to be earned from the State’s resources and Rs
74041.69 Crore from the Centre in FY 2025-26 (BE). In FY 2023-24, the share of the
State’s tax and share of fund from the Centre to total revenue receipts was 37.24 percent
and 62.76 percent. In FY 2025-26 (BE), the share of the State’s tax to total revenue
receipts is expected to be 36.83 percent.

   It is expected that the state will earn tax revenue of Rs. 34823.04 crore in FY 2025-
26 (BE), with a growth of 15.87 percent. The collection of Tax Revenue has exhibited an
average annual growth of 12.95 percent over the last 5 years due to various measures
taken by the Government to augment its own tax resources.

   The state expects to earn non tax revenue of Rs. 8361.24 crore in FY 2025-26 (BE),
with a growth of 56.24 percent. During the last four years, the collection of non-tax
revenue has increased steadily at an average rate of 19.38 percent due to collective effort
of the State Government. The share of non-tax revenue to total revenue receipts was
15.11 percent in FY 2024-25, and it is expected to rise upto 19.36 percent in FY 2025-26
(BE).

   Total revenue expenditure of the state has grown to Rs. 99907.06 Crore in 2024-25
(Pre Actual) as against Rs. 94162.90 Crore in 2023-24. Total non-debt capital expenditure
has grown from Rs. 21508.73 crore in 2023-24 to Rs. 26408.77 crore in 2024-25 with a
growth of 22.76 per cent. Share of non-debt capital expenditure has increased from 3.74
percent in 2022-23 to 4.11 percent in 2024-25.

   During the period from 2019-20 to 2024-25, average annual rate of repayment of loans
is significantly higher (46.93%) than that of borrowings (25.24%). This indicate
sustainable financing through improvement in Net Loan Position of the State by dint of
productive investments and consequently enhanced economic activities. Debt to GSDP
ratio over the last four years from 2021-22 to 2024-25 have also been consistently lower
(23% – 25%) than the national average.

AGRICULTURE:

  Agriculture plays a vital role in the economy of the State. Agriculture is the main source
of occupation and livelihood support to 70% rural population.

  The State Agriculture department has issued 164745 Nos. of Kissan Credit Card (KCC)
and sanctioned limit amount is 2860.47 (Rs. In Crores) in the year 2024-25.



                                                                                      5
                             Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




  The Area under autumn rice is 0.39 lakh hectare, winter rice is 18.65 lakh hectare and
summer rice is 4.01 lakh hectare. The total rice area is 22.86 lakh hectares in the year
2024-25.

  The total crop/Gross cropped area is 40.88 lakh hectare and net crop area shown is
27.58 lakh hectare in the year 2024-25. The intensity of crop in percentage is 148.17 in
the year 2024-25.

  The Yield rate of autumn rice is 1436 Kg/hectare, winter rice is 2341 Kg/hectare and
summer rice is 3051 Kg/hectare. The Yield rate of total pulses is 805 Kg/hectare and total
Oil Seed (Excluding Coconut) is 781 Kg/hectare.

  Under Prime Minister Fasal Bima Yojona (PMFBY) 263590 hectare area are covered in
Kharif season in 2023 Year along with 397088 Nos. of farmers covered.

LIVESTOCK, ANIMAL HUSBANDRY AND DAIRY DEVELOPMENT:

   The cattle population constitutes the largest group, with more than ten million
counts as per the 20 th livestock census 2019. Out of the total cattle,
indigenous/non-descript cattle comprise 1.10 Cr, while the crossbreed cattle
population comprises 7.69 lakhs. In the census, 4.22 lakhs buffalo were found
while sheep were counted to be 3.32 lakhs in numbers. Goats and pigs comprised
about 43.15 lakhs and 21 lakhs numbers, respectively during the 2019 livestock
census.
   The total production of milk in the state for the year 2024-25(P) was estimated
at 1224.08 million litres as against 1149.71 million litres in the previous year
2023-24, thereby recording a growth rate of 6.46 % in 2024-25(P).
   The total production of egg during the period 2024-25(P) for both (fowl and
duck) was 642 (in million numbers), which was 622.86 (in million numbers) in
the previous year 2023-24, thereby showing a growth in egg production by
3.07% over the previous year.
   The total meat production in 2024-25(P) was 69.49 (in ‘000’ Tonnes) and
68.68 (in ‘000’ Tonnes) in the year 2023-24, thereby showing an increase of
1.17% in the year 2024-25(P) over the previous year.


FISHERY:

    The Fishery sector is now emerging as one of the important sector in the state playing
very significant roles in socio-economics development if the state provides rural
employment, nutritional support and livelihood security thereby reducing poverty and
promoting health and more than 90% of the total population of the state consumes fish
as a staple diet contributing toward a high demand of fish throughout the year.

    The Fish production in the state has reached a level of 5.29 lakh MT during the year
2024-25 against the estimated nutritional demand of 5.25 lakh MT. The demand for Fish
for the state was calculated at 15.22 Kg/yr. per capita consumption taking 90% of the
fish-eating population out of the estimated population of the state.




   6
                            Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



    In the year 2023-24(QE), the contribution of the Fishery and Aquaculture sector to the
State’s GSDP at the current price was Rs. 2637315 lakh and Rs. 759817 lakh at constant
(2011-12) price respectively. The share of the fishing and aquaculture subsector to GSVA
of the agriculture and allied GSVA account for 21.7 percent and 4.7 percent of total GSDP
at current prices.

    Assam is endowed with vast water resource covering 2.59 lakh hectares. The mighty
Brahmaputra and the Barak with their tributaries spread up to 11214 Km in 2024-25 as a
riverine Fishery. There are 216 freshwater fish species and over 50 fish species having
ornamental importance.

FORESTRY:

    Assam is a rainbow state with blue rivers and green hills with a unique bio-diversity
treasure house of rare flora, fauna and forest. Forestry is a vital sector of the state. In the
language of Ahom ruler, Assam is the "Golden land". The total Recorded Forest Area in
Assam is 26,836 square km. which is 34.21% of the total geographical area of Assam, as
per India State Forest Report, 2023. Efforts to build a green economy in the state, 8 June,
2023 would be marked as a red-letter day since on this day Hon'ble Chief Minister of
Assam announced the launch of "Amrit Briksha Andolon", 2023. To create a revolution
among the people in respect of strengthening the economy through forest/plantation of
commercially viable trees, for scientific plantation, the focus has been laid on commercial
tree species suitable for timber, plywood making, medicinal and some more valuable trees
like Chandan, Baga Chandan, and fruits which are abundantly grown in Assam. In this
"Amrit Bikshya Andolon", Assam has recorded 9 Guinness records which is one of the
milestones for creating forest out side Recorded Forest Areas.

    At present the world famous one horned Rhino Protection in Assam is one of the
challenging tasks before the Government. Due to strong steps taken by the Govt. the
poaching of one horned Rhino in the state has significantly decreased. With respect to
revenue collection during 2024-25, total Rs. 567.75 crore revenue has been earned by the
Forest department compared to Rs.564.88 Crore during 2023-24. For the year 2025-26,
revenue collected was Rs.371.60 Crore out of a target of Rs.997.00 Crore (till December,
2025).

    In State Compensatory Afforestation and Fund Management and Planning Authority
(State CAMPA) forest department accelerates different activities for preservation of natural
forest, management of wildlife, infrastructure development in the sector and allied works
and recorded Rs. 10266.62 lakh financial achievement during 2024-25 as reported by
PCCF cum Head of Forest Force, Assam.

    The contribution by Forestry and Logging sector toward GSDP was Rs. 6,91,592.00
lakh in 2024-25 (QE) against Rs.6,70,223.00 lakh in 2023-24 (PE) at current price
registering a 3.19% growth.

INDUSTRY:


  Industrial development in Assam has its genesis in the colonial period with the
establishment of tea plantations, coal mining, plywood industries and hydrocarbon
exploration. The State is richly endowed with natural resources including petroleum,
natural gas, coal, limestone and other minerals, which continue to form the backbone of
its industrial economy. Tea remains a principal industry, with Assam contributing more
than fifty per cent of the country’s total production and providing substantial employment.


                                                                                         7
                                Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




     The industrial sector constitutes a significant component of the State economy,
contributing approximately one-third of Gross State Domestic Product. As per advance
estimates for 2025–26, the sector has recorded robust growth, led by construction,
utilities, mining and manufacturing. Manufacturing activity has demonstrated a consistent
recovery in the post-pandemic period, as reflected in the upward movement of the Index
of Industrial Production. The organised manufacturing sector, as captured under the
Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) indicates steady expansion in terms of factories,
employment, output and value addition.

     Mining and quarrying continue to be major revenue-generating activities, with crude
oil, natural gas, coal and limestone contributing substantially to the State exchequer. To
strengthen the industrial ecosystem, the Government of Assam has accorded priority to
the development of industrial infrastructure through industrial estates, parks and common
facilities, supported by institutions such as AIDC and AIIDC.

     The State has implemented a comprehensive policy framework including the Industrial
and Investment Policy, sector-specific policies on ethanol, electronics, logistics and
warehousing, and customised incentive packages for mega projects. These initiatives are
complemented by centrally sponsored schemes such as UNNATI, PMEGP, PMFME and PM
Vishwakarma, and flagship state programmes including CMAAA and APART, which
collectively promote MSMEs, agribusiness, entrepreneurship and employment generation.

     In addition to core industries, Assam has witnessed diversification into rubber, coffee,
sericulture, handloom, khadi and tourism. These sectors play a vital role in rural
development, women’s empowerment and preservation of traditional industries. Overall,
Assam’s industrial development strategy reflects a balanced, inclusive and sustainable
approach aimed at accelerating economic growth, enhancing investment and generating
gainful employment across the State.


POWER:

     In Assam the entire power industry of the State was managed by “Assam State
Electricity Board (ASEB)” up to 10th December, 2004 after that it was divided into the
following three entities to meet the power requirements of the State.
1.        The Assam Power Distribution Company Limited (APDCL)
2.        The Assam Electricity Grid Corporation Limited (AEGCL)
3.        The Assam Power Generation Corporation Limited (APGCL)

     From 2022-23 to 2024-25, the Gross State Value Added (GSVA) from electricity sector
of Assam has grown at an average rate of 20.62 per cent per year. During the same period,
impressive growth in major sectors that are directly related to power has such as
Manufacturing (10%), Communication and broadcasting (15.76%), Hotels& Restaurants
(22.61%) have also exhibited impressive growth patterns.

     As the economy of the state has regained its momentum in the post Covid period,
electricity consumption in the state has also rapidly increased. From 2022-23 to 2024-25,
the total power consumption (in MU) has increased by a staggering 13.91% per year.




      8
                           Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



During this period, the per capita domestic consumption of power (both domestic &
commercial) has also increased by 9.29% per annum.

   As the economy of the state has gained its momentum, electricity consumption in the
state has also rapidly increased. From 2022-23 to 2024-25, the total power consumption
(in MU) has increased by a staggering 13.91% per year. During this period, the per capita
domestic consumption of power (both domestic & commercial) has also increased by
9.29% per annum. Average Purchase Rate of power has also decreased from Rs. 6.63 in
2023-24 to Rs. 5.97 in 2024-25.

   Total energy requirement of the State during 2024-25 is at 15556 MU and peak
demand during the year is at 2684 MW. Average growth of commercial consumption of
power in the State during the period 2022-23 to 2024-25 is 8.59% which is 4 times higher
than the growth of domestic consumption at 2.01% during the same period. During 2024-
25 domestic purpose has the highest share in power consumption (48.40%) followed by
Commercial (16.32%), Industrial (16.24%) and Other Purpose (16.21%).


TRANSPORT AND COMMUNICATION:

    During FY 2024-25, the Transport and Communication sector accounted for 5.27 per
cent of the Gross State Value Added (GSVA), and its contribution is projected to increase
to 5.42 per cent by FY 2026-27. Over the last four years, the sector has recorded robust
and consistent growth, supported by substantial expansion in road infrastructure, rising
motor vehicle density, and improved public transport services.

    The road network in Assam comprises of total 74929.10 km consisting of 5612.79 km
national highways and 69316.31 km of roads under PWD in Assam as on 31.03.2025. Out
of 69316.31 km of PWD roads State Highway comprises 5120 km, Major District road
comprises 8638 km, urban road comprises 3181.97 km and rural road comprises 52376.34
km.

   On the front of railways, Assam at present has total railway route length 2571.19 km
and the running track kilometre of Railways (i.e. lengh of tracks under operation) under
broad gauge railway is 3153 kms as on 31.03.2025. Electrified routes have increased from
2594 Km in 2023-24 to 3374 Km in 2024-25.

    Significant progress has been achieved under programmes such as PMGSY, leading to
enhanced rural and inter-district connectivity. Growth in rail electrification, expansion of
air transport capacity, and modernisation of inland water transport have further
strengthened the transport network. On the communication front, expansion of postal
services and steady growth in telecom subscribers have improved digital and information
connectivity, thereby supporting economic activity and inclusive development across the
State.

   Further, Transport Department of Assam has collected revenue of Rs. 1893.83 crore
during the financial year 2024-25 which exihibits a growth of 7.20 percent from the
previous year’s collection of Rs. 1716.14 crore.




                                                                                       9
                                Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




   Wireless subscribers in the State has increased by 6.92 % during the period 2023 to
2025. During the same period, number of wireline subscribers has increased by 28.73
percent.

LABOUR, ELPLOYMENT AND WAGES:


    Labour is one of the basic factors in the factors in the process of production. In the
State, the total employment in the public and private sector establishments as per the
Employment Market Information (EMI) programme up to the 31 st March 2024 was
11,97,700 Nos. ( in public sector 4,86,500 nos. and in private sector 7,11,200 nos.) Where
it was 11,54,000 nos. ( in public sector 4,90,000 nos. and in private sector 6,64,000nos.)
in 2023, which shows an overall 3.64% increase in employment in the year 2024.

    The manufacturing sector plays the most significant role in employment generation in
Assam. As reported by the Chief Inspector of Factories (CIF), Assam till 2024-25there
were 8,858 nos. of factories in the state with 3,12,982 Nos. of employment compared to
8,620 Nos. of factories and 3,43,824 Nos. of employment in the year 2023-24 showing an
increase of 2.69 % in         number of factories and 9.85% decrease in the context of
employment.
    Handloom & Textile Industry also plays a significant role in the employment generation of the
state economy. During the year 2024-25, this sector has 680687 nos. of weavers as part-time and
78642 nos. as whole-time weavers which are a very remarkable performance of this sector.

    In rural areas, the unemployment rate was 3.5%, whereas in urban areas, the
unemployment rate was 7.4 % percent as per PLFS, 2023-24, Govt. of India. The
unemployment rate of India was 2.5% in 2022-23 in rural areas and 5.1 % in urban areas
during the same period.

    The size of registered educated job seekers is considerably low as compared previous
year. From the records of the live register of Employment Exchanges, during 2024 ,the
registered educated job seekers stood at 1,06,044 nos. against 8,56,546 Nos. during the
year 2023.

    It is to be worth mentioning here that the Govt. of Assam has launched an online portal
https://sewasetu.assam.gov.in/w.e.f         27th    September     2021for     live   registration   of
educated unemployment youths and since then the manual process has been completely
discontinued.

    In 2024, the Assam Government continued its massive recruitment drive, exceeding its promise
of 1 lakh jobs to over 1.25 Lakh plus total appointments by late 2024. Key 2024 distributions included
385 candidates in October, 41 in the Education Department in July and significant recruitment in
P&RD and technical roles etc.


BANKING:

    According to the State level Banker’s Committee Report, the number of reporting Bank
Offices of all Scheduled Commercial Banks in Assam has been increased to 3185 as on




   10
                            Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



March 2025 from 3053 as on March 2024. With further expansion of the banking network,
the dependence per bank office in Assam has reduced to 24.19 sq. km per branch as on
March 2025, compared to 25.69 sq. km in March 2023 and 38.31 sq. km in March 2015,
reflecting improved spatial penetration of banking services across the State. Average
Population served by per bank branch in the State as on as on 31 st March, 2025 is 9622
against all-India average of 7,390 persons per bank branch using 2011 census population
and SLBC report /RBI data on number of all India bank branches.

   The expansion of banking facilities in the State has augmented not only in respect of
volume of deposits but also in respect of disbursement of credit. The aggregate deposit with
scheduled commercial banks in Assam, which was Rs. 223478 as on March 2024 has
increased to Rs. 233618 in March 2024. The total volume of credit disbursed by the banks
has been increased to Rs. 153491 Crore in March 2025 from Rs. 145906 Crore in March
2024, thereby, recorded a growth of 5.19 percent. Using Census 2011 population as the
base, the per capita deposit in Assam increased to ₹74,867.36 and per capita credit
increased to ₹49,189.73 as on 31 March 2025. This represents a growth of 10.53
percent in per capita deposit and a significant 34.83 percent growth in per capita
credit over March 2022, indicating improved credit deepening in the State. The Credit-
Deposit Ratio (CDR) of the SCB in the State as on 31 st March 2025 was 71.31 percent as
per the SLBC Report, as against 79.51 percent at all India level . However, the State Level
Banker’s Committee Report (as on 31st March, 2023) reveals that out of 33 districts in
Assam, 26 districts have crossed the 60 percent C-D Ratio benchmark fixed for Scheduled
Commercial Banks. Seven districts—Dima Hasao, Hailakandi, Cachar, Hojai, Kokrajhar,
Kamrup Metro and Chirang—fall within the 40–60 percent range, indicating moderate
performance that requires monitoring and targeted intervention. No district is below 40
percent, which reflects an overall improvement in credit deployment across the State.
Focused efforts are required in these seven districts to enable them to cross the benchmark
level.

RURAL DEVELOPMENT:

    The Panchayat and Rural Development (P&RD) Department, Government of Assam, is
responsible for poverty alleviation, livelihood enhancement, and strengthening of
Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). The Department implements a range of wage
employment,     self-employment,    infrastructure   development,    and   social   security
programmes aimed at improving the quality of life in rural areas.

    Key flagship initiatives include MGNREGA, which continues to generate substantial
wage employment with increasing participation of women and focused interventions in tea
garden areas, and PMAY-G, which has significantly improved rural housing by sanctioning
and completing a large number of pucca houses for eligible households. Social security
coverage is provided through NSAP and state-sponsored pension schemes, ensuring
financial support to the elderly, widows, and persons with disabilities.

    The 15th Finance Commission Grants have strengthened decentralized planning and
infrastructure development at the Gram Panchayat level, while Mission Amrit Sarovar


                                                                                      11
                             Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




(Assam Model) has contributed to water conservation, irrigation, and livelihood generation
through community-managed water bodies.

    Through the Assam State Rural Livelihoods Mission (ASRLM), large-scale mobilization
of Self-Help Groups has empowered rural women via access to credit, enterprise
promotion, farm and non-farm livelihoods, and social security inclusion. Complementary
initiatives such as skill development, self-employment training, and capacity building of
PRIs through SIPRD further reinforce effective rural governance and sustainable
development.

   In Assam, the number of Government/provincialized under department of Elementary

in 2022-23. Likewise in the Upper Primary level, the drop-out rate is 8.2% in 2024-25 and
it was 9.27 in 2023-24, in secondary (Class IX-X) IT IS 17.5% dropped from 25.1%. The
Transition Rate from primary to upper primary in the state is 90.3%. In 2024-25 total
enrolment in lower primary schools is 1916217 and the same for upper primary is
1654836.

Important Features:



            A
          ssam, a state situated between 24008’N-27059’N latitude in the northeast
          region of India, is the gateway to the region, the premier, largest and the most
          vibrant of the eight states comprising the Northeast. It borders seven states
namely, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Tripura and West
Bengal and two countries, namely Bhutan and Bangladesh. Its topographical asymmetry
underscored by the Barail hill range sandwiched between two valleys – the Brahmaputra
and the Barak, named after the two dominant rivers. Assam has a total geographical area
of 78,438 sq. km (30285 sq. mile), occupying 2.4% of India’s landmass, providing shelter
to 2.6% of India’s population. For administration and revenue purposes, the State has
presently 35 districts, including six newly created districts namely Biswanath, Charaideo,
Hojai, South Salmara, West Karbi Anglong, Majuli, Bajali and Tamulpur.

life expectancy at birth 68.60 where life expectancy of Male is 66.90 and Female is 70.70.
Life expectancy at birth in India is Age 70.30 in 2019-23.

Population: Rural and Urban:
   As per Population Census, 2011, the rural population of the State was 85.9 percent of
the total population. This percentage was much higher than that for All-India (69.0
percent). The proportion of rural population in the State decreased from 87 percent in
2001 to 86 percent in 2011. Out of the total rural population 51.03 percent were male and
48.97 were female. As per the Population Census, 2011, around 14 percent of the total
population of the State was living in urban areas. The proportion of urban population in
the State increased from 12.9 percent in 2001 to 14 percent in 2011.

Assam Highlights – 2011 census:
    The Census Directorate of Assam highlighted the following observation after
completion of the Population Census, 2011.Growth of population in the state during 1971-
2011 is 113.12 percent against the national growth rate of 120.77 percent during this
period.
     Assam ranks 14th in size of population among the states of India.
     Assam ranks 15th in density among the states of India.
     Assam ranks 15th in sex-ratio among the states of India.
     Assam ranks 26th in literacy among the states of India.

SLUM POPULATION:
    As per Census, 2011, thirty-one (31) towns in Assam were reporting slums against
2613 towns reporting slums in India as a whole. According to the Census of India, 2011,
the Slum population stands at 1,97,266 of which 1,01,424 are males and 95,842 females.
The Slum population accounts for 0.63 percent of the total population of the State. The
child population (0-6years) in Slum population is 22,229 out of which 11,378 are males
and 10,851 are females. The corresponding child population (0-6 years) in all India level
is 8,082,743 of which male & females are 4,204,451 and 3,878,292 respectively The Slum
population to the urban population of the State is 4.5 percent. The all-India figure for Slum
population as per Census, 2011 is 65,494,604 of which 33,968,203 are males and
31,526,401 are females.
LITERACY RATE OF SLUM POPULATION:
     The Literacy rate for Slum population is 72 percent with 76 percent for male and 68
percent for female population, according to Census 2011. The corresponding figure for
literacy in all India level is 68 percent with 73 % and 62 % for male and female literacy
respectively.                         *****

CHAPTER – III
                                  STATE INCOME



S
       tate Domestic Product (SDP), commonly known as State Income, is one of the prime
       indicators to measure the state's economic development. In the context of the
       planned economic development of the state, the SDP and Per Capita Income (PCI)
       play a vital role in the formulation of various plans and policies by state
administrators, policymakers, and planners. The estimate of the State Domestic Product
reveals the extent and direction of changes in the state's economic development levels
over a period of time. Assam is one of the potential states registering high growth in terms
of GVA and GSDP.


Economic performance is measured by the pace at which economic activity is growing in
a country or state. Assam by that measure, is one of the high-performing states in the
country. Higher economic growth helps in making the lives of the people better. Assam is
consistently performing better.


        “State Domestic Product” is defined as the aggregate of the economic value of all
final goods and services produced within the geographical boundaries of a state, counted
without duplication during a specified period, usually a year.

F.N. -
1. Advanced Estimates (AE) are estimates that depict how the economy/sector is expected to grow in the
upcoming/ongoing financial year based on earlier performance of various sectors/indicators.
2. Quick Estimates (QE) are revised AE subject to availability of data.
3. Provisional Estimates (PE) are revised QE which become Actual Estimates subject to comparison with the
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Govt. of India and approval from the State Govt.

3.1 Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) of Assam at current prices
    Advance Estimates of GSDP are indicator-based and are compiled using the
benchmark–indicator method. Under this approach, the estimates of the previous financial
year (2024–25) are extrapolated using relevant indicators that reflect the performance of
various sectors of the State economy. Data sourced from different State Government
Departments, Central Ministries, and private agencies serve as key inputs for the
compilation of these estimates.

various plans and programmes for the overall economic development of the State.

3.8. Per Capita Income
    The Per Capita Income is derived by dividing the Net State Domestic Product by the
mid-year total population of the State. The Per Capita Income is one of the indicators to
measure the standard of living of residents of a State. These estimates not only serve as
an indicator to assess the status of the economy among the States in the country but also
throw light on the overall impact of various developmental programmes implemented by
the Government.
     As per the advance estimates, the Per Capita Income (PCI) of Assam at current prices
for the year 2025-26(AE) is estimated to be attained at Rs.1,85,429 against Rs.1,60,417
for the year 2024-25 (QE) registering an increase of 15.59 percent.
    As per the advance estimates, the Per Capita Income of the State at constant (2011-
12) prices for the year 2025-26 is estimated to be attained at Rs.93,351 as compared to
Rs. 85,503 for the FY 2024-25 (QE) showing a growth of 9.2 percent.

3.9 India in Global Economy
    As per the data released by International Monetary Fund (World Economic Outlook,
October 2025 by IMF), India is the fourth largest economy in terms of GDP at current
prices (purchasing power parity) estimated $17714.19 Billion Dollars comprising a share
of 8.5 % in the global economy. With an estimated GDP of more than $4.1 Trillion at
current price during 2025 and with a population of 1.44 billion, India is also among the
highest population-based economies of the world with a robust domestic consumption and
is expected to achieve the $ 5 trillion mark by the end of 2027, contributing more than
9% of the global economy.

CHAPTER-IV

                                   STATE FINANCE




T
     he Government of Assam enacted the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management
     (AFRBM) Act in May 2005, which came into force on the 1st of September’2005 to
     ensure fiscal stability, and sustainability, improve efficiency and transparency in the
management of public finances, enhance the availability of resources, remove the
impediments for effective conduct of fiscal policy and prudent debt management for
improving social and physical infrastructure and human development in the State.
    A Medium-Term Fiscal Policy (MTFP) 2020-2025 is also placed along with this
Statement, which takes into cognizance the key challenges on revenue flows in the GST
regime coupled with current economic scenario and expenditure management.
   With the implementation of GST in 2017, the principle of indirect taxation for many
goods and services and raising revenue shifted from origin-based to destination-based. As
a result, the ability to tax goods and services and raise revenue shifted from the origin or
producing states to the destination or consuming states. With this, changes in the GST
rates from the earlier tax rates added to the uncertainty for states to raise revenue. This
was addressed through a constitutional amendment and the GST (Compensation to States)
Act, 2017 that guarantees states compensation for five years for any loss of revenue
arising due to GST implementation. The compensation to states is to be given out of the
GST Compensation Fund, which consists of collections of a cess levied specifically to
generate funds for this purpose.
   The State Government mobilizes financial resources through direct and indirect taxes,
non-tax revenue, share of central taxes and grants-in-aid from the Central Government
to meet the expenditure on administration and developmental activities.




   36
                              Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



4. The State’s Revenue

   The revenue receipts consist of (i) Tax revenue, (ii) Non-tax revenue, (iii) Share of
Central taxes and (iv) Grants-in-aid from the Centre. Revenue receipts of the State are
shown in Table: 4.1.
   The state expects to earn revenue receipts of around Rs. 1,17,225.97 crore in FY 2025-
26(BE) against Rs. 96907.91 crore in FY 2023-24 (Pre Actual) with a growth of 20.97
percent. Rs. 43,184.28 crore is expected to be earned from the State’s resources and Rs.
74041.69 crore from the Centre in FY 2024-25 (BE).

   The State’s resources consist of Tax revenue and Non-tax revenue. The main
components of the state’s tax revenue are (i) Sales Tax, (ii) Agricultural Income Tax, (iii)
Taxes on Profession, etc., (iv) Land Revenue including cess on Green Tea Leaf, (v) Stamp
duty & Registration, (vi) State Excise Duties, (vii) Motor Vehicle Tax, (viii) Passengers &
Goods Tax which includes Entry Tax (ix) Electricity Duty and (x) Entertainment Tax and
GST.
    It is expected that the state will earn tax revenue of Rs. 34,823.04 crore in FY 2025-
26(BE) with a growth of 15.87 percent. The collection of Tax Revenue has shown
significant improvement of 15% from FY 2022-23 to FY 2023-24 due to various measures
taken by the Government to augment its own tax resources.
     The major component of non-tax revenue is royalty on petroleum crude. Other items
in this category are royalties on coal and gas, receipts from interest and dividends, and
forest produce. It also includes departmental receipts like fees, fines user charges etc. The
state expects to earn non-tax revenue of Rs. 8,361.24 crore in FY 2025-26(BE) with a high
growth rate of 56.24 percent. During the last three years, the collection of non-tax revenue
has increased tremendously due to the collective effort of the State Government. The
share of non-tax revenue to total revenue receipts was 17.32 percent in FY 2023-24 and
it fallen to 15.11 percent in FY 2024-25. It is likely to be achieved at 19.36% in 2025-26
(BE).
4.3 Transfer from the Centre
    The State’s share of Central taxes is received against the collection of Income Tax,
Corporate Tax, Wealth Tax, Union Excise Duty, Customs Duty and Service Tax collected
by the Union Government. After the implementation of GST, the two major components
viz. Central Goods & Services Tax (CGST) and Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST)
have been added to this Head. The share of Central Taxes was Rs. 35330.57 crore in the
FY 2023-24 and it is expected to increase to Rs. 444494.04 crore in FY 2024-25(BE) with
an annual increase of 10.53 percent. The amount of grants has faleen from Rs. 21250.08
crore in FY 2023-24 to Rs. 21250.08 in FY 2024-25 (Pre Actual) crore but is likely to grow
by 39.04% to Rs. 29547.65 Crore in 2025-26 (BE). The share of the Central fund to total
revenue receipts was 38.50 percent in FY 2023-24 and is expected to be at 39.91 percent
in FY 2025-26(BE).

4.4 Revenue Expenditure
   The main components of revenue expenditure of the State Government are - salary
and pension of employees, interest payment on public debt, maintenance of law and order,
out-go on account of Central and State Finance Commissions awards and other
expenditures on General, Social and Economic Services. Component-wise revenue
expenditure is shown in Table: 4.4.
    Total revenue expenditure was Rs.94,162.90 crore in FY 2023-24 and it is expected to
increase to Rs. 99907.96 crore in FY 2024-25(Pre Actual) with an annual average growth
of 6.10 percent. However, the major share of revenue expenditure of the State
Government has to be incurred for payment of the salary and pension of the employees.
During FY 2023-24, the total amount spent under salary head was Rs. 29,806.54 crore
which accounted for 34.60 percent of total revenue expenditure and Rs. 36196.08 for the
year 2023-24(RE) which remained at 31.65 percent of the total revenue expenditure. It is
expected to increase to 33.32 percent in 2024-25(BE) with new employment generated at
the Govt. sector. The share of the pension to total revenue expenditure was about 16.11
percent in FY 2023-24 and it is expected to remain at 18.78 percent in FY 2025-26 (BE).

CHAPTER-V


                                   AGRICULTURE

                                                                                                 4




T
     he Agriculture sector plays a very important role in the socio-economic development
     of Assam. It is the backbone of the state’s economy and holds a key position in the
     overall development of the state. The agriculture sector contributes a large share of
the state’s economy and provides a main source of occupation and livelihood support to
70 per cent rural population. At present Assam's agriculture sector contributes about 23.02
per cent of revenue to the Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP). The total number of
farmer’s families in Assam is 3020765 as per agriculture census 2021-22. The size of
operational holdings on average is 0.85 hectares and more than 85 per cent of farmers
are either small or marginal with average land holdings of just about 0.36 hectares.
Agriculture Census data 2021-22 reveals that the total land under cultivation was 29.77
lakhs hectares i.e. 37.95 per cent of the total geographical land area of the State. The
data thus reveal that the preponderance of small and fragmented land holdings along with
insecure tenancy are the major reasons for underdevelopment of the agriculture sector in
the state. The government of Assam recognised the problems associated with the state's
agriculture sector and made efforts to bring rapid changes to the sector and serve the
cause of farmers.
     Agriculture and allied sectors comprise four key subsectors: crops, livestock, fisheries,
and forestry. In 2025-26 (AE), crops account for 67.58 per cent of the total GSVA of
agriculture and allied sector, while the share of livestock and fisheries in agriculture and
allied GSVA stands at 11.17 per cent and 15.59 per cent, respectively. Forestry constituted
the remaining 5.67 per cent of agricultural GSVA
    Agriculture and allied sectors contributed 18.73% per cent to total GSDP at current
prices in 2025-26(AE). There is a need to accelerate the growth of the livestock and
fisheries sector to increase agricultural growth and farmer income.



                                                                                        53

AGRICULTURE CREDIT
   Recognizing the contribution of farmers, the state government has issued Identity
Cards to the farmers. These Identity Cards are being used to develop a database of the
farmers.


    In view of the necessity to ensure credit flow for investment and development of the
agriculture sector, the government of Assam has introduced “zero interest crop loans” by
giving 100 per cent interest subventions on agricultural loans taken by farmers of Assam
to the limit of Rs.1.00 lakh. It is anticipated that this endeavour will encourage the farmers
to avail agriculture loans towards building the rural economy.


Kisan Credit Cards (KCC)
    The State Directorate of Agriculture, during the period 2001-02 to 2024-25 has issued
5221826 lakhs Kisan Credit Cards (KCC) and sanctioned Rs. 14711.1 crores as credit. The
figures of KCC issued and sanctioned an amount of credit for the past five years are
presented in Table 5.4.

SUPPORT SCHEMES FOR AGRICULTURE DEVELOPMENT
   In addition to the provisioning of credit, to fulfil the dream of the Honourable Prime
Minister for ‘Harkhet Me Pani’, the state government has prepared District Irrigation Plan,
Annual Action Plan and State Irrigation Plan to develop irrigation facilities for the state
holistically. Towards the mission to develop the agriculture sector, the Government of
Assam have distributed 603 Nos. of Tractors, 2925 Nos. of Power tillers, 13 nos. of
Reapers, 402 nos of Rotovators, and 8650 nos of shallow Tube Welles (STW) in the year
2024-25 (Q.E).


A. CSS-Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM)
   The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Govt. of India launched this scheme
in the year 2014-15 to promote the use of agricultural machinery/equipment and increase
the average farm power availability to the small and marginal farmers.



PROVISION OF FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE (SUBSIDY)


        1) Financial assistance@95% (max Rs.9.50 lakh) for procurement of agricultural
           machinery to establish village Level Farm Machinery Bank (VLFMB) by selected
           farmers’ groups to custom hire the service of machinery to local farmers.
        2) For individual farmers, financial assistance of @50% to procure single
          agricultural machinery. Under this subsidy scheme, 730 nos. of VLFMB and 988
          nos. of single machinery were distributed during the financial year 2023-24 with

    The state government is also planning to build Majuli Island, the largest riverine island
in the world as a hub of organic products with the trade mark in the name of “O Majuli”.
The productivity of most of the crops in the state is very low compared to the average
productivity of the country. The reasons for low productivity are primarily due to erratic
rainfalls and various other impediments like floods, soil erosion and sand deposition in
agriculture fields, though Assam is endowed with very rich and diverse soil conditions
conducive to agriculture. Despite all the constraints, the state Agriculture Department has
been successful in giving an impetus to increase the production of food grains by
implementing various programmes. In recent times the state has seen an increase in
productivity of food grains and cropping intensity. The Department has taken steps to
formulate State and District specific plans considering the agro-climatic conditions, growth
potentials and specific requirements of the districts with due emphasis on use of quality




   58
                            Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



seeds of high-yielding crop varieties, adoption of multi-cropping, access to assured
irrigation, use of improved farm mechanization, use of bio-fertilizers and bio-pesticides,
adoption of organic farming practices, establishing market linkage and ultimately creation
of employment opportunities and enhancement of income of the people. The agriculture
sector in the hill districts of the State, namely East Karbi-Anglong, West Karbi-Anglong
and Dima Hasao is constrained because of inadequate transport and communication
facilities, infrastructure, extensive practice of traditional Jhum cultivation and non-
availability of markets etc. To improve the condition of agriculture in the hill districts, the
state government has emphasized the promotion of cash on horticultural crops,
particularly pineapple and citrus fruits and on ginger and turmeric. Emphasis is also given
to support settled agriculture in terrace lands, wherever it seems feasible in the hill areas.

WEATHER AND RAINFALL
   The climate of Assam is sub-tropical with warm humid summers and cool dry winters.
The state is situated in a high rainfall zone with an annual average rainfall of 2297.4 mm.
The state normally receives 2 per cent of the total rainfall in the winter season (January-
February), 25 per cent in the summer season (March-May), 65 per cent in the monsoon
season (June-September) and 7 per cent in post-monsoon season (October-December).
Assam is prone to floods and drought-like situations. The state though has the natural
potential to drive the agriculture sector, erratic and unpredictable weather conditions and
floods have been creating adverse impacts making the farmers vulnerable to the
situations.

PRODUCTION
   Total food grain production in the state is showing a rising trend since 2011-12. The
total food grains production was 6611 thousand tonnes in 2022-23 and 6209 thousand
tonnes in the year 2023-24. There is a marginal decline (-6%) in the current year 2023-
24 over the previous year 2022-23.
YIELD
   The Yield rate of rice shows oscillations during the years 2010-11 to 2023-24 for
autumn and summer rice. The yield rate of autumn rice is 1436 Kg/Hect, winter rice is
2341 kg/hect and summer rice is 3051 kg/hect. In the year 2024-25. The following table
presents the yield rate of principal agricultural crops for last eleven years.

HYBRID RICE
   The state Agriculture Department since 2009-10 has been putting special efforts into
promoting the cultivation of hybrid varieties of rice on an experimental basis considering
the high yield potential of such varieties over the conventional high-yielding varieties. The
area under kharif rice (Autumn+winter) decreases up to 90.440 thousand hectares in the
current year 2024-25 as against 138.089 thousand hectares in the previous year 2023-
24. The area under Rabi rice (summer rice) increased from 156.616 thousand hectares in
2023-24 year up to 172.741 Thousand hactares in the current year 2024-25. The
percentage of hybrid rice area to the total rice area is 12.84% in the year 2024-25. This

HORTICULTURE
   Assam produces a wide range of horticultural crops including fruits, vegetables,
flowers, spices, nuts, tubers, medicinal and aromatic plants. The climatic conditions and
diverse landscape of the state have helped to develop diverse ecological habitats such as
forests, grasslands, wetlands etc. Which harbour and sustain wide-ranging floral and
faunal species in the state. The state has tremendous scope to promote the horticulture
sector that can help ensure food and nutritional security, as well as enhance employment
opportunities via cultivation and post-harvest management and value addition of
horticulture products.



   Horticulture crops occupy about 15 per cent of the gross cropped area of the State
with an annual production of more than 67 lakh metric tonnes of various horticultural
products. The state has now emphasized the commercialization of the sector as a priority
basis.



   The emphasis of the state is now on raising the productivity of various commercial
potential crops through the use of better technology, management and provision of
planting materials to the farmers. Moreover, emphasis is also placed on pre and post-
harvest treatment, proper harvest techniques, setting up of collection centres with grading
facilities, transport facilities and marketing facilities.



   The Directorate of Horticulture and Food Processing of the Government of Assam has
taken up some positive steps towards the creation of self-employment opportunities in the
horticulture sector by helping 15,000 rural women to get themselves engaged by setting
up 350 small and 4 medium fruit processing units. Assam also exports Assam Lemon to
London, pineapple to Dubai, Ginger and Turmeric to Swaziland has been facilitated through
APEDA-accredited exporters.

INTEGRATED NUTRIENT MANAGEMENT (INM)
FERTILIZER AND MANURE

    Fertilizer plays a dominant role in augmenting the productivity of crops. The State
Government has put thrust on promoting “Integrated Nutrient Management” (INM) and
also organic farming to reduce farmers’ dependence on chemical inputs and encourage
optimal use of farmers’ on-farm resources, economize production costs through adoption
of optimum doses of fertilizer and care for the health of the soil and the ecology. The uses
of bio-fertilizers, compost green manures and organic farming practices have gradually
increased. In addition to the promotion of organic manure, the government of Assam
however, has accorded due importance to the timely availability of fertilizers at the
doorstep of farmers during peak season of cultivation. Public institutions such as AIDC,
NAFED, GPSS, and other organizations - IFFCO, BVFCL, Green Chemicals Ltd, and Testa
Agro Industries Limited have been playing a pivotal role in the distribution of fertilizer
throughout the state. At present, there are 416 wholesale points and 6855 fertilizer sale
points in Assam.


                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 69
                                Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




CONSUMPTION OF FERTILISER
    The consumption of fertilizer in Assam is low. Farmers are reluctant to invest in
fertilizer because of the fear of loss caused by heavy rainfall and floods. Consumption of
fertilizer during summer and Rabi seasons is low because of the non-availability of water.
The consumption of fertilizer in the state is 58.99 Kg. /hectare in 2023-24 and covering
Gross Cropped Area 41,21,576(p) hectares in 2023-24. Table 5.14 presents the details of

SOIL HEALTH MANAGEMENT
    The state Agriculture Department has taken up initiatives to restore the depletion of
soil nutrients and sustain the crop production system. The state has promoted the use of
bio-fertilizers, micronutrients, lime, organic manures like green manures and
vermicompost and FYM to increase crop productivity and maintain soil health. Of late, the
use of bio-fertilizers has assumed significance due to motivational demonstration
programmes of the agriculture department. Special thrust has been given to the use of
Bio-fertilizer by initiating the Programme ‘Input support to the agriculturist having KCC’
under the state priority scheme, which has been implemented since 2006-07. Table 5.16

INTEGRATED PEST MANAGEMENT (IPM)

    For sustainable agricultural production, a key component is Integrated Pest
Management (IPM). The humid sub-tropical climate and diverse eco-system of the state
favour intensification of insect and pest attacks causing yield loss up to 30 percent.
Excessive and injudicious use of chemical pesticides however results in many residual
problems and negative externalities. To mitigate the externalities and sustain the yield of
agriculture fields, the department now has started to facilitate the availability of the Bio-
Control Agent (BCA) for the Bio-pesticide Intensive BPMI module, the thrust has been
given to increase production of already established BCA and the newly introduced BCA in
the State Bio-Control Laboratory (SBCL).



    The Agriculture Department of the state is trying to popularize the use of bio-pesticides
and other methods of IPM by organizing training and demonstrations. The initiatives have
shown results, rising trend of consumption of bio-pesticide in the state over the years. The
trend of consumption of chemical and bio-pesticides during the last four years is presented
in Table 5.17.

DEVELOPMENT OF THE SEED SECTOR
    The most vital component for increasing the production and productivity of crops is the
quality of the seeds used. Certified seed production is a process through which seeds are
produced in conformity with the standard variety by taking specific measures. In Assam,
production of certified seed has been taken up in the Field Trial Stations (FTSs), of some
of the government seed farms and Assam Seed Corporation’s seed farms. Despite the
efforts made, there is a dearth of quality seeds in the state and the seed replacement rate
(SRR) is at a low level. The State has to depend on outside sources for quality seeds for
some crops every year to meet the demand immediately after the occurrence of natural
calamities. To meet the growing demand and increase quality seed production, the
Agricultural Department has taken the following measures:


        Expansion of Seed Village Programme;
        Production of certified seeds of Paddy, Pulse and Oilseeds in Seed Village on large
         scale
        To focus on capacity building of Registered Seed Growers;
        Strengthen Seed Farms to facilitate the production, processing & storage of seeds.

SEED CERTIFICATION

    Assam State Seed Certification Agency (ASSCA) is the Nodal Agency, which has been
entrusted with the responsibility of seed certification of namely paddy, mustard and seeds
of pulses as per feasibility in the state. For planting crops namely coconuts, litchi, guava
etc. are under consideration for certification. Under ASSCA there are three notified seed
testing laboratories located at Guwahati, Jorhat and Silchar. The total annual testing
capacity of these three notified laboratories is about 20,000 samples. Seed testing and
certification guidelines are to be strictly followed for proper quality control and certification
as per the set norms.
SYSTEM OF RICE INTENSIFICATION (SRI)

   Adoption of the System of Rice Intensification with the use of hybrid seeds has shown
significant result in annual growth of production of rice in the State. As compared to normal
practices, the adoption of the SRI system enhances productivity with minimum use of
seeds, fertilizers and water, thus reducing the cost of production. The SRI also helps to
shorten the crop duration, which may be significant to go for another round of cropping
during the year.




                                                                                                          73
                              Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




CROP DEVELOPMENT

    To motivate the farmers to adopt the practice of double/multiple cropping the
government of Assam is taking up initiatives to facilitate the cultivation of summer paddy,
rabi pulses and oil seeds. The mission double cropping envisages additional coverage of
1.00 Lakh hectares presently under mono-cropping and allocates Rs. 6,200.00 Lakh. The
plan is further to add 3.0 lakh hectares to increase the cropping intensity of the state to
160.0 per cent.


FARM MECHANIZATION AND IRRIGATION

   Several factors, particularly, fragmented and small land holdings, farmers’ poor
economic conditions and non-availability of situation-specific prototypes of farm
implements stand as a serious hindrance to the mechanization of agriculture in the state.
However, has undertaken serious efforts to boost farm mechanization. The State
Agriculture Department has taken up initiatives to procure farm equipment like tractors,
power tillers and other farm machinery under externally aided, centrally sponsored and
state-plan schemes for the benefit of farmers, particularly the small and marginal farmers.
Estimates show farm power available per hectare of land in the state is 1.10 HP in the
year 2023-24 and 1.04 HP (Q.E) in the year 2024-25.

CROP INSURANCE
    In Assam about 4.75 lakh hectares of land is chronically flood prone and about 0.94
lakh hectares
       ((Q     of land is drought prone. To mitigate the distress of the farmers caused by
crop loss/crop damage Crop Insurance is a vital policy adopted by the government. In
addition to the floods and draught the farmers of the state also faced attacks of pests in
the agriculture fields. The Government of India launched a Crop Insurance programme
under the nomenclature “National Agricultural Insurance Scheme” (NAIS). All farmers who
avail loans from financial institutions are covered under the scheme and it is optional for

                                                                                                                          75
                             Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




non-loaned farmers. Under this scheme, 50 per cent of the premium amount is contributed
as a subsidy to small and marginal farmers which is shared equally by the Government of
India and State Government. This scheme is expected to be an important instrument for
development in the field of crop production by providing financial support to the farmers
in the event of crop failure and help in maintaining the flow of agricultural credit. This
programme covers 8 (eight) crops - 3 crops in Kharif Season, 4 crops in Rabi season and
one crop in summer season. The crops are-



 Kharif Season                            Autumn/Ahu Paddy, winter/Sali Paddy and
                                          Jute
 Rabi Season                              Rape & Mustard, Wheat, Potato, Sugarcane

 Summer Season                            Boro Paddy.



    This scheme, under the area approach, not only facilitates insurance coverage to each
of the notified crop damage within the defined area for widespread calamities but also on
an individual basis for localized calamities such as hailstorms, landslides, cyclones and
floods. National Agriculture Insurance Scheme though is being implemented in the state
since 2009-10, has not been able to provide the desired solution to the risk involved in
the agriculture sector due to reasons like lack of awareness, low subsidy premiums (10
per cent) for small and marginal farmers, delayed claim settlement, slow response of
banks in issuance of Kissan Credit Cards have emerged as the main impediments in the
successful implementation of the scheme.


MODIFIED NATIONAL AGRICULTURAL INSURANCE SCHEME (MNAIS)
   The scheme is being implemented on a pilot basis in 50 districts in the country. NAIS
is withdrawn from those districts in which MNAIS will be implemented.
       The unit of insurance for major crops is Village/Village Panchayat.
       The scheme is compulsory for loanee farmers and voluntary for non-loanee
        farmers. Uniform seasonality norms will be applicable for both loanee & non-loanee
        farmers.
       Sum insured can be opted up to 150% of the value of average yield. Premium
        subsidy is available up to the value of threshold yield/loan amount only.
       The entire claim will be borne by the implementing agency. The scheme provides
        account payments up to 25% of the likely claim for immediate relief to the farmers.
       Minimum indemnity level will be 70% against 60% in case of NAIS.
       Calculation of threshold yield: Average yield of last 7 years excluding up to 2
        years of declared natural calamity.
       The scheme is implemented in two districts of Assam viz., Kamrup and Dhubri
        from the Rabi season of 2010-11.




   76
                            Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



WEATHER-BASED CROP INSURANCE SCHEME (WBCIS)
    With the objective to overcome the shortcomings of delayed settlement of claims under
NAIS, a Pilot Weather Crop Insurance Scheme (WBCIS) was introduced for implementation
in 20 States on a pilot basis. WBCIS has been implemented in Assam since the Rabi season
of 2013-14.
    WBCIS is intended to provide insurance protection to farmers against adverse weather
incidents. Such as deficit and excess rainfall, high or low temperature, humidity etc. which
are deemed to impact adversely crop production


PROCUREMENT OF PADDY AS A MEASURE OF PRICE SUPPORT
At present Assam has a surplus in Rice production. The improvement in production and
productivity is the result of better input management practices and the adoption of
improved technology. Despite the progress made, the un-remunerative price received by
the farmers for not having institutionalised markets is acting as a disincentive to drive the
initiatives of the farmers. To ensure the interest of the farmers the state government has
engaged the Assam State Agricultural Marketing Board (ASAMB) for procurement of paddy
at Minimum Support Price, in addition to procurement to be done by the Food Corporation
of India.


AGRICULTURE MARKETING AND STORAGE
    Marketing of agricultural produce in the state is a serious problem for the farming
community. Lack of organized marketing facility, lack of storage infrastructure near the
field, poverty and need for money after harvest for repayment of agricultural debt and
other contingencies force the farmers to dispose of their hard-earned produce at the
earliest and throwaway prices. Keeping in view, the interest of farmers, the government
of Assam in addition to engaging the Assam State Agriculture Marketing Board and FCI for
procurement of products have developed storage capacity shown in the following Table

    At present, the state has 24 Regulated Market Committees, 20 Primary Market Yards,

Wholesale Markets, One Organic Market, 18 Packaging Room, 42 Drying Platform and 15
Processing units. The Regulated Markets have been covered under AGMARKNET. As
regards cold storage infrastructure in the state, there are 26 cold storages of which 23 are
in the private sector and 3 in the state sector.
   To assist the farmers in carrying vegetables to distant markets, the Assam State
Agriculture Marketing Board provides transport subsidies to farmers. Government of
Assam has taken steps to construct a three-storied market at Pamohi (Guwahati), a
growers-consumers market complex at Ulubari (Guwahati), and establish 11 sale counters
for marketing of farm products have been undertaking by the Government. The
Department has also taken initiative for the establishment of market infrastructure, and
storage facility and to eradicate the transportation bottlenecks. The rural connectivity
scheme implemented under PMGSY is a major step towards the benefit of farmers to take
out their agricultural products to the nearest markets.


SOME OF THE MAJOR STEPS TAKEN TO BOOST MARKETING SUPPORT AND POST
HARVEST MANAGEMENT:

       The farming community has been mobilized to form 25 numbers of Farmer Producer
        Organizations (FPO) to secure better produce prices;
       Rural farm women have been empowered by training and providing mini processing
        units of pulses and oil seeds from which they can earn from their homes;
       Tie-up has been made for the export of Red Bao Paddy to the USA and the process
        started in 2012-13 regularly;
       Export of Pineapple cubes, orange, ginger, dendrobium orchids to other states and
        countries have already been started;
       Some Self Help Groups are assisted in taking up Agri-Horti activities including post-
        harvest management.

NATIONAL MISSION ON OILSEEDS & OIL PALM
   The State is highly deficient in oil seed production. To achieve targeted area the
Agriculture Department has been launching Mini-Mission-I-Development of cultivation of
vegetable oilseeds crop, Mini-Mission-II-Development of cultivation of oil palm and Mini-
Mission-III-Development of cultivation of tree borne oil seeds. The state has set a target
of 3.75 lakh hectares under oil palm cultivation, while Patanjali Food Limited (PFL) has set
a target of 60,000 hectares of plantation by 2026 in Assam.

BRING GREEN REVOLUTION TO EASTERN INDIA INCLUDING ASSAM
    The Central and the State Governments have chalked out a strategy to achieve the
planned growth in the agriculture sector of the country Several interventions such as
Bringing Green Revolution to Eastern India (BGREI), double cropping, supply of improved
seeds, fertilizer and technology equipment now have been undertaken. Under the initiative
on BGREI, the government of India considers the states namely Assam, Bihar,
Chhatisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Eastern Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal as potential areas
for increasing food grain production and productivity. The states are however mired by
low credit availability, poor extension facilities and infrastructure bottlenecks. To remove
the impediments on a priority basis steps have been taken emphasising better seed
replacement ratio, adequate and timely availability of critical inputs, improving
infrastructure facilities and other required interventions including bank credit. In Assam,
the scheme was launched in 2010-11 as a sub-scheme of RKVY to overcome the


                                                                                       79
                                           Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




constraints limiting the productivity of rice-based cropping system in the state by adopting
short-term activities related to the transfer of technology through Rice demonstration in
farmers’ fields along with activities about the creation of irrigation facilities to maximize
agricultural production sustainably.

PRADHAN MANTRI FASAL BIMA YOJANA: THE HIGHLIGHTS
    The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana was introduced in February 2016 to provide
insurance services to farmers for their yield. It was formulated in line with the one nation–
one scheme theme by replacing the earlier two schemes National Agricultural Insurance
Scheme (NAIS) and Modified National Agricultural Insurance Scheme (MNAIS) by
incorporating their best features and removing their inherent drawbacks.

STATUS OF PMFBY IN ASSAM
    The Assam Government rolled out the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana from the Rabi
season of 2016-17 intending to benefit about 5.5 lakh farmers but later in 2021-22, it
benefited 627869 farmers. In the year 2023, the scheme covered the Kharif area of
263590 hectares and 397088 farmers. For effective rolling out of the scheme, the state
plans to impart training to the officials of the agriculture department and organise
publicity-cum-awareness programmes among the farmers. Table- 5.24 shows the status

SCHEME FOR MARKETING OF FRUITS AND VEGETABLES
TRANSPORT SUBSIDY SCHEME 2018-19:
    Affordable transport facilities are one of the prime requisites to enable farmers to place
their produce at remunerative markets. The provisioning of transport facilities also helps
to reduce the number of intermediaries involved in the market chain and thus ensure fair
returns to the farmers and procurement at reasonable prices for the consumers. The state
has formed the Agricultural Production Management Group (APMG) for better crop
planning and marketing.


The scheme proposes to provide subsidy @ Rs.2.0/Quintal per km to each selected
APMG/growers Group etc. for a maximum of 2 tons per group per trip for a maximum
distance of 100 Km.
    The scheme had placed a supplementary demand of Rs. 250 lakh under the budget
head of other agriculture programmes (2435) on subsidy for transportation support for
marketing of fruits and vegetables for the year 2017-18. The physical target for
transportation was approximately 20,500 MT.


OBJECTIVE OF THE SCHEME
        The objective of the scheme is to facilitate the marketing of surplus agricultural
         products particularly perishable fruits and vegetables from areas where surplus
         production takes place. The goal is to ensure a remunerative price for the farmers.
        It is also expected that the approach will encourage the growers to take up
         production on a commercial point.
        To facilitate the urban population to get products at reasonable prices.
        To check the fall of market price in the surplus growing areas beyond the cost of
         production. Subsidised transport facilities are thus required to be provided to the
         growers to safeguard the growers from financial losses in the harvest season.

PROCEDURE FOR SALE
    1.    The sale price is to be fixed by the District Agricultural Officer in consultation with
          farmers and on the basis of the prevailing market rate. The price list is to be
          displayed every day at the sale points.
    2.     In case the farmers of the APMGs are not getting remunerative prices the
          Agricultural Development Officer (ADO) will inform the District Agricultural Officer
          (DAO). In such cases, the DAO is to take measures to facilitate the sale of the
          products at identified points.



SCHEME FOR DEVELOPMENT OF JUTE GRADING AND BALING -

AIM AND OBJECTIVE

    The aim and objective of the Jute grading and baling scheme is to extend facilities and
modern know-how of the grading jute to the growers of the state. It is expected that
grading of jute would help the growers to involve themselves in the marketing of jute to
get remuneration prices of graded jute.

                                                                                           81
                             Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




    During 2018-19 under the scheme, it was proposed to impart training to 90
unemployed educated youth selected from the families of jute growers in three batches in
the jute grading training centre located at Howly of Barpeta District. The training centre
was established in 2000, but the infrastructure of the centre was damaged in 2001 due to
natural calamities. Since then the centre has not been operational and the staff associated
with the centre were attached to the district agriculture office, Barpeta. Now a financial
proposal of Rs. 350 lakh has been made to revive the training centre. The duration of the
training is planned for one month with the provision of a stipend of Rs.1000/-for each of
the trainees. In addition, there is provision for food and accommodation.

MARKET INTELLIGENCE SCHEME (PLAN): OBJECTIVES
    The scheme of market intelligence has been in operation in Assam since November
1957. The scheme originally covered seven markets, now it covers 72 important markets
and representative markets and 40 commodities to collect requisite information for
formulation of economic policies. The scheme is importance for formulating price policy by
the state and it provides necessary support to address problems of marketing. The
activities under the market intelligence scheme are to collect and dissemination of daily
and weekly wholesale and retail prices of market arrival of important agricultural
commodities and livestock products from the selected markets and furnish the market
information to the Economic and Statistical adviser of the government of India, state
government, public and private institutions and Army Head Quarter through various
reports, bulletin and review. The All India Radio, Guwahati broadcasts the daily price
bulletin of wholesale prices of selected agricultural commodities of important markets of
Assam in the evening programme of “KRISHI JAGAT” for the best interest of growers,
consumers and traders. This scheme has an annual operational budget of 150 lakh.
SCHEME FOR QUALITY CONTROL AND AGMARK GRADING (PLAN)
    This scheme was introduced in the state during the year 1966-67. Agmark is a symbol
of purity guaranteed by the Government. It is voluntary for the packers and millers. Under
the scheme, Agmark laboratories have been established in Guwahati, Tezpur, Nagaon,
Jorhat, Dibrugarh and Silchar. The principal objective of the scheme is to promote the
grading of commodities like mustard oil, spices, honey ghee, wheat etc. under Agmark
grading. To encourage the packers and millers to produce quality products. At present,
there are six District Agmark Laboratories established in different parts of Assam.

 CHAPTER-VI:                    IRRIGATION




T   he economy of Assam is basically agrarian in nature, and so easy access to agro-
    inputs, such as irrigation facilities is considered an important part of rural
    infrastructure and sustainability in the agricultural sector.
    Although Assam is blessed with abundant natural water resources, irrigation is
indispensable because of adverse and unpredictable weather conditions like flood, erosion
and drought. Irrigation could also help leverage multiple cropping and modernization of
agricultural practices in the state
    Therefore, the Irrigation Department plays a vital role in socio-economic development
by harnessing the rich surface and ground water resources of the state. The mandate of
the Department is to supply water to cropland according to the demand of the cultivators.
   There are three types of Irrigation schemes being implemented by the Irrigation
Department, Assam. These are - Major Irrigation Scheme (Culturable Command Area more
than 10,000 hectare), Medium Irrigation Scheme (Culturable Command Area between
2000 and 10,000 hectare) and Minor Irrigation Scheme (Culturable Command Area upto
2000 hectare). These Schemes may be of three categories. These are –
   Surface Flow Irrigation Scheme: It uses surface gravity flow to convey water through
canals to croplands by constructing diversion weirs. This type of Schemes consists of
Major, Medium and Minor Irrigation Schemes.
   Surface Lift Irrigation Scheme: Surface water is lifted by pumps from rivers, lakes,
ponds etc and channelized to croplands through canals. This type of Schemes consists of
Major, Medium and Minor Irrigation Schemes.
Ground Water Lift Irrigation Schemes: Ground water is lifted by installing Deep Tube
wells/Medium Deep Tube wells/Shallow Tube wells and the water channelized to crop fields
through canals or underground pipe networks.
Other than the Irrigation Department, Agriculture Department, Panchayat& Rural
Development Department and Soil Conservation department also carries out irrigation


                                                                                   83
                              Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




activities in the state. The Irrigation Department has created an irrigation potential of 8.84
Lakh Hectare up to 31/03/2025 and the Ultimate Irrigation Potential (UIP) of Irrigation
schemes under the Irrigation Department as on 31/03/2025 is 12.6 Lakhs Hectare.
