Project Elephant:
        There are 32 notified Elephant Reserves in the country, spread over 15 states.
According to the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, there are five
Project Elephant sites in the state: Sonitpur, Dihing Patkai, Kaziranga, Dhanshiri-Lamding,
and Chirang Ripu.
        Project Elephant was launched in 1992 by the Government of India to provide
financial and technical support for wildlife management efforts by states, aimed at
protecting the free-ranging population of wild Asian elephants. The project's primary goal




  156
                               Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



is to ensure the long-term survival of a viable and conservation-resilient population of
elephants in their natural habitats and migration corridors.
         Other objectives of Project Elephant include supporting research on the ecology
and    management        of   elephants,   creating   conservation   awareness    among    local
communities, and providing improved veterinary care for captive elephants. Despite the
government’s initiatives, significant efforts are still needed to save and support elephants
in the state.

Assam Project on Forest and Biodiversity Conservation Society (APFBCS):
         Assam Project on Forest and Biodiversity Conservation Society (APFBCS) was
constituted by Government of Assam and registered under the Societies Registration Act
1860. The Society has the mandate for planning and implementation, monitoring,
coordination and management of all the activities proposed in conservation contexts under
the project. The activities of the project put special emphasis on creating sustainable


                                                                                          157
                               Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




livelihood opportunities for forest dependent communities with a view to promote
sustainable forest management and restore forest ecosystems. The society came into
existence on 28th June 2012. To achieve the goals, APFBC adopts participatory micro
planning by forming Joint Forest Management Committee (JFMC) and Eco Development
Committee (EDC) among the forest dependent communities. At present there are 185 EDC
in different protected areas in the state and doing their works for conservation of forest.

Man-Animal conflict Scenario of the State:
       Though the Assam Forest Department has taken many steps for the overall
development of the forest sector, the man-animal conflict in the present state scenario
cannot be ignored. This has emerged as one of the most challenging problems for wildlife
management and conservation in recent times. Human-elephant conflict has reached
alarming proportions in recent years, followed by human-leopard and human-monkey
conflicts. The human-elephant conflict creates considerable economic hardship for farmers
by way of crop and property damage. Due to elephant disturbance in the present state
scenario, most cultivators in the forest-side area have left their valuable crop fields to
grow paddy or other crops. Moreover, due to monkey disturbance, cultivators have
stopped growing vegetables for household and commercial use, and so on. So, there is an
urgent need to estimate crop losses due to animal disturbance. Besides this, human deaths
due to encounters with elephants are also a serious concern, and vice versa. The principal
reasons for such conflicts are the fragmentation of elephant corridors, habitat loss, and
food crises in forest areas, among others. Given this increasing man-elephant conflict, an
immediate, reasonable, and acceptable solution is urgently required.


OTHER NEW INITIATIVES IN CONSERVATION CONTEXT:
       The protection of forests is a key motto of the current government. The government
is highly concerned about encroachment on forest land, especially in Reserved forests and
Protected areas. To safeguard these areas, the government has taken strong measures to
recover lost forest land and maintain the state's ecological balance. In this effort, some
areas have already been reclaimed from encroachers and conserved. Restoring open forest
regions, increasing the capacity of the Forest Department, and providing livelihood options
for forest-dependent communities all require significant funding and various forms of
support.

Chapter-XI

                      INDUSTRY, TRADE AND MINING

                                                                                            4




   I
        ndustrialisation in Assam traces its roots to the British period, marked by the
        establishment of tea estates, coal mines, plywood factories and pioneering oil
        exploration in this mineral-rich region. Assam proudly hosts Asia’s first and the
world’s second oil refinery — the Digboi Refinery, commissioned on 11 December 1901
— which remains India’s oldest functioning refinery and one of the longest continuously
operating refineries globally. The State is richly endowed with strategic mineral and
hydrocarbon resources including crude oil, natural gas, coal, limestone and granite. For
decades, Assam’s tea industry has been a cornerstone of its economy, accounting for
over 50% of India’s total tea production and serving as a key export commodity.
   Assam’s strategic location in the Northeast, with direct connectivity to East and
Southeast Asian markets, supported by robust banking and financial institutions, reliable
power supply, expanding communications and an evolving transportation network,
significantly enhances its appeal as a destination for manufacturing and trade. This
advantage is further strengthened by the Government of India’s “Look East” policy.




  162
                           Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



   The State’s industrial base, though modest, is expanding across diverse sectors
including petrochemicals, fertilisers, textiles, cement, plastics, agro-based and mineral-
based industries, traditional handlooms and handicrafts, ornamental fisheries and
tourism — collectively generating substantial employment. Among these, oil, natural gas
and tea remain the principal contributors to Assam’s industrial revenue.


CONTRIBUTION OF INDUSTRIAL SECTOR TO STATE ECONOMY
   In the State Income Estimation framework, the industry sector encompasses the sub-
sectors of mining & quarrying, manufacturing, electricity, gas, water supply & other utility
services, and construction. According to the advance estimates for 2025-26 at current
(2011-12) prices, the industry sector is projected to grow at an annual rate of 14.27%,
compared to 11.49% at constant prices. At constant prices, the annual growth rates of
the industry sub-sectors for 2025-26 are estimated at 5.52% for mining & quarrying,
6.97% for manufacturing, 11.96% for electricity, gas, water supply & other utility services,
and 22.98% for construction. These figures are to be compared with the corresponding
growth rates at current prices of 6.49%, 10.76%, 19.32% and 27.42%, respectively. For
the year 2025-26, the industry sector’s contribution to the State’s GDP is estimated at
approximately 32.53% at current prices, against 42.40% at constant (2011-12) prices.

INDEX OF INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTION [IIP] (Base: 2011-12=100)
   The Index of Industrial Production (IIP) quantifies the rate of growth across key
industrial sectors of the economy over a defined period. It encompasses three primary
sectors—Mining, Manufacturing, and Electricity—which collectively represent the industrial
production landscape. The IIP is compiled on a month-to-month basis and aggregated into
annualised figures to assess performance trends. Like all segments of the economy, these

                                                                                      163

sectors experienced significant disruption due to the prevailing pandemic, which also
impeded the timely collection and reporting of data at both the state and Union
Government level. A diagrammatic representation of IIP from 2016-17 to 2024-25 is
presented below:

future demand within the State.

ANNUAL SURVEY OF INDUSTRIES (ASI)
   The Annual Survey of Industries (ASI) is the principal source of industrial statistics
for the registered organised manufacturing sector, generating estimates on key
aggregates such as input, output, capital, employment, value added and related
parameters. It encompasses all factories registered under Sections 2m(i) and 2m(ii) of the
Factories Act, 1948, which define operational thresholds for inclusion in the survey
frame.In the ASI 2023-24 results, Assam ranked 14th in terms of the number of operating
factories and 18th with regard to the workforce engaged in the organised manufacturing
sector.

2. Industrial and Investment Policy (Amendment) Assam 2023

   The Industrial and Investment Policy of Assam (Amendment), 2023, notified by the
Government of Assam, amends the Industrial and Investment Policy of Assam, 2019 with
the objective of attracting large-scale investments and promoting employment-led
industrial growth in the State.

    The amendment primarily revises Clause 14 of the Policy to introduce a framework for
customised incentive packages for Mega Projects. Under the amended provisions, a Mega
Project is defined as an industrial unit having a minimum fixed capital investment of ₹100
crore and generating at least 200 permanent jobs.

Committee and Approval Process

    Proposals seeking customised incentives are examined by an Empowered Committee
constituted by the Government. The Committee is chaired by the Hon’ble Minister,
Industries & Commerce and comprises seniormost secretary from key departments such
as Finance, Industries & Commerce, Revenue, Power and other concerned departments.

    The Empowered Committee evaluates the project proposal based on parameters such
as investment size, employment generation, socio-economic impact, regional development
and overall benefit to the State and recommends a suitable incentive package. The final
approval of the customised incentive package is accorded by the State
Government/Cabinet, based on the Committee’s recommendations.

   The amendment thus provides flexibility to the Government to support strategically
important projects through project-specific incentives, strengthening Assam’s
competitiveness as an investment destination.

   Till date, the Hon’ble Cabinet has approved 56 proposals involving a total investment
of Rs 26,848.41 crore, expected to generate 45,020 employment opportunities. Of these,
industries like Varun Beverages Ltd., Dalmia Cements NE Ltd. (Phase I), Star Cements NE
Ltd., SBL Biscuits Pvt. Ltd., Gulshan Polyols, Aadhar Green Industries LLP, Kamakhya Bio-
fuels Industries Ltd., Seas Biotech Pvt. Ltd., etc has already started commercial production
until 2024-25.

3. The Assam Ethanol Production Promotion Policy, 2021 (as amended in 2022)
    To strengthen the ethanol production in Assam and further to facilitate the upcoming
    ethanol units in the State, the Assam Ethanol Production Promotion Policy, 2021 was
    introduced and later amended in 2022.


Objectives:
1. This policy aims to achieve the following objectives for the overall growth and
   development of green-field new 100% ethanol manufacturing industrial units in the
   State with a goal of providing remunerative returns to investors, farmers and all other
   stakeholders:
2. To allow production of Ethanol from all feedstocks permitted under National Policy on
   Biofuels, 2018 and by the National Biofuel Coordination Committee.
3. To offer fiscal benefits and provide an enabling environment in Assam for the promotion
   of, and investment in, fuel-grade standalone new or green-field ethanol manufacturing
   units by facilitating and financially incentivizing potential investor.
4. To increase incomes of farmers producing feed-stock/ raw material which may be used
   for Ethanol manufacturing.
5. To create local employment opportunities, and foster sustainable industrial growth
   through promotion of new Ethanol industries.


Eligibility for type of Units:
   Only green-field standalone distilleries (single feed or dual feed) producing and
supplying Ethanol to Oil Manufacturing Companies (OMCs) under Ethanol Blending
Programme (EBP) of Government of India, shall be eligible for incentive under this Policy.
   In case of production capacity proposed by the proponent exceeds production output
approved by OMCs in procurement agreement under EBP, such ethanol manufacturing
units shall be allowed to sell ethanol to buyers other than OMCs, provided the entity does
not violate any clauses of the procurement contract under Ethanol Blending Programme.


Incentives to Ethanol Manufacturing Units:
   The Policy recognizes the need for providing additional incentives to eligible units in
the ethanol manufacturing sector in order to engender further improvement in the
investment prospects of that sunrise sector in the State.


Incentives under this Policy:
   Available provisions of incentives and their quantum under the the Assam Ethanol
Production Promotion Policy (Amendment), 2022 are as below:

4. Assam Electronics (Semiconductor etc.) Policy, 2023.
    The Assam Electronics (Semiconductor etc.) Policy, 2023 aims to position Assam as a
frontrunner in the realm of semiconductor manufacturing and electronics production,
fostering, innovation, economic growth and global competitiveness. This policy endeavours
to leverage Assam’s strategic location, robust infrastructure, and stable governance to
attract substantial investments in the semiconductor and electronics sectors. Key
objectives of this policy include job creation, reversing brain drain, strengthening the value
chain and positioning Assam on the global stage through strategic partnerships and trade.
Policy Period: The Assam Electronics (Semiconductor etc.) Policy, 2023 shall come into
force from the date of notification and shall remain in operation for a period of 5 years.
Eligibility:
       All new units falling under “Semiconductor Manufacturing” are entitled for benefits
        under this policy unless specifically stated otherwise in the provisions of the policy.
       Eligible industrial units shall be allowed to take up phase wise commissioning of the
        total approved plant capacity within the overall prescribed time limit of 3 years for
        MSMEs and 5 years for large industries from the date of first fixed capital investment
        and avail applicable incentives in a phased manner.

6. Assam Agribusiness & Rural Transformation Project (APART)
1. Background
      The Assam Agribusiness and Rural Transformation Project (APART) is a World Bank
financed project implemented from January 2018 with the objective of enhancing value
addition, competitiveness, and resilience of selected agricultural value chains, focusing on
small farmers and       agro-entrepreneurs.
Under APART, the Industries & Commerce Department, Government of Assam, through
the Office of the Commissioner of Industries & Commerce (OPIU-I&C), was entrusted with
the           implementation            of         key           interventions       under:


            Component A- Enabling Agri-Enterprise Development
            Component B- Facilitating Agro-Cluster Development
      These interventions directly addressed long-standing constraints in Assam's agro-
industrial sector such as fragmented value chains, limited private investment, absence of
shared infrastructure, and weak MSME institutional capacity.


2. Strategic Role of the Industries & Commerce Department
The Industries & Commerce Department played a pivotal and catalytic role in
transforming Assam’s agribusiness ecosystem by:
            Positioning Assam as an investment-ready agribusiness destination.
            Enabling large-scale private sector participation
            Organising MSMEs into functional Industry Associations
            Creating Common Facility Centres (CFCs) to bridge technology and
             infrastructure gaps
            Strengthening district-level institutional capacity through DI&CCS


The Department acted as the nodal interface between investors, entrepreneurs, district
administrations, and line departments, ensuring coordinated and outcome-oriented
implementation.

7. Mukhya Mantrir Tholuwa Udyog Bikash Asoni (MMTUBA)

    The basic objective of Mukhya Mantrir Thaluwa Udyog Bikash Asoni is to provide
assistance to the Handicraft Industries & Clusters which are registered with Co-operative
Deptt, Govt. of Assam. It aims to promote the livelihood of artisans and boost their
activities with new technology and design.
The activities identified for promotion are Bell Metal Craft, Brass Metal Craft, Fire works
Craft, Jute diversified products, Cane & Bamboo, Sital Patti, Water Hyacinth Jewellery,
Pottery& Terracota, Wood Carving, Decorative textile, Black smithy, Gold & Silver Smithy,
Masks, Japi Craft etc.
       a) Incentives provide under the scheme :-
               Revolving Fund for Raw Material Bank: Interest-free loans will be provided
                to Artisan Co-operative Societies to establish and operate Raw Material
                Banks etc..
               Training: Partners with institutions like NID, IIT Guwahati, and the Indian
                Institute of Packaging to enhance artisan skills, design, and packaging.
               Supply of Tools & Equipment: Government will allocate funds for the
                procurement and distribution of tools and equipment, with a maximum
                ceiling of Rs. 20,000 per artisan.
               Marketing Assistance: Provides marketing assistance for                 paper
                advertisements in DIPRO-approved print and electronic media.
               Infrastructure Grant: Artisan Co-operative Societies will receive an
                Infrastructure Grant of Rs. 15.00 lakh for constructing working sheds within
                a maximum ceiling of Rs. 30,000 per artisan.
               Award Scheme: The scheme includes an awards program where selected
                handicraft artisans from different craft industries are recognized at a state-
                level ceremony.

8. Chief Minister's Atmanirbhar Asom Abhijan (CMAAA)

   1. About CMAAA and Its Objectives

The Chief Minister’s Atmanirbhar Asom Abhijan (CMAAA) is a flagship programme of the
Government of Assam, designed to mitigate unemployment and promote inclusive socio-
economic development across the State. Under this initiative, eligible applicants in the
General category are entitled to financial assistance of ₹2, 00,000, comprising a 50% grant
and a 50% interest-free loan. Applicants in the Professional category (including disciplines
such as Engineering, MBBS, BDS, etc.) are eligible for financial assistance of up to ₹5,
00,000 on the same grant-loan basis.
The principal objectives of the scheme are to:
             Facilitate self-employment opportunities for educated youth through
        appropriate mechanisms.
              Establish an entrepreneur-centric ecosystem within the State.
             Promote the creation of gainful employment in both rural and urban areas
        through the establishment and expansion of economic ventures.
              Provide requisite financial support to entrepreneurs and entrepreneurial
        groups for undertaking new or existing income-generating activities.
             Reinforce the Government’s strategic emphasis on strengthening the rural
        economy.
Following the successful execution of CMAAA 1.0, the Government of Assam has launched
the second phase of the programme, referred to as CMAAA 2.0.
2. Eligibility Criteria for Applicants
To qualify for participation in the CMAAA, applicants must satisfy the following eligibility
conditions:
              Must be a permanent resident of the State of Assam.
              Must be aged between 28 and 45 years as of 1 April 2024.
              Must satisfy the prescribed minimum educational qualifications: a pass in
        Class X for General category applicants; and up to Class X qualification for
        candidates belonging to SC, ST, or OBC categories.
             Must possess relevant skills, experience, and capability to undertake an
        income-generating activity.
               Must hold an operative scheduled commercial bank account opened prior to
        1 April 2024.
             Must have a clean credit record, with no history of default on loans from
        scheduled commercial banks.
       Only one eligible member per household (defined as husband, wife, brother, sister)
        may apply under the scheme.
              Must possess valid registration with the Employment Exchange.
In addition, applicants under CMAAA 2.0 must not have been beneficiaries under CMAAA
1.0.

3. Total Number of Beneficiaries
Under CMAAA 1.0, a total of 25,277 individuals benefited from the scheme, of whom
25,056 (99%) were from the General category and 221 (1%) were from the Professional
category. Of the total beneficiaries, 74% were male and 26% were female. The beneficiary
cohort comprised 55% existing entrepreneurs and 45% new entrepreneurs who
successfully initiated business ventures.
For CMAAA 2.0, a total of 1, 09,155 applications have been received, including 1, 08,873
from the General category and 282 from the Professional category. The selection process
is in progress, with interviews completed for all applicants in both categories.


4. Disbursement of Funds
Under the ongoing disbursement:
             Beneficiaries in the General category have received financial assistance of
       ₹1, 00,000 each.
             Beneficiaries in the Professional category have received grants up to ₹2,
       50,000, commensurate with the amount specified in their respective Detailed
       Project Reports (DPRs).
The evaluation process for disbursing the second tranche of the interest-free loan to
CMAAA 1.0 beneficiaries is underway. Upon completion of the evaluation, eligible
beneficiaries in the General category may receive an interest-free loan of ₹1, 00,000, while
Professional category beneficiaries may receive an interest-free loan of up to ₹5, 00,000.


5. Programme Impact
All beneficiaries under CMAAA 1.0 have successfully completed a mandatory three-day
Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP). A baseline survey indicates that 84%
of CMAAA 1.0 beneficiaries have effectively utilized the financial assistance provided.
Efforts have also been undertaken to integrate CMAAA 1.0 beneficiaries with other
government credit facilitation schemes, including PMEGP, PMFME, and Mudra.

A. Government of India:
   Following schemes/ policies of Govt. of India are implemented by the Industries,
Commerce & Public Enterprise Department. Schemes of Central Government being
implemented by Industries and Commerce Department:

9. Uttar Poorva Transformative Industrialization Scheme (UNNATI–2024)
    The Uttar Poorva Transformative Industrialization Scheme (UNNATI–2024) is an
industrial development initiative launched by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry,
Government of India, administered through the Department for Promotion of Industry and
Internal Trade (DPIIT). The scheme is aimed at strengthening the industrial ecosystem in
the North Eastern Region (NER) and catalysing new investment by incentivising industrial
expansion and operational optimisation. UNNATI seeks to foster a performance-driven,
innovation-oriented economy, with particular emphasis on sectors aligned to the region’s
comparative advantages.
    The policy prioritises strategic growth sectors including Manufacturing, Tourism, Hotels
& Hospitality, Healthcare, Bio-Technology, IT & ITeS and other allied segments, with
dedicated support for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs). UNNATI provides a
comprehensive incentive framework comprising capital investment support, tax
exemptions, interest subventions, streamlined clearances, and access to industrial
infrastructure. Detailed scheme provisions are accessible on the official portal:
https://unnati.dpiit.gov.in.
    The scheme covers all eight North Eastern States: Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur,
Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura. The total scheme outlay is ₹10,037
crore, and the registration window remains open until 31 March 2026.
Eligibility and Investment Thresholds
       Manufacturing Sector: Minimum investment of ₹1 crore
       Services Sector: Minimum investment of ₹50 lakh
       Micro Enterprises: Minimum investment of ₹50 lakh (Manufacturing or Services)
       Existing Units: Eligible on undertaking a minimum of 25% expansion over previous
        investment
    Districts within the NER are categorised into Zone A (Industrially Advanced) and Zone
B (Other Districts). In Assam, Kamrup Metropolitan, Kamrup, Nalbari, Nagaon, and Jorhat
are designated as Zone A; all remaining districts fall under Zone B.
Scheme Incentives
1. Capital Investment Incentive (CII)
Applicable to both new and expanding units:
       Zone A: 30% of eligible investment (maximum ₹5 crore; where GST is not
        applicable, up to ₹10 crore)
       Zone B: 50% of eligible investment (maximum ₹7.5 crore; where GST is not
        applicable, up to ₹10 crore)
2. Central Capital Interest Subvention (CIS)
Interest support on term loans (up to ₹250 crore principal):
       Zone A: 3% per annum for up to 7 years
       Zone B: 5% per annum for up to 7 years




  182
                            Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



3. Manufacturing & Services Linked Incentive (MSLI)
Available for new units only:
      Zone A: Incentive up to 75%
      Zone B: Incentive up to 100%
       Eligible units receive MSLI equivalent to 100% of net GST paid (Gross GST less
       Input Tax Credit) for a period of up to 10 years.
Sectoral Coverage
Positive List (Service Sector) includes:
      Hotels, resorts, guest houses and allied hospitality services
      Tourism services such as homestays, houseboats, cruise services, adventure
       tourism, film tourism, ropeways, and amusement parks
      Heritage property restoration services
      Bio-technology and healthcare (secondary & tertiary)
      EV charging infrastructure
      IT-ITeS (Data Centres)
      Technology-oriented start-ups including EdTech
Negative List excludes:
      Tobacco and related products under CGST Chapter 24
      Petroleum/gas refinery products under Central Excise Chapter 27
      Low-value addition activities (storage, basic packaging, re-labelling)
      Cement, arms and ammunition
      Units non-compliant with environmental requirements
      Tourism services reliant solely on mobile units without fixed infrastructure
      BPO, Fin-tech, financial services and education (vocational/digital) units
      Other categories as determined by the Steering Committee
Scheme Implementation Status (as on 12 January 2026 – Assam)
      Registrations received: 507
      Proposed investment: ₹10,154 crore
      Projected employment generation: 26,512 persons


10.Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises(PMFME)
   The Pradhan Mantri Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)
Scheme is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) of the Government of India, launched to
formalize the unorganised micro food processing sector. With an overall outlay of ₹10,000
crore, the scheme aims to formalize 200,000 micro food processing enterprises nationwide
during the period 2020–21 to 2025–26. The State of Assam has been allocated an overall
target of 12,778 units, with a revised target of 6,000 units for the financial year 2025–26.
   In Assam, the Department of Industries, Commerce and Public Enterprises serves as
the State Nodal Department, with the Assam Industrial Development Corporation Ltd.
(AIDC) designated as the State Nodal Agency. A dedicated State Project Management Unit

                                                                                      183
                                Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




(SPMU) has been established to support scheme implementation, while the scheme is
executed at the district level through District Industries and Commerce Centres (DICC).
Private District Resource Persons (DRPs) are empanelled to mobilize beneficiaries and
provide implementation support.
1. Scheme Components
   Credit-linked subsidy at 35% of capital investment, up to a maximum of ₹10 lakh, is
   provided for setting up or upgrading food processing units. Eligible entities include
   individuals, proprietorships, partnerships, FPOs, FPCs, cooperatives, NGOs and SHGs.
   Proposals are submitted via the online PMFME portal. Post-sanction monitoring and
   support for formal registrations (e.g., UDYAM, FSSAI, GST where applicable) are
   provided by DRPs.
2. Seed Capital for SHG Members

        Under this component, eligible SHG members linked to Assam State Rural
        Livelihood Mission (ASRLM) and Assam Urban Livelihood Mission (ASULM) may
        receive soft loans of up to ₹40,000 per member as grant funding to purchase
        machinery, packaging and raw materials. This enables SHG members to scale and
        transition into credit-linked subsidy beneficiaries.

3. Capacity Building
   Beneficiaries receive enterprise development training to enhance business skills.
   Training is delivered in two formats:
        o    Three-day training for credit-linked subsidy beneficiaries at the district level.
        o    One-day training for beneficiaries approved for seed capital support.
4. Common Infrastructure Support
   To strengthen supply chain linkages, credit-linked capital subsidy at 35% of eligible
   project cost (up to ₹3.00 crore) is provided to establish common infrastructure
   facilities. Eligible costs include plant & machinery and technical civil works (capped at
   30% of project cost), with total project cost not exceeding ₹10 crore. Applications are
   invited    from   SHGs,    FPOs,   FPCs,   cooperatives,    federations   and   government
   organisations. Facilities operate on a pay-per-use basis.
   An Incubation Centre at Tezpur University has been supported with ₹2.73 crore to
   establish five food processing lines for grains, fruits & vegetables, and spices. Of this,
   ₹2.35 crore has been released, and the centre is operational for public utilisation to
   support enterprise incubation.
5. Branding and Marketing Support
   The scheme offers 50% grant assistance to support branding and marketing activities
   proposed by Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) created by PMFME enterprises,
   government organisations, FPOs, FPCs, SHGs, cooperatives and federations. Eligible
   expenditures include brand creation, packaging design, and development of online
   marketing channels.The following table depicts the Year-wise progress of the PMFME
   scheme in Assam

11.Prime Minister Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
    The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India
introduced the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP) in 2008. This
scheme, which provides a credit-linked subsidy, aims to create employment opportunities.

   The Ministry of MSME administers PMEGP as a Central Sector programme, with the
Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) designated as the National Nodal Agency.
The implementation of the scheme is carried out by the Khadi and Village Industries Board
(KVIB) and District Industries & Commerce Centre (DICC). Under this scheme, units in
urban areas are eligible for a subsidy of 25%, while units in rural areas can receive a
subsidy of 35%. Manufacturing sector projects up to Rs. 50 Lakh and service sector
projects up to Rs. 20 lakh can be undertaken under this scheme.




                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       185
                                Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




The positive outcome of PMEGP

  The PMEGP has proven to be a catalyst for positive results, fostering growth and
development across multiple sectors. Some of the positive outcome are:

  1.    Income Generation
  2.    Employment Generation
  3.    Poverty Alleviation
  4.    Rural Development
  5.    Financial Inclusion.

across the state. From 1st April 2024 to 31st March 2025, a total of 3224 projects have
been sanctioned worth Margin Money of Rs 9465.7lakhs. A total of 3143 projects have
been disbursed worth Margin Money of Rs 9016.76 lakhs. From 1 st April 2025 to 7th January

lakhs. A total of 1338 projects have been disbursed worth Margin Money of Rs. 3934.55
lakhs

    This has enabled individuals to establish and expand small businesses, thereby

SOME MAJOR INDUSTRIES IN ASSAM
TEA INDUSTRY:
    The tea industry holds a central position in Assam’s economy, with its origins dating
back to the early nineteenth century when commercially produced Assam tea was first
shipped to the United Kingdom in 1838. Assam remains the largest tea-producing region
in India, contributing more than half of the country’s total tea output and accounting for a
significant share of global production. The extensive area under tea cultivation in the State
includes large estates operated by reputed Indian and multinational companies as well as
numerous small tea gardens established by local entrepreneurs.
    According to Tea Board and State statistics, the tea sector in Assam comprises several
hundred estates and gardens and generates employment for approximately seven lakh
workers on a daily basis, representing a substantial proportion of the sector’s total
workforce nationwide. Assam tea’s enduring reputation for quality and its substantial
contribution to production and employment underscore its continued importance to both
the State and national economy
   Assam has witnessed a spurt in the growth of small tea holdings during the last three
decades and there are 1.33 lakh small holdings in the year 2025 accounting for 313.52
million kg in production. Most of the Small Tea Growers (STGs) are first generation young
and educated entrepreneurs who have started contributing immensely towards the
transformation of socio-economic life in rural Assam. As per Tea Board of India, in 2025
there were 133833 nos. registered Small Tea Growers (with an area up to 10.12 hectares
of land) in Assam covering a total area of 126067.81 ha of land.
The Small Tea Growers produced 313.52 million kg in 2025. The number of big grower tea
estates (i.e. with holding above 10.12 hectares) as per the Tea Board, in the state is 763




                                                                                      187
                                   Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




covering a geographical area of 232864.282 ha and they have produced 321.85 million kg
of tea in 2025.
    The total production of tea in Assam was 675.88 million kg during 2023 and total tea
production was 621.60 million kgs in 2024 and 635.37 million kgs in 2025. Year wise no
of gardens, area, production and average yield of tea in the State is given in the Table
11.9 which has also been graphically depicted in Fig 11.4

   Recognizing the need to improve the profitability of the tea sector and ensure its
long-term financial sustainability by promoting a shift from predominantly CTC
production to increased orthodox and speciality tea manufacturing, the Government of
Assam has introduced the Assam Tea Industries Special Incentives Scheme (ATISIS),
2020. This strategic intervention is intended to reduce the over-supply of CTC tea and
thereby support price enhancement over time.



   188
                           Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



    Under ATISIS, four key components of benefits are provided to encourage the
production of orthodox and speciality teas—including green, white, Oolong, Singhpo,
purple, yellow and other non-CTC specialty varieties—namely: interest subvention on
working capital, orthodox and speciality tea production subsidy, subsidy for plant and
machinery for orthodox and speciality tea units, and agricultural income tax holiday for
eligible producers. The scheme has four components:

  1. Component-I: Interest Subvention on Working Capital Loan: An interest
     subvention of 3% p.a., a maximum 20 lakhs per annum, will be provided on Working
     Capital Loan.
  2. Component-II: Subsidy on Orthodox or Specialty Tea Production: An
     industrial unit manufacturing Orthodox tea/ Green tea / White tea / Oolong tea /
     Singhpo Tea / Purple Tea / Yellow tea or other Speciality tea (not manufactured
     through CTC (Crush, Tear, Curl) process will be eligible for a subsidy of Rs. 7 per kg
     against such tea manufactured in a financial year. This subsidy has been increased
     from Rs.7/- per KG to Rs.10/- per KG till the end of this scheme. In view of the
     completion of 200 years of Assam Tea, the Government has decided to increase the
     production subsidy to Rs.12/- for the financial year 2023-24.
  3. Component-III: Subsidy for Orthodox & Specialty Tea Unit for Plant &
     Machinery: A subsidy of 25% of the cost of Plant & Machinery of orthodox or any
     other Speciality tea will be provided.
  4. Component-IV: Agricultural Income Tax Holiday: Six year agricultural income
     tax holiday starting from Financial Year 2019-20 to 2024-25.

     The State Government has announced extension of the Scheme for another 5 years
i.e. till the financial year 2027-28. So far, an amount of ₹109.94 Cr. has been disbursed
to 647 Tea Estates under the ATISIS Scheme. The status of achievement under the ATISIS
for 2022-23 is given below:

RUBBER PLANTATION
   The rubber plantation has gained popularity in Assam due to congenial agro-climatic
conditions in the state. The Rubber Board has identified Assam as a “Potential state” from
the “productivity” point of view as the state has ample scope for the expansion of rubber
plantations.
    Between 2023–24 and provisional estimates of 2024–25, all key metrics showed
positive growth. The area under cultivation increased from 79,600 ha to 94,500 ha, a rise
of about 18.7%, while production grew modestly from 46,500 MT to 47,500 MT, an
increase of approximately 2.1%. The tapping area expanded slightly from 37,370 ha to
37,900 ha, reflecting around 1.4% growth. Employment generation saw a substantial jump



  190
                              Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



from 254,720 to 302,400 persons, also increasing by roughly 18.7%. These figures
indicate robust expansion in cultivated area and labor engagement, with relatively smaller
gains in actual production and tapping. The Area and Production of Rubber has been

COFFEE PLANTATION
    Coffee was first introduced in Assam in 1953 in Cachar district. Pilot cultivation began
in 1954 under the State Forest and Soil Conservation Department.
   The Coffee Board initiated systematic activities during the IX Five Year Plan (1997–
2002). Coffee promotion aimed to curb jhum cultivation, prevent forest degradation, and
provide sustainable livelihoods to tribal farmers.
   Assam’s coffee plantations are a growing part of India’s coffee map, with cultivation
mainly in Dima Hasao (Haflong), Cachar, Karbi Anglong and other districts. Both Arabica

                                                                                               191
                                     Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




and Robusta are grown on a modest scale, adding earthy, spicy flavours to the region’s
agricultural output.
Areas of Coffee Cultivation
   Coffee is presently grown in Dima Hasao, Karbi Anglong, and Bijni–Shantipur areas of
Chirang district (BTR).
         Dima Hasao: Coffee development started in 1978 with a Technology Evaluation
          Centre (1980). The region has elevations of 1100–2300 ft, rainfall of 1500–2500
          mm, red lateritic soils with high organic matter, and temperatures ranging from 7–
          26°C, making it highly suitable for coffee.
         Karbi Anglong: Coffee plantations were established in tribal blocks to promote
          socio-economic development. During the IX Plan, 49 ha were planted in Hapjan
          and Umcherra villages, but group plantations were later abandoned due to law and
          order issues.
         Chirang: (Bijni/Shantipur): Located in the foothills of Bhutan, this area has 1800–
          2200 mm rainfall, acidic porous soils (pH 4.5–6.2), and is ideal for Robusta (CxR)
          coffee. About 90% of the population depends on agriculture.

Ongoing Coffee Development Schemes in the North Eastern Region
(Period: 2022–23 to 2024–25)
Background
   The Coffee Board is implementing multiple developmental interventions in the North
Eastern Region (NER) with the objective of expanding coffee cultivation, improving
productivity and quality, enhancing growers’ income, and providing sustainable livelihood
opportunities, particularly to tribal communities.
Key Interventions
   1. Coffee Expansion / Consolidation
      Financial assistance is provided for expansion of coffee cultivation in new suitable
      areas and for consolidation, rejuvenation, and productivity enhancement of
      existing plantations to improve overall output and farmer income.
   2. Raising of Seedlings through Group Nurseries
      Support is extended for raising quality coffee seedlings through group nurseries
      to ensure availability of good planting material and proper establishment of coffee
      plantations.
   3. Quality Up-gradation
      Assistance is provided for creation of infrastructure such as baby pulpers and
      drying yards to facilitate production of quality coffee and improve market
      realization for growers.
   4. Organic / Eco-certification
      This initiative promotes production of organic and eco-certified coffee to enable
      access to high-value specialty markets. The scheme also encourages formation of
      grower groups/collectives to facilitate eco-certification and development of
      common facilities.
   5. Water Augmentation
      Financial support is provided for creation of infrastructure for water augmentation
      for irrigation and wet processing of coffee, aimed at improving productivity and
      quality.
   6. Support for Coffee Marketing (MSS)
      Under the Marketing Support Scheme, the Board provides complete logistical
      support from farm-gate collection of estate-processed coffee to sale through
      a transparent auction platform, ensuring fair price discovery and improved
      returns to growers.
   7. Welfare Measures for Children of Plantation Labourers
      Educational stipends, merit incentives, and financial assistance for higher
      education are provided to the children of SC/ST labourers working in coffee
      plantations and curing establishments, particularly for those pursuing studies
      beyond Class X.
Research & Capacity Building
    A Regional Coffee Research Station, established in 1985 at Diphu, Assam, over an
area of 25 hectares, undertakes development of location-specific technologies for coffee
cultivation in NER. The station also demonstrates scientific cultivation practices and
conducts regular training and capacity-building programmes for tribal coffee farmers.


                                                                                    193
                             Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




Outcome
    The integrated approach covering production, quality improvement, marketing
support, welfare measures, and R&D is contributing towards sustainable development of
the coffee sector in the North Eastern Region with improved income security for tribal
growers.

SERICULTURE
      The Sericulture sector in Assam is deeply inter-wined with the cultural heritage and
plays a pivotal role in its economy. Four type of Silk namely Eri, Muga, Silk and Mulberry
are produced in Assam. But for Muga, Assam has been recognised as the Hub.

      The origins of sericulture in this region dated back to around 3000-2000 BC with the
arrival of Tibeto- Burman Groups and its prominence is reflected in ancient texts like
Valmiki’s Ramayana and Kautilya’sArthashastra. By 7th Century, Assam’s silk was
renowned, with King Bhaskaravarman of Kamrup presenting fine silk fabrics to King
Harshavardhan of North India. During the Ahom Dynasty, Silk production became central
to the royal courts receiving royal patronage from Ahom Kings.

      Today Assam continue to lead India’s silk industry, contributing 90% of the country’s
total Muga Silk, which is endemic to the region, and 65% of its Eri Silk, and ranks 3rd in
overall silk production. Assam’s Muga silk, recognised with a Geographical Indication (GI)
Tag in 2007 is globally renowned for its golden hue and superior quality. The Sericulture
sector support s approximately 32000 Muga reares, 5000 Mugareelers, and 10000
Weavers with 65% of the workforce comprising Women Folk. In total 300,000 Families
across 8722 Villages are engaged in sericulture activities.

   With the introduction of modern technologies such as motorised reeling, waste
processing units and certified looms, the sector has enhanced both the quality and
productivity of its silk, opening up new commercial opportunities. These advancements,
coupled with Government support through financial assistance, have created sustainable
forward linkage in value-added process such as yarn reeling, weaving, apparel, and
product diversification further boosting the State’s economy.

   With     its   long-standing     tradition,     growing    technological     advancements,   and
commitment to sustainability, Assam’s sericulture industry remains a cornerstone of the
State’s economy. Continued investment in the infrastructure and innovation will ensure
the industry’s expansion and maintain Assam’s leadership in global Silk production.

HANDLOOM
    Handloom weaving in Assam represents a cherished generational legacy, preserved
and sustained by generations of skilled artisans and deeply intertwined with the State’s
cultural heritage. It is a labour-intensive activity that provides significant employment,
particularly for women, who constitute a substantial proportion of the handloom workforce
and play a key role in its production and continuity.
   The sector has continued to support socio-economic development in rural and semi-
urban areas by offering livelihood opportunities and preserving traditional craftsmanship,
while gradually adapting to meet market demand through increased commercial
production.
    The state had an estimated number of 78642 full time weavers and 680687 nos. of
part time weavers during 2024-25. There were 210 handloom demonstration circles in the
state covering 21642 villages. In 2024-25 there were 135 Handloom Training Centres in
the state accommodating 1516 trainees. Combined Handloom production during the year
2024-25 in the weaver’s extension service units and handloom production centres of the
Directorate was 14549.92 Meters.
   The Directorate has been implementing various schemes and programmes under the
State Sector Schemes and Central Sector. Some of them are discussed below:


       SWANIRBHAR NAARI SCHEME
   An initiative under the Directorate of Handloom & Textiles, Assam to directly procure
handloom items from the indigenous weavers of the State through a dedicated online
portal (swanirbharnaari.assam.gov.in) under the State flagship scheme, “SWANIRBHAR
NAARI (SNN)” without involving any middlemen. The total no. of approved registered
weavers under this Scheme to date was 5, 64,811, marking a significant milestone in the
scheme’s implementation.

 THE SUALKUCHI INSTITUTE OF FASHION TECHNOLOGY (SIFT)
   The Sualkuchi Institute of Fashion Technology (SIFT) was established on 30 August
2008 under the initiative of the Kamrup (Rural) District Administration to provide short-
term, in-house training in textile and fashion designing, primarily targeting weavers and
unemployed youth for self-employment.
   The institute receives government support in the form of grants-in-aid for its operations
and development. During 2022–23, ₹95.00 lakh was sanctioned and released. In 2024–
25, ₹27.00 lakh was allocated, sanctioned, and released, and a similar amount of ₹27.00
lakh was provided for running and development in 2025–26. Additionally, ₹28.50 lakh has
been allocated in the budget provision for SIFT for the financial year 2025–26.


 HANDLOOM MODEL VILLAGE
   The Government of Assam has implemented the Handloom Model Village scheme at
Koklabari in Baksa district with the objective of achieving sustainable economic growth
through handloom development.. During 2022–23, the project covered 478 targeted
weavers with a total project cost of ₹315.47 lakh, of which ₹157.72 lakh was released as
the first installment. An allocation of ₹200.00 lakh was made in the budget for 2024–25
for implementation; however, the funds could not be drawn. Subsequently, for 2025–26,
₹250.00 lakh has been provided in the budget, and financial sanction of ₹157.75 lakh has
been accorded for implementation of the Handloom Model Village at Koklabari.


 SAMARTH


   SAMARTH is a skill development scheme of the Ministry of Textiles, Government of
India, implemented in Assam through the Directorate of Handloom & Textiles, Assam. The
scheme aims to build skilled manpower in the handloom and textile sector through
structured training aligned with national guidelines.

   A total of 158 training centres were approved in Assam, with an initial target of training
17,820 candidates. These centres are being upgraded into smart training centres with
biometric attendance, CCTV, power backup, internet connectivity, and essential classroom
facilities. Trainers are required to undergo Training of Trainers (ToT) conducted by the
Textile Committee, which also certifies trainers and assesses trainees.

   Each course has a duration of 300 hours, comprising 30% theory and 70% practical
training, with training kits and study materials provided to trainees. Successful candidates
receive skill certification and are enabled to pursue employment or self-employment in the
handloom sector.

    Implementation was delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to a reduction of
the training target to 6,198 candidates. Full-scale training resumed in November 2021 and
is scheduled for completion by 31 March 2026. The table 11.19 showing year wise progress
of SAMARTH is given below:

TOURISM
    Tourism in Assam is anchored in the State’s rich natural and cultural assets, including
abundant wildlife, scenic landscapes, unique flora and fauna, revered holy sites, verdant
tea gardens, and vibrant cultural festivals. Eco-tourism has emerged as one of the fastest
growing segments, prompting the Government of Assam to prioritise its development.
While the traditional peak tourism season in the State extends from October to May, efforts
are underway to establish Assam as a year-round tourism destination by promoting
attractions and experiences suited to all seasons and showcasing them in national and
international forums. Strategic promotional campaigns aim to enhance visibility and attract
a diverse range of visitors.

     The Tourism Department serves as the nodal agency responsible for policy formulation
and programme implementation for the development and promotion of tourism in the
State. Over the years, the Department has invested in infrastructure and supporting
facilities with financial assistance from the Central Government, State Government and
the North Eastern Council (NEC) to improve accessibility and visitor experience. Recent
initiatives include the introduction of signature events such as the Brahmaputra Carnival
along the banks of the mighty river, which offers cultural, adventure and lifestyle
experiences for tourists, and the promotion of tea tourism as a unique product offering.
The Department also undertakes guide training and other capacity-building measures to
enhance service quality and support the sustainable growth of the tourism sector.

Key Highlights of “Tourism Policy of Assam, 2022”

    The Assam Tourism Policy, 2022 is a part of Assam's strategy to enable rapid growth
in the Tourism sector. This policy provides a comprehensive framework for the state's
tourism sector to grow in an inclusive and sustainable manner. The policy's goals are to
improve the state's tourism development framework, promote tourism related industries,
and strengthen tourism support services.

    Assam's tourism policy has been developed to closely align with the National Tourism
policy and highlights areas where collaboration will be sought from the Ministry of
Tourism. This policy will replace the five-year Tourism Policy of Assam, 2017.

ASSAM SCIENCE TECHNOLOGY AND ENVIRONMENT COUNCIL (ASTEC):
   The Assam Science Technology and Environment Council (ASTEC) is an autonomous
body constituted in 1986–87 under the Science, Technology and Climate Change
Department, Government of Assam             to implement key science, technology and
environment programmes in the state. Its mandate is to identify and support areas where
science and technology can drive socio-economic development, to promote and coordinate
research and development, to foster scientific temper and innovation, and to advise and
provide financial support to researchers and institutions for sustainable development
initiatives. ASTEC executes a range of central and state schemes — spanning research and
development,    science   popularisation,   education,   capacity   building,   environmental
awareness, science centres and technology interventions — with the objective of
strengthening human resources and addressing developmental challenges across Assam.


MINING
   The Directorate of Geology and Mining (DGM), Assam, established in 1960 under the
Mines and Minerals Department, Government of Assam, functions as the State’s nodal
geo-scientific agency. The Directorate is entrusted with the responsibility of providing
scientific inputs for exploration, assessment, and monitoring of mineral and groundwater
resources across the State. In addition, it administers mineral resources through grant of
exploration licences and mining leases, auction of mineral blocks, approval and monitoring
of mining plans, issuance of dealer licences, and collection of revenue in the form of
royalty, fees, and rents from minerals, oil, and natural gas.


   The primary objective of these programmes is to evaluate the economic potential of
mineral resources, including groundwater, for industrial use and to create sustainable
revenue streams for the State. Revenue collection from mineral resources remains a key
performance indicator of the Directorate’s functioning.


   Over the last three financial years, the Directorate of Geology and Mining, Assam, has
made a significant contribution to the State exchequer. Royalty and related collections
amounted to ₹4,121.36 crore in 2022–23, ₹3,792.76 crore in 2023–24, and ₹3,926.67
crore in 2024–25. During the current financial year 2025–26, revenue of ₹2,339.39 crore
has already been collected up to November 2025, reflecting sustained growth in mineral-
based revenue mobilisation.


   A major achievement during this period has been the successful auction of seven
limestone blocks with an estimated total resource value of ₹62,769.26 crore. These blocks
are expected to generate approximately ₹10,184 crore as royalty over a lease period of
50 years. The estimated auction premium from these blocks stands at ₹3,011.75 crore,
calculated on the basis of the prevailing Average Sale Price of limestone. One of the leased
limestone blocks has been operationalized within nine months of issuance of the Letter of
Intent, indicating effective post-auction implementation. The total upfront payment
received from all seven blocks during 2024–25 and 2025–26 amounts to ₹124.56 crore.




  202
                           Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



   The Directorate has also successfully completed multiple exploration projects funded
by the National Mineral Exploration Trust (NMET) and the Central Mine Planning and Design
Institute (CMPDI) during 2023–24. These include exploration of limestone in the
Voteranglangso area of West Karbi Anglong district, iron ore in the Lengpara area of
Goalpara district, sillimanite in the Samelangso area of Karbi Anglong district, and coal in
the Larbo area of Dima Hasao district. In 2024–25, four additional NMET-approved
limestone exploration projects were initiated in Karbi Anglong and Dima Hasao districts,
which will continue into 2025–26. Further, proposals for two G-3 level limestone
exploration projects in Choto Lakhindong and Krungming areas of Dima Hasao district are
under consideration of the Ministry of Mines, Government of India.


   During the review period, two mining lease deeds were executed—one for a sillimanite
block in Karbi Anglong district and another for a limestone block in Dima Hasao district.
Additionally, six granite blocks were auctioned in 2024–25 with a sold value of ₹361.87
crore, expected to yield approximately ₹11 crore annually as royalty.


   Overall, the Directorate of Geology and Mining, Assam, has demonstrated consistent
progress in mineral exploration, transparent auctioning, and revenue generation, thereby
supporting industrial development and strengthening the State’s fiscal resources.

CHAPTER-XII

                                       POWER


P
     ower here means the electrical & solar energy which are the key inputs for overall
     development of the economy of the state. Electricity has direct impact on the core
     sectors of the economy viz. Agriculture, Industry, Irrigation, and Transport &
Communication, etc. Therefore, augmentation of the Power Sector is directly related to
the expansion of various economic activities of the state as well as the country.

    From 2022-23 to 2024-25, the Gross State Value Added (GSVA) from electricity sector
of Assam has grown at an average rate of 20.62 per cent per year. During the same period,
impressive growth in major sectors that are directly related to power has such as
Manufacturing (10%), Communication and broadcasting (15.76%), Hotels& Restaurants
(22.61%) have also exhibited impressive growth patterns.

    The growth and development of a particular region is determined to a large extent by
energy availability and per capita consumption of energy. As the economy of the state has
regained its momentum in the post Covid period, electricity consumption in the state has
also rapidly increased. From 2022-23 to 2024-25, the total power consumption (in MU)
has increased by a staggering 13.91% per year. During this period, the per capita
domestic consumption of power (both domestic & commercial) has also increased by
9.29% per annum.

    In Assam the entire power industry of the State was managed by “Assam State
Electricity Board (ASEB)” up to 10th December, 2004 after that it was divided into the
following three entities to meet the power requirements of the State.

        4. The Assam Power Distribution Company Limited (APDCL)
        5. The Assam Electricity Grid Corporation Limited (AEGCL)
        6. The Assam Power Generation Corporation Limited (APGCL)

1. The Assam Power Distribution Company Limited (APDCL):
    Assam Power Distribution Company Limited (APDCL) is to undertake distribution,
trading and supply of electricity in the state of Assam in accordance with provisions of
applicable law and all activities ancillary to it.
    It has the mandate to develop, maintain and operate the power distribution system in
the state of Assam by carrying out the business of power supply to every part of the state.
    The Assam Power Distribution Company Limited has a vision to be the catalyst for
holistic growth of the state by powering agriculture and industry: lighting homes – rural
and urban, and generating internal resources for continually improving technology and
delivery systems to induce customers’ delight”.


(A) Power Supply Position:
    Energy requirement in Assam was worked out at 15556 MU (Million Units) for the year
2024-25. At the same time the peak demand of electricity in the state has been increased
from 2576 MW in 2023-24 to 2684 MW in 2024-25. There is no shortfall of power during
this period as per records.

(C) TRANSMISSION, DISTRIBUTION & COMMERCIAL LOSSES:
The power supplied through various stages of transformation from sources to final
consumers involves energy loss known as transmission, distribution and commercial
losses.
The aggregate transmission and commercial losses in the state is 16.22% in 2022-23,
which has decreased to 15.86% in 2023-24 and 15.73% in 2024-25.
The measures taken up by APDCL to bring down distribution losses are:-
  1. Implementation of Artificial intelligence in recording the meter readings for accurate
     billing of consumers to bring down the commercial losses.
  2. Energy auditing at feeder and transformer level to identify the core loss making
     areas.
  3. Installation of smart meters.
  4. Installation of energy efficient distribution transformers to reduce transformation
     losses
  5. Energy bill payment through mobile application, UPI, prepaid wallets, etc.
  6. Construction of new distribution sub stations under Asian Infrastructure Investment
     Bank (AIIB) Scheme for bifurcation of lengthy feeders.
  7. Conversion of bare LT lines to insulated cables in theft prone areas
  8. Re-conducting of 33 KV, 11 KV and LT lines under Revamped Distribution Sector
     Scheme (RDSS)

(E) INITIATIVES ON SOLAR POWER GENERATION IN ASSAM:
    The current energy scenario and the deteriorating environmental plight even
threatening extinction of humanity have compelled nations to embrace Renewable Energy
research & development. Economic development of a state resembles the overall growth
in various sectors. Consumption of electricity in Assam is increasing at a steady pace every
year hence to reduce the conventional energy consumption growth in renewable energy
field is extremely crucial.

Assam Energy Development Agency (AEDA)
    The Assam Energy Development Agency (AEDA) will ensure the convergence in the
     areas of New and Renewable Sources of Energy (NRSE) for the State of Assam by
     disseminating information to initiate, promote, support and co-ordinate all activities
     in the field of Renewable Energy Sources with other stakeholders and by concerted
     efforts of governments, local institutions, NGOs, the private sector as well as the
     international community towards the promotion of different DRE technologies.
    As a technical entity in new and renewable energy sources within the state, the
     organisation is responsible for exploring and promotion of various renewable
     energy technologies through different decentralized power generation models to
     achieve SDG7.
    The previous data pursuance of different NRSE projects may be helpful for the
     baseline assessment and implementation of DRE project

    Power sector in India has been thriving steadily since Independence and is predicted
to witness massive development in the field of renewable energy in the near future. Energy
sector plays a key role in the economic growth of the country.

   AEDA is implementing various types of renewable projects in the solar field, viz.
Rooftop SPV, Solar Street Lights, Floating Solar Power plants since inception.

2. The Assam Electricity Grid Corporation Limited (AEGCL):
    Assam Electricity Grid Corporation Limited, a vibrant growth oriented Public Sector
Company registered under ‘Company Act, 1956’. It was formed by restructuring Assam
State Electricity Board in 2003 and was notified as the State Transmission Utility (STU).
Its core business is to efficiently transport electrical power from electrical power bulk heads
to the distribution company networks in the state of Assam. Assam Electricity Grid
Corporation Limited inherited 3862 Circuit Kilometres of Extra High Voltage (EHV) lines
above 66 KV voltage class and 38 numbers of EHV sub-stations having a total




  210
                            Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



transformation capacity of 1636.50 Mega Volt Ampere (MVA) at its year of formation in
2003.
    After 2003 with the inclusion of new sub stations and transmission lines its
transmission capacity has been increased up to 7826 MVA, line length 5248.68 Circuit
Kilometres and 73 nos. of substation which includes 1 no. 400 KV (Kilovolt), 12 nos. Of
220 KV, 60 nos. of 132 KV stations as on October, 2022.
     Assam Electricity Grid Corporation Limited (AEGCL) is playing a strategic role as it the
largest “STU” in the North Eastern Region. It also understands it responsibility towards
the entire North East India and is always extending a helping hand by way of transporting
a fair share of power to the other sister States of the region.
   AEGCL has consistently maintained the transmission system availability at over 99%
which is at par with other National Transmission Utilities.
    AEGCL vows to ever strive till all transmission bottlenecks get eradicated. It pledges
to deliver unrelenting brilliance in performance, deliver power efficiently but economically,
so high safety standers and is committed to respecting environmental and heritage issues.

3. The Assam Power Generation Corporation Limited (APGCL):

capacity in 2024-25, gross 2285.45 MU were generated out of which 102.02 MU were
auxiliary consumption and 2183.51 MU were net unit generation of electricity.
    The vision of APGCL’s is to achieve generation expansion up to 2000 MW by the year
2030 including power generation from renewable energy sources such as hydro and solar
etc. to cope with the growing energy demand and to accelerate economic growth in the
state.

   T
           he Transport and Communication sector has emerged as one of the fastest
           growing segments of the Assam economy, playing a crucial role in enhancing
           connectivity, mobility, and access to services. During 2024-25, the sector
accounted for 5.27 per cent of the Gross State Value Added (GSVA) of the State, and its
contribution is projected to increase to 5.42 per cent by 2026-27. Over the last four years,
the sector has recorded robust and consistent growth, supported by substantial expansion
in road infrastructure, rising motor vehicle density, and improved public transport services.
Significant progress has been achieved under programmes such as PMGSY, leading to
enhanced rural and inter-district connectivity. Growth in rail electrification, expansion of
air transport capacity, and modernization of inland water transport have further
strengthened the transport network. On the communication front, expansion of postal
services and steady growth in telecom subscribers have improved digital and information
connectivity, thereby supporting economic activity and inclusive development across the
State.

    Transport and Communication has multidimensional effect for overall growth and
development of the state economy. Growth in this sector has significant impact upon
various other important economic sectors such as health & education, manufacturing,
services etc. During the year 2024-25, transport & communication sector has contributed
5.27% to the total Gross State Value Added (GSVA) of the State which is expected to
increase up to 5.42% in 2026-27. During the last four years the transport and
communication sector has exhibited impressive growth as shown in the table below:

ASSSAM STATE TRANSPORT CORPORATION:

    Assam State Transport Corporation (ASTC) is a state government owned Road
Transport Corporation of Assam which provides reliable, safe, dependable and
comfortable passenger bus services within Assam and adjoining states. Assam State
Transport was started as a State Government Department with two buses to run
between Guwahati and Nagaon. Gradually, the transport network of the department
expanded throughout the state of Assam. The state transport department was converted
to a corporation on 31st March 1970.

    As a step towards improvement of passenger amenities, ASTC has initiated major
infrastructure development projects like the Construction of ISBT at Khanapara
in Guwahati, Construction of ISBT at Tezpur and development of station
building at Majuli.

RAILWAYS:

    The development of rail infrastructure in North Eastern Region is one of the priority
areas of the Ministry of Railways. The endeavour of the Government is to provide rail
connectivity to all the sister states in the region and thereafter, extend the same to the
capital cities. Out of 8 States of North Eastern Region, rail network connectivity now exists
in 7 States. Sikkim is being connected with the new line project Sivok-Rangpo (44.96 km).

kilometre of Railways (i.e. length of tracks under operation) under broad gauge railway is

to 3374 Km in 2024-25. Table 13.8 below provides details of all routes and running tracks.

AIR TRANSPORT:

    Assam is well connected with the rest of the country through Air Transport. The state
has seven operational civil airports located at Guwahati, Tezpur, Jorhat, Dibrugarh, North
Lakhimpur, Dhubri and Silchar. All major airlines including private commercial airlines are
operating their flights to and from Guwahati to different locations of the country and an
international flight to Thailand from Guwahati. In addition to these civil airports, small
private airstrips in the interior areas are also present to address the need of the corporate
houses. A new integrated terminal at Lokapriya Gopinath Borodoloi International Airport
has recently been inaugurated that spans across 1.4 lakh square metres and can handle
up to 13.1 million passengers annually—a sixfold increase from the previous terminal’s
capacity.


INLAND WATER TRANSPORT:
   The Brahmaputra has 891 km navigable length of waterways from Sadiya to Dhubri as
National Waterway No.2 while the river Barak has 121 km length of navigable waterways
between Lakhipur and Bhanga as National Waterways No.6 for unified development of the

                                                                                      223
                                  Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




waterways for shipping and navigation and transportation of cargo to the North Eastern
Region particularly in the states of Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, Manipur, Tripura and
Arunachal Pradesh.
    The Government of Assam launched a project to transform the quality of Inland Water
Transport (IWT) services and integrate high quality passenger and vehicle ferry services
into Assam’s wider transport network system with the financial assistance from the World
Bank.
    The World Bank has sanctioned an amount of Rs 770 crore towards realising this goal
to Assam Inland Water Transport Development Society (AIWTDS), an autonomous society
registered under the Transport Department, Government of India.
    The government of Assam is implementing a World Bank funded “Assam Inland Water
Transport Project” through which a comprehensive River Information System (RIS) will be
set up for real-time monitoring of all boats/vessels operating on the River Brahmaputra
with an Integrated Command Control Centre (ICCC). Furthermore, the National
Technology Centre for Ports, Waterways and Coasts (NTCWPC) has been engaged to help
implementation of Night Navigation facilities on Brahmaputra. Further, an incentive based
scheme of the IWT named “Jibondinga” is being set up for an efficient and sustainable
ferry service system in the State.
   Directorate of Inland Water Transport is operating 94 nos. of ferry services in
Brahmaputra (NW-2) and Barak (NW-16) and other tributaries for transportation of
passengers. The feasibility of running river transport in 12 newly notified national
waterways has been established to develop the last mile inter-connectivity in NE region.
    Besides these state owned organisations, large number of private owners conducted
ferry services to transport goods and passengers to the remotest hinterlands under un-
organised sector by maintaining high level security measures.
    From the three ferry divisions viz. Guwahati, Jorhat and Silchar, Govt. has collected
total revenue of Rs. 57650648.00. Detailed division wise pessengers and goods carried
are provided in Table 13.8 below:

CHAPTER-XIV


                         INSTITUTIONAL FINANCE



  I
       nstitutional finance plays a crucial role in the economic development of the state
       by mobilizing deposits and providing credit to various sectors of the economy. The
       government has taken initiatives to secure institutional finance from banks and
other term-lending institutions to support development programs in Assam as a
supplementary financing plan. Banks and financial institutions are integral to this process,
addressing the credit needs of all sections of society as well as funding infrastructure
projects.

   Scheduled commercial banks and nationalized banks are actively involved in extending
credit to rural areas. Meanwhile, non-banking financial institutions (NBFIs) serve as
financial intermediaries that contribute significantly to capital formation. These institutions
address the growing financial needs of diverse segments of society, ranging from
microfinance for small households to financing for corporate entities.



Banking Institution:


       Commercial banks are the biggest financial intermediaries. They include both
scheduled and non-scheduled banks. The Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) comprises
of Public Sector Banks, Regional Rural Banks (RRB), Small Finance Banks, Private Banks,
Cooperative Banks and Foreign Banks. As per the SLBC (State level bankers committee
report) Report, 2025 there are 12 public sector banks, 14 private banks, 6 small finance
bank, 1 regional rural bank and 1 cooperative bank operating in the state. As per the SLBC
Report, about two percent of the total banking offices in India numbering 3243 branch
offices of SCB were functioning in the State As on 30 June, 2025. Of which 48 percent
were in rural areas, 29 percent were in semi-urban areas and 22.8 percent in urban areas.
The Credit-Deposit Ratio (CDR) of the SCB in the State as on 31 st March 2025 was 71.31
percent as per the SLBC Report, as against 79.51 percent at all India level. The facility of
onsite Automated Teller Machine (ATM) in the State was 4294 as against 255885 at All
India Level as on 31st March, 2025. Growth of SCB in the State and status of deposits and
credit since 2015 are given in table- 14.1 and district wise status of CD Ratio in respect of
all SCBs and of RRB (AGVB) are given at Annexure 14.1 and 14.2.

        In Assam, there were a total of 3243 Scheduled Commercial Bank (SCB) branches
(Reporting offices only) in the State as per SLBC Report as on 30 June ,2025. The share
of SCB branches in Assam is two percent of the total SCB branches at all-India level and
this indicates the low coverage of banking services. However, as seen from the Table- 14.1
over the period from 2015 to 2025 the compound annual growth of bank branches in
Assam has been 4.71% per annum which is higher than the all-India growth of 2.66% per
annum. Over 2015–2025, the number of offices in Assam grew at a substantially faster
annualized pace than the national average, indicating stronger relative expansion in Assam
compared to India as a whole. Assam's credit growth rate is approximately 1.5 times
higher than India's, which highlights focused financial development in the state.
        The distribution of bank branches (as on March, 2025) across the districts shows
that only ten districts in the State have more than 100 numbers of bank branches. In other
words, banking network coverage is not up to the mark in the State.

   The trend of the Credit–Deposit (C–D) Ratio of Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs)
in Assam, which had historically remained below the RBI’s indicative benchmark of 60
percent, has shown a marked and sustained improvement in recent years. The C–D ratio
improved to around 61 percent in 2024, crossing the RBI benchmark for the first time in
a sustained manner. This positive momentum further strengthened, and as of 30 June
2025, Assam’s C–D ratio has risen to about 72 percent, indicating a substantial
acceleration in credit deployment relative to deposits.

District wise C-D Ratio of Assam:
       As per Figure 14.3, out of the 17 districts presented, 13 districts have crossed the
60 percent C-D Ratio benchmark, indicating satisfactory credit deployment relative to
deposits. As per the figure, out of 33 districts in Assam, 26 districts have crossed the 60
percent C-D Ratio benchmark fixed for Scheduled Commercial Banks. Seven districts viz.
Dima Hasao, Hailakandi, Cachar, Hojai, Kokrajhar, Kamrup Metro and Chirang fall within
the 40–60 percent range, indicating moderate performance that requires monitoring and
targeted intervention. No district is below 40 percent, which reflects an overall
improvement in credit deployment across the State. Focused efforts are required in these
seven districts to enable them to cross the benchmark level.

Deposit of Commercial Bank:
    Deposits of SCBs increased overall by 6.17% in 2025 compared to 2024. This growth
was mainly driven by a strong rise in Term deposits (↑16.98%), indicating a preference
for long-term savings. In contrast, Current (-3.93%) and Savings deposits (-1.44%)
declined, reflecting lower transactional and savings balances. Urban areas continue to hold
the largest share of deposits, followed by semi-urban and rural regions, showing persistent
urban dominance in banking deposits.

Credit Support
    The public sector banks are the major supplier of credit requirements in the State. The
share of credit for Private Sector Banks in Assam was approximately 28.33 percent while
the same for Public Sector Banks was approximately 58.26 percent.
    In order to ensure availability of credit to agriculture, weaker section of the population
and other small scale sectors, the banks have to ensure at least 40 percent of the credit
to these priority sectors of the economy. Approximately 54 percent of the loans from banks
are made available to priority sectors in Assam as on 30.06.2025.
