REGIONAL RURAL BANKS:
   The two RRBs in the State, Assam Gramin Vikash Bank [AGVB] and Langpi Dehangi
Rural Bank [LDRB] operating in the Brahmaputra Valley and Barak Valley have been
amalgamated with effect from 1st April, 2019 as Assam Grameen Vikash Bank covering
entire geographical area of the State through its network of 468 branches. Further, after
amalgamation of United Bank of India (sponsor bank of AGVB) with the Punjab National

                                                                                     235
                                              Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




          Bank, the sponsorship of the bank has gone to Punjab National Bank w.e.f 1 st April, 2020.
          District wise deposit and credit status of RRB is given at Annexure 14.2.

                 Aggregate deposits of RRBs increased from ₹12,372.6 crore in March 2024 to
          ₹12,718.99 crore in March 2025, registering a growth of about 2.8%. Aggregate credit
          rose from ₹6,918.9 crore to ₹8,107.43 crore, showing a growth of about 17.2%. The
          Credit–Deposit Ratio improved to 63.74%, indicating better credit deployment of mobilized
          deposits by RRBs.

          THE ASSAM CO-OPERATIVE APEX BANK LTD:
             The Assam Co-operative Apex Bank Ltd was established as a State Cooperative Bank
          under the short-term Cooperative Credit Structure of the State in 1948. The Bank with a
          network of 67 (sixty-seven) branches and 6(six) zonal offices spread throughout the state
          extending all financial services including loans & advances, issuing of Kisan Credit Cards
          to small & marginal farmers of the state for seasonal Agricultural operation and other
          activities allied to agriculture and other Term Loan through the primary Agricultural Credit
          Societies (PACS) and also directly to farmers/ SHG/JLGs/Individuals/firms & companies &
          others. Out of 774 registered PACS (Gaon Panchayat Level Samabai Samittee) at bottom
          of the structure operating in the state, the Bank has adopted 543 number of PACS for
          economic development of farmers of which only 290 PACS has availed Credit from the
          Bank. CD Ratio of the Bank was estimated at 44.74% as on 30-06-2025 as against 42.58
          % % as on 31-03-2024. Share of the Bank’s Credit flow to priority sector as on 30.06.2025
          stood at 86 % as against 85.68% for the corresponding period as on 31-03-2024 which
          includes credit participation for food procurement through Food Credit Consortium.
              There are various important government Schemes/Projects under implementation in
          the State for upliftment of the poor as well as women and unemployed youth. Some of the
          flagship Schemes/Projects and their outcome is presented at Table 14.10

Financial Inclusion:
   The basic objective of financial inclusion is to provision of banking services to
underprivileged section and to unbank and under-banked regions in the country. The
Government initiated the National Mission for Financial Inclusion (NMFI), namely, Pradhan
Mantri Jan DhanYojana (PMJDY) in August, 2014 to provide universal banking services for
every unbanked household, based on the guiding principles of banking the unbanked,
securing the unsecured, funding the unfunded and serving unserved and underserved
areas.
   Table 14.12 shows RRBs dominate the PMJDY landscape with 61.35 lakh accounts,
forming ~25% of the state total.Public sector banks, despite having wider presence, show
much lower numbers (18.03 lakh), indicating either reporting differences or a shift of rural
customers toward RRBs. Private banks contribute just 1% of total PMJDY accounts,
showing minimal engagement in financial inclusion schemes.

   An important aspect of financial inclusion is enabling the flow of credit to small
businesses. In pursuance of the announcement in the Union Budget 2015-16, the Micro
Units Development finance Agency (MUDRA) was set-up and the Pradhan Mantri Mudra
Yojana (PMMY) launched on 8th April, 2015. For achieving sustained expansion in the flow
of credit to the non-corporate small business sector, loans up to Rs. 10 lakh without
collateral are extended to borrowers under PMMY. These loans are extended through
partner Member Lending Institutions (MLIs) – such as Scheduled Commercial Banks, Non-
Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) and Micro-Finance Institutions (MFIs). In turn,
MUDRA Ltd. offers refinance to MLIs for PMMY loans extended by them. Status of
beneficiaries under MUDRA in the State as on 30.06.2025 is given in Table-14.13.

    As a part of financial inclusion “ASSAM MICRO FINANCE INCENTIVES AND RELIEF
SCHEME (AMFIRS), 2021” was formulated with the objective to give incentive and relief
to the borrowers, who availed small loans from different Microfinance lending institutions
in the State of Assam.

The objectives of the scheme are as follows:

   a. Incentivizing borrowers for making regular repayments and maintaining good credit
      discipline.
   b. Providing relief to stressed borrowers to encourage and help them to regularise
      their repayments.
   c. Providing partial/ full relief from repaying loans to stressed, destitute borrowers
      with no capacity to repay.

   Accordingly, the mode of disbursement of benefit has been categorised as given below:

Category-1: Borrowers who have been repaying regularly with zero Days Past Due, will
be provided one-time incentive to the extent of their outstanding balance, subject to a cap
of Rs.25,000/-. This is proposed as an incentive to continue maintaining good credit
discipline.
Category-2: Borrowers whose payments are overdue by 1-89 days but not NPA will be
considered under this category. Government will pay the overdue amount to encourage
the borrowers to make timely installment payments so that their accounts remain standard
and credit culture is reinforced. To incentivize such credit discipline, the Government will
make onetime incentive payment of Rs.20,000/- or equal to the outstanding balance,
whichever is lower.




  238
                            Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



Category-3: Borrowers whose accounts have become NPA, as per Credit Bureau verified
data received from lenders will be eligible under this Category. State Government will
consider providing partial or full relief based on detailed evaluation. The borrowers under
this category will be further categorised into the following slabs based on the outstanding
principal amount as of 31.03.2021:
       a. Up to Rs.25,000
       b. Rs.25,001 to Rs.50,000
       c. Rs.50,001 to Rs.75,000
       d. Rs.75,001 to Rs.1,00,000
       e. Rs.75,001 to Rs.1,00,000
       f. Rs.1,00,001 to Rs.1,25,000
    The above amount is cumulative outstanding principal amount, which implies if any
borrower has more than one (1) NPA loan, but not exceeding three (3) NPA loans as on
31.03.2021, then in such cases cumulative of the NPA loans will be considered for deciding
the slab.

Mukhya Mantrir Eti Koli Duti paat
   The Scheme- Mukhya Mantrir Eti koli duti paat has been announced in the Budget
Speech, 2025-26 to recognise the contribution of tea garden workers in the growth of Tea
industry in the State and provide one-time financial assistance of Rs. 5000 to all tea garden
workers (both temporary and permanent) and employees, excluding tea garden
management. This initiative marks the 200th year celebration of Assam Tea. A Budget
provision of Rs. 34200.00 lakh had been made for the Financial Year 2025-26 for
implementation of the Scheme.
Assam Tea Industries Special Incentive Scheme (ATISIS), 2020

    The ATISIS Scheme was launched in the year 2020 to incentivize the tea
manufacturers on production of Orthodox and other specialty tea by providing subsidy to
the manufacturer on working capital loan, orthodox and specialty tea production and
purchasing of plant and machinery. This scheme will help in upliftment of the tea markets
in Assam. The scheme has four components:




                                                                                      239
                             Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




Component I: Interest Subvention on Working Capital Loan

   An interest subvention of 3% per annum, subject to a maximum limit of ₹20 lakh
per annum, is provided on working capital loans availed by eligible tea manufacturers.
Component II: Subsidy on Orthodox and Specialty Tea Production

    Industrial units manufacturing orthodox tea, green tea, white tea, oolong tea,
Singhpo tea, purple tea, yellow tea, or other specialty teas (excluding those produced
through the CTC (Crush, Tear, Curl) process) are eligible for a production subsidy.
Initially fixed at ₹7 per kg, the subsidy was later enhanced to ₹10 per kg for the duration
of the scheme. In view of the completion of 200 years of Assam Tea, the Government
further increased the production subsidy to ₹12 per kg for the financial year 2023–
24.
Component III: Subsidy for Plant and Machinery

   A capital subsidy of 25% of the cost of plant and machinery is provided to units
engaged in the manufacture of orthodox and other specialty teas.

Component IV: Agricultural Income Tax Holiday

   The scheme offers a six-year agricultural income tax holiday for eligible units,
applicable from financial year 2019–20 to 2024–25.

    The ATISIS Scheme has been extended up to the financial year 2027–28, reinforcing
the State Government’s commitment to promoting value-added tea production and
strengthening Assam’s position in the global specialty tea market.

   The State Government has announced that the ATISIS scheme will be extended for
another 5 years i.e. till the financial year 2027-28

Orunodoi Scheme:
   To ensure wholesome socio-economic development, the Government of Assam
launched the Orunodoi Scheme on 1 December 2020. The scheme aims to support
families who continue to face daily financial challenges by providing assistance for ensuring
healthy and nutritious meals. During the financial year 2020–21, beneficiaries with a
composite annual household income of less than ₹2 lakh received financial assistance of
₹830 per family per month, effective from November 2020. Subsequently, the monthly
assistance was enhanced to ₹1,000 per beneficiary from October 2021, expanding
coverage to around 19 lakh families. Further strengthening the scheme, an additional ₹250
per beneficiary was introduced as a power subsidy from October 2022, thereby increasing
the total monthly benefit to ₹1,250 per beneficiary.
Following the launch of the scheme, Orunodoi Month was observed in August 2022, during
which a door-to-door survey of existing beneficiaries was conducted. As a result,
approximately 2.2 lakh ineligible beneficiaries were excluded from the scheme, leading to
an estimated annual saving of ₹330 crore.
   During 2022–23, the Government of Assam launched Orunodoi 2.0 with an
expanded and more inclusive coverage. Under this phase, apart from Antyodaya women,
Transgenders, and Divyangjan of the State, beneficiaries of the Deen Dayal
Divyangjan Pension Scheme and the Indira Miri Universal Widow Pension Scheme
were also brought under its ambit. This integration resulted in the removal of nearly 1.2
lakh beneficiaries who were receiving benefits under multiple schemes, thereby
improving efficiency and avoiding duplication.




                                                                                        241
                             Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




   To fulfil its commitment towards the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) of
ending poverty, the Government undertook the inclusion of new beneficiaries under
Orunodoi 2.0, raising the total number of beneficiaries to 27 lakh.
Subsequently, Orunodoi 3.0 was launched on 19 September 2024. Under this phase,
a key precondition for eligibility is that the individual must be enrolled as a beneficiary
under the National Food Security Act (NFSA). For effective implementation, the
definitions of household, family, income criteria, and related parameters are aligned with
the prevailing NFSA guidelines.
   A notable feature of Orunodoi 3.0 is the provision for automatic Aadhaar seeding of
beneficiaries, which has proven to be an efficient mechanism for the direct transfer of
benefits to Antyodaya households. This measure is particularly effective in Assam, as
almost all NFSA beneficiaries are already Aadhaar-seeded, ensuring transparency,
accuracy, and timely disbursement of benefits.

NABARD INFRASTRUCTURE DEVELOPMENT ASSISTANCE (NIDA):
   RIDF is Government driven wherein limited resources are provided at concessional rate
of interest with shorter repayment period to State Governments. The limited flexibility of
terms and conditions and limited borrowing power of State Governments warranted
opening of additional opportunity to State Governments including the well managed State
Government entities to access the financial resources. Accordingly, a new window of
support, NABARD Infrastructure Development Assistance (NIDA) was designed to directly
fund the State Governments/State owned institutions/ Corporations on both on-budget as
well as off-budget for creation of rural infrastructure outside the ambit of RIDF borrowing.
AIFA (Assam Infrastructure Financing Authority)
        AIFA was formed in 2009 to take up major infrastructure projects not covered under
NLCPR, EAP, and State Plan, RIDF or any other schemes. The aim and objective of the
society is to take up projects of critical infrastructure for speedy overall economic and
social development of the state. To keep the momentum of infrastructure going, AIFA has
further taken up projects in diverse sector with tangible and quantifiable benefits in this
financial year also. The projects sanctioned and taken up under NABARD Infrastructure
Development Assistance (NIDA) in the financial year 2024-25 are as follows: -

NEDFi Micro Lending Scheme
   “NEDFi Micro Lending Scheme” was launched, by Hon’ble Chief Minister of Assam, on
9th August 2022, to provide financial assistance to the micro borrowers directly, through
Business Correspondents, at cheaper interest rate. As on March 31, 2025, an amount of
₹102.14 crore was extended to 9030 beneficiaries of the State of Assam under the
Scheme.


North East Venture Fund (NEVF)
   NEDFi, jointly with the Ministry of DoNER, had set up the North East Venture Fund
(NEVF) with a corpus of ₹100 crores. As on March 31, 2025, the Fund had provided, in-
principle, commitment of almost ₹73.46 crores into 46 startups in the State of Assam in
sectors such as Agri and agri-allied, Health care, Biotechnology, IT & ITES, Tourism, Food
Processing, Industrial products etc.

ASSAM FINANCIAL CORPORATION (AFC):
    Assam Financial Corporation (AFC) was established on 19th April, 1954 under State
Financial Corporation’s Act,1951 with a view to provide financial assistance to micro, small
and medium scale industries with the main objectives of accelerating the industrial growth
of the region , promotion of self-employment etc. AFC has active presence throughout the
state with 11 Branch Offices including one Microfinance Branch and the head office located
in Vittiya Bhaban, Md. Shah Road, Paltan Bazar, Guwahati-8.
   During FY 2024-25, the Corporation’s sanction and disbursement recorded a growth
rate of 1.27% and 68.4% respectively. The Corporation sanctioned loans amounting to
Rs. 2085.65 lakh in FY 2024-25 as against Rs. 2059.50 lakh in the previous financial year.

ASPIRATIONAL DISTRICTS OF ASSAM:
   The Aspirational District Program (ADP), launched in January 2018 by NITI Aayog, GoI,
represents a pioneering initiative to catalize comprehensive development in regions
grappling with various socio economic challnages identifing 115 districts nationwide for
targeted intervention, the program introduces an innovative element of competition. Each
month, districts engang in a dynamic process of assessment through delta ranking,
fostering a sense of competition and urgency for progress.
   ADP goes beyond its immidiate objectives, aliening with the broader agenda of
sustainable development. With 49 Key Performace Indicators (KPIs) spanning five crucial
themes- health and nutrition, education,agriculture and water resources,finacial inclusion
and skill development and basic infrasturure.
   Over the past five years, the seven aspirational districts of Assam, i.e. Baksa, Barpeta,
Darrang, Dhuburi, Goalpara, Hailakandi and Udalguri have been actively enganed in the
program under the nodal department of Transformation and Development.
   One way of accelerating progress in Aspirational Districts is to focus on a few select
indicators at one time and saturate them so that one can see quick impact. As part of this
initiative, NITI Aayog has conceptualized a 3-month campaign, the “Sampoornata
Abhiyan,” to carry out a sustained campaign to achieve saturation in 6 identified indicators
in ADP/ABP Districts and Blocks. The duration of the initiative was three months, from 1st
July 2024 to 30th September 2024. The following table shows the districts that achieved
100% saturation for each Key Performance Indicator (KPI):

CHAPTER-XV

                                 CO-OPERATION


      o-operation means the system of voluntarily associated working together in term           4
C     of equality to eliminate their economic exploitation. International Co-operative
      Alliance (ICA) has defined it co-operation as a non-profit system of production and
      trade based upon voluntary and mutual self-help and organised in the interest of
whole community. Now, Co-operative society is not synonymous with Co-operation. That
is, in present economic scenario co-operative societies are undividable part of the
economic system to overcome different micro needs of societies, especially in rural
economy. Co-operative revolution are spurting through the socialist ideologies “all for
each and each for all”. The Co-operative form of organisation is an indispensable
instrument of planned economic action in a democracy. A Co-operative is an autonomous
association of persons united voluntarily to meet their common economic, social and
cultural needs and aspirations through a jointly owned and democratically controlled
enterprise.


     Co-operatives play a very significant role in the socio-economic development of our
State especially the rural areas of Assam. All Co-operative Societies in Assam are
registered under the Assam Co-operative Societies Act, 1949, which has since been
repealed and replaced by the Assam Cooperative Society Act, 2007. These societies
function under the administrative control of the Co-operation Department.


     The Mandates of the Co-operation Department include registration, supervision,
assistance counselling audit of co-operative societies in the State. During the current year,
there are 13722 Nos. of different Co-operative Societies including (State Level) in the
State operating across almost all economic sectors viz. Agriculture, dairy, fishery,
pisciculture, primary housing, consumer, Processing and Marketing, banking, healthcare,
education and other agricultural and allied sectors. (List in Annexure–I).


    These societies have contributed significantly to the state economy by generating
employment opportunities, regulating market prices, and empowering women both
socially and economically. These 13722 nos. of Cooperative Societies include:
      1898 nos. of GPSS/LAMPS,
      2867 nos. of GPBMSS,
      01 State Level Apex Bank for short term Agricultural Cooperative Credit,
      01 State Agricultural and Rural Development bank (ASCARD Bank) for long and
       medium term agricultural credit
      01 State Level Housing Federation (HOUSEFED),
      01 State Level Fishery Co-operative Federation (FISHFED),
      01 State Level Co-operative Jute Mill (Assam Cooperative Jute Mill Ltd., Silghat),
      8 nos. of Urban Co-operative Banks and various types of other Co-operative
       Societies.

                                                                                      251
                                Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




PRIMARY AGRICULTURAL COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES
      The Gaon Panchayat Level Multipurpose Cooperative Societies (GPSS) and
large size multipurpose cooperative society in Assam are known as Primary Agricultural
Cooperative Societies (PACS). These societies have been playing vital role in ensuring
the flow of Cooperative agricultural credit to the farmer members.

      In addition to the provision of agricultural credit, PACS function as handling agents of
Public Distribution System (PDS) under poverty elevation scheme of Govt. of India and
the Mid- Day Meal Scheme. At present there are 1898 nos. of PACS operating in the State.

      PACS need to be reoriented to strengthen their role for dealing in fertilizer, pesticides,
farm mechanism, agricultural credit through KCC, supply of quality seeds and to provide
forward backward scheme for micro- finance. These societies can play an important role
as a financial institution for rural poor who are unable to access the benefit of institutional
finance.

GAON PANCHAYAT LEVEL WOMEN MULTIPURPOSE COOPERATIVE SOCIETY
      There are 2867 nos. of Gaon Panchayat Level Women Multipurpose Cooperative
Societies (GPBMSS) in the state for Socio- economic development of women of rural
areas, with a view to upgrade Self Help Groups (SHGs) under NRLM, 680 Village
Organisations were registered under the Assam Cooperative Societies Act.

      These societies are doing some activities like handloom, knitting, embroidery, pickle
making for economic upliftment of women members. Some of the societies are doing PDS
business as an agent of GPSS of their respective area of operation. The Government have
taken scheme in the name and style of “Samannita Mahila Samabai Sabalikaran” and
“Samabai Biponi” for the betterment of the society during the year 2017-18 and 2018-
19.

ASSAM STATE CO-OPERATIVE APEX BANK LTD.
      Assam has two tier short terms Agricultural Cooperative Credit Structure, the Assam
Cooperative Apex Bank Ltd. At the top and Primary Level Agricultural Credit
Cooperative Societies at the grass root level. GPSS and LAMPS were entrusted with the
responsibility to disburse agricultural credit to the farmer members. The Assam
Cooperative Apex Bank Ltd. is managed by an elected Board of Directors and a professional
Chief Executive. Presently, it has 68 branches and it adopted core banking solution
successfully. The bank has provided all types of advance facilities to the customer to access
advantage like others Nationalised Bank like ATM facilities to its customers for smooth
running of the banking business. The performances of the Assam State Cooperative Apex
Bank Ltd. for the last consecutive six years are given below.

ASSAM COOPERATIVE JUTE MILL LTD.

    Assam Cooperative Jute Mills Ltd. at Silghat (1959) in Nagaon District is one of the
most successful Cooperative Industries in Assam. This Industry is earning profit
continuously and has been awarded with ISO certificate. The society has taken initiative
to expand one unit of Assam Cooperative Jute Mills Ltd. at Bihdubi with Rs. 47 Crores from
NCDC in 2017-18. The Central Government had provided Rs. 240.60 lakhs as grant-in-
aid. The State Government had also written off accumulated tax liabilities of pre closure
period to the tune of Rs. 96.00 lakhs & Rs. 46.39 lakhs. Further, the State Govt. had
provided 50% power subsidy for 5 years from 01/01/1986 to 31/12/1990 amounting to
Rs. 48.12 lakhs for its rehabilitation. The Mill had liquidated most of the old liabilities and
also acquired some assets out of those funds, but could not put in sound financial footing
up to the year 1992-93 in spite of sufficient subsidies from the Govt. for its revitalization.

DAIRY COOPERATIVES

    There are 880 numbers of primary dairy cooperatives societies and three number of
regional level milk union namely 1) West Assam Milk Producers Ltd. (WAMUL), 2) East
Assam Milk Producers Cooperative Union (EAMUL), 3) Cachar and Karimganj District Milk
Producer Cooperative Union Ltd. (CAMUL). Though there is vast potential in the dairy
sector, the growth of the dairy cooperative societies are not satisfactory. A number of
primary cooperative societies like Sitajakhala Dugdha Samabai Samiti Ltd. (SJDUSS),
Kamdhenu Dairy Cooperative Society, Sundarpukhuri Dairy Cooperative Society etc. are
performing well. The management of WAMUL, EAMUL and CAMUL were handed over to
the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) New Delhi a years back with a view to
revive those weak organisation towards a successful dairy cooperatives in the line of AMUL
model. For the development of dairy cooperatives, government has been providing
financial assistance to these cooperative in a phase manner.

ASSAM STATE COOPERATIVE UNION (ASCU)

   The Assam State Cooperative Union (ASCU) is an apex level cooperative organisation
for promotion of cooperative education, training, publicity and propaganda activities in the
state of Assam. It was registered vide registration no. ASCU-29/2055 -56, dated
12/09/1955.

       The aims and objectives of ASCU:-

       1) To promote and develop cooperative movement in Assam
       2) To educate, train and guide people and to assist them in their efforts to build
          and expand the cooperative sector.
       3) To serve as an exponent of cooperative union.
       4) To propagate and publicize the cooperative principles and ideas in order to
          create public opinion in favour of the movement by holding seminars,
          conference etc.
       5) To arrange for inter- state study visit of successful cooperatives in other
          cooperatively developed states of India.

The Infrastructure Support under Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF)

  The State Cooperation Department has undertaken initiatives to strengthen rural
storage infrastructure through the construction of rural godowns in various Gaon
Panchayat Samabai Samity (GPSS), Large Area Multipurpose Cooperative
Societies (LAMPS) and other Cooperative societies with assistance under the NABARD
sponsored Rural Infrastructure Deveploment Fund (RIDF) scheme.

  The Govt. have released mobilization advance for an amount of Rs. 24.08 lakh for
construction of 105 nos. of rural godowns under RIDF in the year 2017-18 and released
amount of Rs. 195.87 lakh as state share for construction of 244 nos. rural godowns during
the year 2017-18. As on 1st December/ 2018 out of godowns, construction of 222 nos. of
godowns have been completed and the remaining are in progress.

CHAPTER-XVI

            PRICES & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM



                                                                                              4




T   he economic activities as well as the purchasing power of the people of a country are
    greatly influenced by the changes in commodity prices. Changes in prices of
    commodities and services affects the standard of living of the people. Therefore, it is
crucial to monitor the price behavior of an economy to regulate and frame economic
policies accordingly.
    Price Index acts as a barometer to study the price scenario of an economy. It is a
Statistical device that measures the relative change in price level with reference to
time/geographical location and other characteristics. Different indices helps the state
government to adopt policies or offer compensation to eliminate the effect of increasing
price levels.


PRICE SITUATION IN ASSAM
     The purchasing power of commodities is significantly influenced by the fluctuations in
their retail prices. An increase or decrease in retail prices directly affects consumers'
purchasing power, which in turn impacts their living conditions. Retail price is defined as
the amount paid by the consumer, inclusive of all taxes but excluding any discounts. To
monitor the variations in price levels, the Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Assam,
collects retail price data for 28 essential commodities from 27 urban and 26 rural centres
across the state on a weekly basis.



                                                                                    261
                            Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




PRICE INDICES
     Price Indices helps in assessing the inflationary or deflationary condition of the
economy. Both Wholesale Price Index (WPI) and Consumer Price Index (CPI) are measures
of inflation. While, Wholesale Price Index (WPI) considers the price volatility of the
Wholesale markets; the Consumer Price Index (CPI) on the other is based on the Prices of
the Consumer purchases from the retail trade market.

CONSUMER PRICE INDEX NUMBER FOR INDUSTRIAL WORKERS (CPI-IW)
   This Index is the oldest among the CPI indices as its dissemination started as early as
1946. Consumer Price Index Number for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW) measures a change
over time in the prices of a fixed basket of goods and services consumed by industrial
workers.
    CPI-IW is mainly used for the determination of Dearness Allowance (DA) and Variable
Dearness Allowance (VDA) which is paid to the public sector employees besides fixation and
revision of minimum wages in scheduled private sector employees respectively. It is also
used for measuring inflationary trends of the economy which is used for framing policy in
the country to compensate the general public for the adverse effect of price volatility. Since
its inception in 1946, the Labour Bureau, Ministry of Labour, Govt. of India has been
compiling CPI for Industrial Workers. The Price data for CPI-IW are collected from the
selected centres of each state. At present, there are six centres in Assam, viz; Kamrup,
Biswanath, Doomdooma (Tinsukia), Golaghat (Numaligarh), Sivasagar and Labac (Silchar).
The data collected from the six centres are sent to the Labour Bureau for CPI-IW compilation.
   The Labour Bureau Compiles the index of individual centres and releases it every month.
The index with the base year 2016 is timely recorded by DES and the state index is compiled
based on the six-centre index. The CPI for Industrial workers (CPI-IW) of the previous base
year, i.e. 2001=100 is compiled by the state based on linking factors as provided by the
Ministry of Labour and Employment. The following Table 16.4 shows CPI-IW (Base
2016=100) for 2024 and 2025.

PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM
    The Public Distribution System is a major instrument of the Government's food control
policies for providing food security in India through affordable food distribution and
emergency management system. It helps ensuring availability of food grains at affordable
prices thereby helping to eradicate poverty by serving poor who are nutritionally at risk.
Public Distribution System in India is perhaps the largest distribution system of its type in
the world. Public Distribution System is operated under the joint responsibility of the
Central and the State governments. The Central Government has taken the responsibility
for procurement, storage, transportation and bulk allocation of food grains etc. The
responsibility of distribution food articles to the consumers through the network of fair
price shop rests with the State governments. In Assam, the Food and Civil Supplies
Department looks after the allocation and distribution of food grains, identification of
families below poverty line, issue of ration cards and supervision and monitoring of stock
position and distribution of food articles etc. by the fair price shops. The department is
also entrusted with the responsibility of procurement of paddy and rice under ‘Minimum
Support Price’ scheme under the ‘The Food Management Policy’ of the Ministry of Food and
Public Distribution of Govt. of India to ensure remunerative price to the producers for their




  272
                          Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



agricultural produce and to provide the procured food grains to the consumers fairly at
reasonable and affordable price.

CHAPTER – XVII


                     LABOUR, EMPLOYMENT & WAGES



                                                                                                       4




L
      abour is one of the basic factors in the process of production. It necessitates a relationship
      between employees and employer which in other terms is called employment, where the
      labourers rent the services in exchange for wages from employers. The employers can be large
corporate houses, NGOs or other businesses, or the Government. With the passage of economic
development, more and more employment opportunities are created. In earlier days workers and
employees had not been much respected over the years. The employers were to some extent,
unscrupulous. But those days have gone and nowadays the welfare part of the employees has been
merged with the creation of employment opportunities. These days the relationship between
employers and employees has been enriched with the concept of value judgment, mutual respect,
and trust. On the other hand, the Government has also implemented some laws to protect the
employees from unscrupulous behaviours of the employer class. Economic growth always results in
the generation of employment opportunities which in turn results in poverty alleviation. In the
context of employment, there arise two aspects i.e. labour supply and Labour Force Participation
Rate (LFPR). LFPR refers to the proportion of a country’s working-age population meaning
the working or seeking work in the labour market at the prevailing wage rate. The working
age population refers to people aged 15 to 64 years. This indicator is split by age as well as sex
group. The Ministry of Labour and Employment of the Govt. of India has been emphasizing the
matter of improvement of life and dignity to protect the interest and welfare aspects and to ensure
social security of the labour force both in organized and unorganized sectors by enacting various
Labour Laws. These laws regulate the terms and conditions of service and employment of workers.
The State Governments are also competent to enact legislation, as labour is a subject in the
Concurrent List under the Constitution of India.


                                                                                             279
                                  Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




PERIODIC LABOUR FORCE SURVEY (PLFS)
    The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) is conducted regularly every year by the National
Statistical Office (NSO).It includes studies and analyses on various aspects such as Households
and Population, Labour Force, Workforce, Employment in the Informal Sector and conditions of
employment, Earnings from employment, Hours worked Unemployment, Technical education,
vocational/technical training, and number of years in formal education, Employ ment status among
social groups, Employment status among major religious groups, etc. The National Statistical
Office (NSO) conducted the last Periodic Labour Force Survey from July, 2023 to June
,2024. Out of the total number of 12,743 FSUs (6,975 villages and 5,768 UFS blocks) allotted for
the survey at the all-India level, the number of households surveyed was 1,01,920 (55796 in rural
areas and 46,124 in urban areas) and the number of persons surveyed was 4,18,159 (2,42,546 in
rural areas and 1,75,613 in urban areas). Estimates of the labour force indicators are based on the
usual status i.e. Primary Status and Subsidiary Status (ps+ss) approach and current weekly status
approach for classification of the population by activity statuses. The reference period for the usual
status i.e. ps+ss approach is for 1 year and for the current weekly status approach, it is for 1 week.
LABOUR FORCE PARTICIPATION RATE

    The labour force participation rate (LFPR) is defined as the percentage of persons
in the labour force among the persons in the population. The result of the PLFS Report
2023-24 reveals that the Labour Force Participation rate in respect of the age group 15
years and above according to the usual status approach in Assam is 68.50 percent in rural
areas, 55.80 percent in urban areas and 66.90 percent taking urban and rural areas as a
whole against the all-India rate of 60.10 percent. The 17.1 given below shows the Labour
Force Participation Rate for persons aged 15 years and above in the State.

FEMALE LABOUR FORCE PARTICIPATION IN ASSAM
     The labour force participation rate shows the gender gap present in employment opportunities.
It is calculated as the labour force divided by the total working-age population. Female LFPR not
only shows the extent of women’s willingness to work but also its increasing trend reflects the
elimination of social and institutional bottlenecks present concerning women’s participation in the
labour force, especially in a country like India. As shown in Figure 17.2 the female LFPR in
Assam(52.8% in rural ) was above the national rate(47.6%) in the year 2023-24 but the same were

                                                                                                        281
                                  Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




less than the all-India rate for the year 2021-22 and 2022-23. In the case of urban areas, it is higher
than the national level for the years 2022-23(29.0%) and 2023-24(31.5) but the same was a little
bit less than the all-India female force participation for the year 2021-22.

WORKER POPULATION RATIO (WPR)
    The worker population ratio is one of the major estimates of the employed persons. Worker
Population Ratio (WPR) is the percentage of persons employed among the persons in the
population. In other words, it is the ratio of total number of workers to the total population in a
country and expressed in terms of percentage. Worker population Ratio reflects the proportion of
the population engaged in the production process which also tells us about the employment situation
in an economy. Higher WPR usually reflects a higher proportion of the population engaged in
production activities and vice-versa. It is very important to have a high WPR which will boost the
economy in the process of growth and in further cases development. Table 17.3 shows the Worker
Population Ratio (WPR) for both Rural and Urban areas from 2021-22 to 2023-24.

    Of course, the decline in both male as well as female unemployment rate in Assam has been

rate in the state has been undergoing heavy fluctuations. However, fluctuations can be observed in
both male and female unemployment rates in the state, although the male unemployment rate
hasn’t witnessed peaks and troughs as sharp as the female unemployment rate.
   Most of these fluctuations can be attributed to the rural sector. Urban areas of Assam witnessed
a decreasing trend in female unemployment rate (18.3% to 12.7%) during the period from 2019-
20 to 2022-23 but it has fluctuated in nature. The same for rural males declined steadily from 6.8
% to 1.2 % from 2019-20 to 2022-23 as shown in Table 17.7. Similarly, the rate for urban males
has recorded a decreasing trend during the same period. In most of the years, the unemployment
rate in Assam has been hovering above the national rate. Most of it can be attributed to the high
female unemployment rate. However, the rates have come down below the national level (1.7% in
Assam against a national rate of 3.2%) in the year 2022-23. This is primarily due to a sharp fall in
both male (6.8% to 1.2%) and female (12.8 % to 2.7%) unemployment rates in the rural areas as
shown in Tables 17.7 and 17.9 as well.

receding trend has been observed in the case of rural female unemployment, from 12.8% to 2.7%

Employment Market Information

     Employment market information (EMI) is an important unit of Employment Exchanges that deals
with the collection of all sorts of labour market information. This unit is solely resp onsible for the
timely collection of Employment market information on manpower for both the public as well as
private sector. Data collected through the EMI programme is reported through an 'Establishment
Reporting system'. There are 31 districts of Employment Exchange in the state. The main objectives
of the EMI Programme are as follows:
    A) To provide information about the structure of Estimated Employment in the Public as well as
         Private Sector Establishment.

    B) Occupational-cum-educational profile of employees in the Public and Private Sector on
         regular intervals.

    C) Identify an occupation that has characteristics of a given industry.

    D) To assess Manpower shortage in the Organized Sector.

    E) Implementation of "Employment Exchanges (Compulsory Notification Vacancies) (CNV) Act,
         1959".

     EMI programme is not free from demerits. One of the major drawbacks of the EMI programme
is that it does not cover Employment in the unorganized sector. Apart from that self -employment,
part-time employment, defence employment, and employment in household works and non-
agricultural establishments employing less than 10 workers in the private sector do not fall under
the arena of such a programme.




   288
                              Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



EMPLOYMENT IN THE PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SECTOR IN ASSAM

    The total employment in the public and private sector establishments under the EMI programme
in 2023 was 11,54,000 nos. (In public sector 4,90,000 nos. and in private sector 6,64,000 nos.)
Whereas it was 11,22,200 nos. (In the public sector 4,87,1000 nos. and the private sector 6,35,100
nos.) in 2022 which shows a slight increase in the public sector & substantial increase in the Private
sector. The increase in employment in the public sector is attributed to the various employment -
generating schemes taken by the State Government.
    During 2023, female employment in the public sector was 93,900 nos. and in the Private sector
was 3,17,800 nos. Whereas the female employment in the public sector was 90,400 nos. and in the
Private sector was 3,10,000 nos. in 2022.The year 2023 which shows an increasing trend in female
employment compared to the year 2022.
    In parallel , the total employment in the public and private sector establishments under the EMI
programme in 2024 was 11,97,700 Nos.( in public sector 4,86,500 nos. and in private sector
7,11,200 nos) where it was 11,54,000 nos ( in public sector 4,90,000nos. and in private sector
6,64,000nos. ) in 2023, which shows an increasing trend in employment in the year 2024.
    During 2024 female employment in public sector was 96,700 nos. and private sector was
3,52,300 nos . Whereas in 2023, female employment in public sector was 93,900 nos and in the
private sector 3,17,000 nos which shows an increasing trend in female employment in the year
2024.

UN-EMPLOYMENT SCENARIO IN THE STATE

    The State has at present 52 nos. of Employment Exchanges comprising establishments of 47
general, 1(one) special, 1(one) for unskilled applicants and 3 (three) Employment Information and
Guidance Bureau. Moreover, there are 29 Employment Information and Assistance Bureaus to guide
unemployed youths to employment.

    The size of the registered job seekers is considerably high, which is a great challenge before the
growing economy of the State. From the records of the live register of Employment Exchanges, the
registered educated job seekers stood at 20,10,517 Nos. in 2023 as against 11,53,971 nos. in
2022.The registered educated job seekers stood at 21,16,561 in 2024. An upward trend in overall
size of the registered job seekers can be seen in each year.

DISTRIBUTION OF APPOINTMENTS IN ASSAM IN THE YEARS 2024

      In 2024, the Assam Government continued its massive recruitment drive, exceeding its promise
of 1 lakh jobs to over 1.25 Lakh plus total appointments by late 2024 highlighting a focus on
transparency and merit –based across various departments.
Major recruitments-
(i) By late September 2024, the state reached a total of 1,25,030 recruitment candidates, surpassing
the initial 1 lakh job promise.
(ii)On July, 2024: 41 appointment letters were distributed to the Education Department, pushing
the total count to 97,495 at that time.
(iii) On October 7, 2024: 385 candidates were given appointment letters at the GMCH Auditorium.
(iv) Focus area: Significant hiring occurred in the Public works, Public health Engineering and Rural
Development Department.

EMPLOYMENT GENERATION PROGRAMME
    Our economy is developing at a fast pace but still, a major part of the population who are
poverty-ridden, illiterate and lacking requisite skills need support to earn. Keeping this in mind the
Central Government and the State Government have initiated and implemented many programmes
for self and wage employment generation as well as for the creation of production of assets through
various organizations like the Panchayat and Rural Development Department, Directorate of
Industries and Commerce, Agriculture Department, etc. The achievements of some of these
programmes are briefly discussed as follows:




   294
                              Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



RURAL SELF EMPLOYMENT AND TRAINING INSTITUTES (RSETI)

    Rural Self Employment and Training Institutes (RESTI) provide skilling for self-employment.
RSETI program is a three-way partnership between the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD),
Government of India, the State Government and the Sponsoring Banks. MoRD provides grant –in –
aid to the sponsoring Banks for reimbursement of training costs of the rural poor and infrastructure
support for each RSETI building. Banks are mandated to open at least one RSETI in their lead District
to provide training to rural youth to take up self-employment entrepreneurship ventures. State
Government provides land for RSETI’s permanent infrastructure & reimbursement of training cost.
Target group RSETI programme is rural poor youth in the age group of 18-50years.

NAMO Drone Didi Scheme-

    NAMO Drone Didi Scheme was launched by Govt. of India on 30 th of November, 2023 under the
Ministry of Rural Development to promote women led development and empower rural women
through advanced technology in agriculture. This initiative aims to integrate women self-Help Group
(SHG) members into the modern agri-tech landscape by training and deploying them as Drone Didi
and drone Service Providers. The Lead Fertilizer Companies (LFCs) are the implementing agencies
of the scheme. In Assam, two LFCs namely IFFCO and Brahmaputra Valley Fertilizers Corporation
limited (BVFCL) have trained a total of 27 SHGs members from 10 Districts with the help of
Guwahati-based RPTO (Remote Pilot Training Organization). Now, the Didis are providing drone
services in farmlands on a rental basis. Total cumulative income Rs.7,90,616.

ASSAM STATE RURAL LIVELIHOODS MISSION SOCIETY (ASRLMS)


DEENDAYAL ANTYODAYA YOJANA–NATIONAL RURAL LIVELIHOOD MISSION (DAY-NRLM)

     ASRLMS has been implementing the DAY-NRLM in the State since the 11 th of November, 2011,
 with the objective of enhancing the social and economic empowerment of the rural poor in Assam.
 It has been designed as a multipronged approach to strengthen the livelihoods of the rural poor by
 promoting SHGs, providing skill development and placement for youth for wage-based occupations
 in different private/business organizations and imparting self-employment-oriented training.
 ASRLMS has undergone various phases of learning and has demonstrated significant successes till
 date in terms of the formation of quality Self Help Groups, their financial assistance and
 sustainability. Attention has been given to the assessment of the status of the SHG movement in

                                                                                              295
                                Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




 the state, bringing good SHGs into Village Organization and Cluster Level Federation fold, further
 support and facilitation required, on bank linkages to SHGs and how the programme is to be
 implemented in a mission mode in a phased manner. The Mission envisages empowering rural
 women Self Help Groups (SHGs) with capacity building, credit linkage and market support. All
 products produced by these SHGs are sold under the brand name ‘ASOMI’, where the word itself is
 an amalgamation of alphabets A-Atmo, SO- Sohayok, M- Mahila Gootor, I- Identity Porichoy. ASOMI
 also evokes the identity of Assamese people. Till March2025, the total SHGs under NRLM is about
 6623 and the cumulative progress in the state is 3,59,000.These SHGs are further organized to
 higher-level federations like Village Organizations (VO) and Cluster Level Federations (CLF) to
 provide a common platform for collective action for socio-economic development. Total of 19,563
 VO and 757 CLF have been promoted under ASRLM since its inception.

    The Mahatma Gandhi National Employment Guarantee Programme was introduced during the
11th five-year Plan to give wage employment opportunities (100 days work) to the rural poor during
the lean agricultural season when they require wage employment to boost their purchasing power
to supplement their income requirement for livelihood. The other objective of the Act is to create
durable community assets for the development of rural infrastructure for the upliftment of the quality

PRIME MINISTER EMPLOYMENT GENERATION PROGRAMME (PMEGP)
     Pradhan Mantri Employment Generation Program is a credit-linked subsidy scheme merging two
schemes Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Yojana and Rural Employment Generation Programme. The scheme
was launched back in 2008 by MSME to provide financial assistance to set up new enterprises. The
maximum admissible cost of the project/unit is 50 lakhs for the manufacturing sector and 20 lakhs
for the service sector. During the first five months of the financial year 2021-22, the approval of
projects under the PMEGP increased to 59.61%.The KVIC is the nodal agency for implementing the
PMEGP scheme at the national level and the State level the scheme is implemented by the state
KVIC Directorate, State KVIB and the District Industries and Commerce Centers and Banks. The
Government subsidy under the scheme is being routed through the KVIC to the identified Banks.
Units in Urban areas are eligible for subsidy of 25%, while units in rural area can receive a subsidy
of 35% of the project.

Small Scale Industries/Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise (MSME)
    The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector has emerged as a highly vibrant and
dynamic sector of the Indian economy over the last five decades. It contributes significantly to the
economic and social development of the country by fostering entrepreneurship and generating the
largest employment opportunities at comparatively lower capital cost, next only to agriculture. The
small-scale industries sectors have a major contribution towards creating employment in the State.
Presently the small-scale industries have been subdivided into Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise
under the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act 2006. A Number of
statutory and non-statutory bodies work under the aegis of the Ministry of MSME which include the
Khadi Village Industries Commission (KVIC), the Coir Board of India and the National Small
Industries Corporation (NSIC). Government of India Scheme envisages financial assistance to State
Governments for setting up new and modernizes existing Mini Technology Centres.

    Up to the year 2024-25, there were total 10, 21,226Nos.,out of which 10,14,028 of Micro, 517

FACTORY EMPLOYMENT

    Manufacturing generates more economic activities than other sector. The establishment of the
factory is more important in the state for speedy development in the production and employment
perspective. As reported by the Chief Inspector of Factories till 2024-25 there were 8,858 Nos. of
factories in the state with 3,12,982 Nos. of employment compared to 8,620 Nos. of factories and
3,43,824 Nos. of employment in the year 2023-24 showing a 2.69 % increase in the number of
factories and 9.85% decrease in the context of employment.
HANDLOOM & TEXTILE INDUSTRY AND EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY
    Handloom & Textile Industry plays an important role in the socio-economic life of the people of
Assam particularly in rural areas. It is one of the major ways of earning livelihood next to agriculture
of the people of Assam. As such the Govt. of Assam is paying more importance for the upliftment of
weavers and other workers by launching various schemes relating to the handloom & textile industry.
Handloom & Textile Industry also plays a significant role in the employment generation of the state

SERICULTURE AND EMPLOYMENT GENERATION
    The Sericulture industry of Assam has evolved a unique world identity of the state. It includes
four endemic silk-producing insects viz. Eri, Muga, Mulberry and Tasar. Although sericulture activities
are commonly practised in some other states of the N. E. Region, Assam ranked highest among all
in terms of production of different varieties of silk. Assam has tremendous potential of producing
these silkworms whereas the state has already occupied the lion’s share i.e. 90% of total Muga silk
and 65% of Eri Silk produced in the country and ranks 3rd in overall silk production. The following
Table-17.21 shows the nos. of villages and families engaged in the sericulture activities in Ass am.

CHAPTER–XVIII

                PANCHAYAT & RURAL DEVELOPMENT


Panchayat and Rural Development Department

    Panchayat & Rural Development (P&RD) Department is responsible for
allevation of rural poverty, enhancement of rural livelihood by creation of self-
employment to the people living below the poverty line through implementation
of various schemes and programmes and to to strengthen the Panchayati Raj
Institution (PRIs). The Department is concerned with empowering the PRIs to
enable them to increase the capacity of the rural poor through self-employment
generation programs and by developing critical infrastructure in the rural areas.
With this mandate, the P&RD department has been developing different schemes
for development of rural infrastructure and upliftment of the quality of life of rural
people. The schemes implemented by the department are broadly classifies into
three categories.

  i.   Self-Employment
 ii.   Wage Employment
iii.   Welfare schemes for the Disabled, Widows & other down trodden people
       living below poverty line.

SCHEMES IMPLEMENTED BY THE PANCHAYAT & RURAL DEVELOPMENT
DEPARTMENT:

1. MGNREGA: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act.

2. PMAY-G: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana- Gramin.

3. NSAP: National Social Assistance Programme.

4. Central Finance Commission Grant.

5. State Finance Commission Grant.

6. MAS: Mission Amrit Sarovar.

MAHATMA GANDHI NATIONAL RURAL EMPLOYMENT GURANTEE ACT (MGNREGA)

       MGNREGA was launched in 2005 and introduced in Assam during the year 2006,
and has been implemented for more than a decade for overall rural development by
creating wage employment avenues and livelihood through asset creation by natural
resources management and infrastructure development. Also, various strategies are being
developed to create new avenues for the socio-economic upliftment of rural livelihoods by
covering the vulnerable section of the society.

Govt. of Assam has also taken following new initiatives under MGNREGA:

Special emphasis on Tea garden area

    Tea Garden workers of Assam are one of the biggest contributors to the organized work
force. Only about 50% percent of the total population under Tea Garden Area is employed
in the tea gardens as permanent and casual labours and the remaining working age
population either migrates out or engages in manual work away from the gardens,
therefore the living standard of the tea garden labourers is very low. During the period
from December to February, the activities in Tea industry reduce, thereby reducing
generation of employment by the industry.

   As part of new initiative under MGNREGA, the State Govt. has decided to provide 100
days of work to Tea Garden workers under MGNREGA during the lean season.

PRADHAN MANTRI AWAAS YOJANA GRAMIN (PMAY-G)

   The Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana Gramin (PMAY-G) is a flagship scheme of the
Government of India aimed at providing affordable housing to the rural population. The
scheme aims to provide pucca houses with basic amenities to all eligible houseless
households and households living in kutcha and dilapidated houses in rural areas.

   Since the program's inception and in alignment with the program's objective, i.e.
‘Housing for All’, Assam has received a target of 29,87,868 from the Ministry of Rural
Development, Govt. of India. From the target, 29,06,826 PMAY-G houses were sanctioned
under SECC and Awaas+ in Assam and 20,89,255 houses were completed till January
2026.

    The PMAY-G scheme coincides with the Agenda of Sustainable Development's first goal,
‘no poverty by 2030’. Sustainable Development Goal 1 or SDG 1 aims to eradicate extreme
poverty and reduce inequalities.

   Under PMAY-G, eligible beneficiaries receive financial assistance of Rs 1,30,000 from
the government to construct their homes. The scheme also emphasizes the use of
environmentally sustainable construction practices and promotes the adoption of clean
energy technologies.

     By addressing the housing needs of the rural poor, PMAY-G contributes to SDG Goal
by lifting people out of extreme poverty, reducing inequalities, and improving living
conditions. It recognizes the importance of adequate housing as a fundamental human
right and a key driver for overall development and social progress.

NATIONAL SOCIAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAMME (NSAP)

   It is a centrally sponsored programme to promote social security through financial
support to families living below the poverty line. Under NSAP, there are four schemes
being implemented in the state namely- i) Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension
Scheme (IGNOAPS), ii) Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS), iii)
Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) and iv) National Family
Benefit Scheme (NFBS).


                                                                                  305
                             Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




     The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) in Assam during FY 2024–25
recorded significant outreach across districts under its three major pension schemes. The
Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) supported 6,77,720
beneficiaries, while the Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) covered
1,11,599 beneficiaries, and the Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS)
assisted 31,777 beneficiaries. Districts such as Nagaon (41,003 old age pensioners, 6,449
widows, 2,181 disabled), Kamrup (39,862 old age, 5,252 widows, 921 disabled), and Dhubri
(35,644 old age, 7,098 widows, 2,118 disabled) reported the highest coverage, reflecting
concentrated demand and effective implementation. Smaller districts like Majuli and Dima
Hasao recorded comparatively lower figures, indicating demographic and geographic
variations in beneficiary distribution.

     Financial expenditure under NSAP in Assam for FY 2024–25 amounted to ₹25,991.98
lakh for IGNOAPS, ₹16,810.18 lakh for IGNWPS, and ₹1,151.35 lakh for IGNDPS. The
highest spending was observed in Nagaon (₹2,056.46 lakh for old age pensions, ₹944.16
lakh for widow pensions, ₹79.63 lakh for disability pensions) and Kamrup (₹2,244.64 lakh
for old age pensions, ₹781.37 lakh for widow pensions, ₹29.72 lakh for disability pensions),
reflecting their large beneficiary base. Districts such as Dhubri, Cachar, and Goalpara also
reported substantial allocations, while smaller districts like Majuli (₹326.71 lakh old age,
₹83.70 lakh widow, ₹7.08 lakh disability) and Dima Hasao (₹119.74 lakh old age, ₹85.72
lakh widow, ₹3.49 lakh disability) recorded relatively modest expenditures. This distribution
highlights both demographic concentration and fiscal prioritization across Assam.

STATE SPONSORED SOCIAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAMME:

   The Swahid Kushal Konwar Sarbajanin Briddha Pension Achoni, Assam’s universal old-
age pension scheme, achieved extensive coverage during FY 2024–25, benefiting
1,049,348 elderly citizens with a total expenditure of ₹33,475.17 lakh. Districts such as
Nagaon (65,340 beneficiaries, ₹2,313.18 lakh), Lakhimpur (54,797 beneficiaries,
₹1,556.18 lakh), and Morigaon (51,622 beneficiaries, ₹1,588.03 lakh) recorded the
highest figures, reflecting strong implementation. In contrast, smaller districts like South
Salmara-Mancachar (2,391 beneficiaries, ₹111.14 lakh) and Dima Hasao (4,714
beneficiaries, ₹135.35 lakh) reported lower coverage, consistent with their population size.
Overall, the scheme demonstrates Assam’s commitment to universal social security, with
equitable financial distribution aligned to demographic needs.

MISSION AMRIT SAROVAR: ASSAM MODEL

    The objective of construction/development of Mission Amrit Sarovar is to ensure ground
water recharge and availability of water for irrigation purpose for the farmers. It will also
act as an income generating asset through pisciculture, horticulture and commercial
plantation. It has been targeted to complete atleast 75 nos of Amrit Sarovars in every
district of Assam.

    In the Assam model, the Amrit Sarovar is being constructed on at least 1 hectare
pondage area with a water holding capacity of at least 10,000 cubic metres. The Assam
model of Amrit Sarovar is conceptualized with minimum 1 Hectare of pondage area, 3 layers
of commercial plantation, chain link fencing, flag hoisting platform, working shed for user
groups and solar lighting. Mission Amrit Sarovar was formally launched by the Hon'ble Prime
Minister on National Panchayat Day on 24th April, 2022. The foundation stone for the Amrit
Sarovar in Assam will be laid by the Hon'ble Prime Minister on 28th April, 2022.

    The main objective of the Mission Ammit Sarovar is water conservation through
excavation of Amrit Sarovar at the rate of 75 nos per district. Amrit Sarovar (Assam Model)
will not only ensure availability of water to the residents of the villages for agriculture
activities, but will also act as an income generating assets for user groups through
pisciculture & commercial plantation.

   As per Govt. of India (MoRD) target of Amrit Sarovar in Assam is 2625. Assam has
achieved total excavation of 2966(112.99%) as per BISAG-N. Out of which 2787 has been
executed by P&RD and 178 by other departments (soil conservation etc.).

     Amrit Sarovar in Assam is done on convergence mode with Fisheries Department and
Chief Minister Samagra Gramya Unnayan Yojana (CMSGUY) by Panchayat and Rural
Development Department, Assam. Approval received from CMSGUY for excavation of
Sarovars is Rs 607.46 Cr. Total Estimated cost under CMSGUY is Rs. 356.46 Cr and total
fund received from CMSGUY is Rs. 356.46 Cr in three tranches - Rs. 182.00 Cr in the 1st
Tranche and Rs. 125.00 Cr in the 2nd tranche and Rs. 49.46 Cr in 3rd tranche. Total fund
utilised by districts as on date 19-01-2026 is Rs. 290.8 Cr (81.57%).

    In order to ensure sustainability, most of the completed Amrit Sarovars situated in the
government land have been handed over to Cluster Level Federations (CLF) under ASRLM
which are being treated as user group which will lead to sustainable livelihood generation
for rural women and lead to their empowerment. According to data received from the
districts, out of a total of 2,120 Amrit Sarovars situated on government land, 1,426 have
been handed over to the CLFs. However, of these, 595 Sarovars are reported to have
various issues. In addition, 619 Sarovars have been handed over to village committees.
The handover process for the remaining 75 Sarovars is still pending. Discrepancies were
identified between the Amrit Sarovar survey reports submitted by ASRLM and the

                                                                                      307
                              Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




Commissionerate of P&RD. Consequently, instructions were issued for accurate verification.

    As per the instructions received from Hon’ble Chief Minister of Assam via letter no
CMO.1/2024/4785 Dated 13/08/2024 it was mentioned in Office Memorandum no.
E404491/701011/2024, that in 863 nos of Amrit Sarovar situated in Govt. Land which could
not be taken over by Cluster Level Federations (CLFs), it has been instructed that the Amrit
Sarovars are to to be handed over to the appropriate authority/ village committee with prior
approval of District Level Committee chaired by the Guardian Minister. If in some cases the
appropriate authority finds it difficult to determine the genuine allottees, District
Commissioner will decide it through transparent auction process in a free and fair manner.

FARM LIVELIHOODS

   ASRLM recognises the importance of sustainable livelihoods for the enhancement of
the income of SHG members' households. Under Farm Livelihoods, interventions like
adoption of Agro-ecological Practices by the members, capacity building on livestock
production and management, value chain development projects, organic farming, etc.
have been undertaken. Agro-ecological practices are promoted to improve soil health,
conserve water, reduce reliance on synthetic inputs, and enhance biodiversity. These
practices include techniques like crop rotation, intercropping, composting, and integrated
pest management. ASRLM utilises a community-based approach, empowering women and
other marginalised groups to adopt agro-ecological practices. Community Resource
Persons (CRPs) are trained to provide support and guidance to farmers in adopting these
practices.

    ASRLM also focuses on livestock interventions as a key strategy to improve rural
livelihoods. ASRLM aims to enhance income and employment opportunities for the rural
population by promoting livestock rearing, particularly among landless labourers and
small/marginal farmers. ASRLM provides training on improved livestock management
techniques, including feeding, breeding, and disease control.

    Additionally, ASRLM has taken the promotion of AgriNutri gardens as a key component
of its efforts to improve food and nutritional security among rural communities. These
gardens are designed to enhance access to nutritious food through the cultivation of
vegetables and fruits, contributing to both household income and dietary diversity.

   The three major initiatives, i.e. Agro-ecological Practices and Livestock intervention,
had been started in the FY 2019-20, and promotion of Agri-Nutri Garden had been started
from FY 2020-21. Year-wise progress (addition of members) has been given below:

Apart from the above, the following are some of the key interventions undertaken under
Farm Livelihoods-

I) Promotion of Producer Groups (PGs):

    A Producer Group is a primary collective of SHG members, promoted under NRLM,
where all members are involved in similar production-based livelihood activities. The PG
enables them to: Improve production, Access inputs and services, Aggregate and market
their produce, Enhance bargaining power and income. ASRLM has promoted and supported
6,848 Producer Groups under Value Chain Interventions across the state, with 4,55,927
Mahila Kisans (women farmers) associated with these groups. The major commodities
produced by the Producer Groups include Paddy, Backyard Poultry, Piggery, Goatery,
Mustard, Maize, Horticultural crops, Seasonal Vegetables, Honey, Spices, Assam lemon,
Mushroom, and Dairy products. Additionally, under NRLM, Rs. 73.875 Crores as Working
Capital and infrastructure funds have been released to the 3896 nosof Producer Groups
during the financial years 2021-2022 to 2024-2025.

II) Promotion of Farmer Producers Company:

    A Farmer Producer Company (FPC) is a legal entity registered under the Companies
Act, formed and owned by a collective of farmers or producers—primarily Self-Help Group
(SHG) members—to enhance their income through collective production, aggregation,
value addition, and improved market access.

   In FY 2021–22, with technical support from the Foundation for Development of Rural
Value Chains (FDRVC), ASRLM established the Xotphul Mahila Kisan Farmers Producers
Company in Tinsukia district, Assam. This initiative aims to develop value chains for ginger
and speciality rice, with a goal of covering 10,000 women farmers across three blocks.
Currently, 4,200 Shareholders have been onboarded, and the business of Speciality rice
and ginger has started. The total turnover of Xotphul Mahila Kisan Farmers Producers
Company is Rs. 53.2 Lakhs so far.

    During the financial year 2023–24, ASRLM, functioning as a Cluster-Based Business
Organization (CBBO), has successfully registered 59 all-women Farmer Producer
Companies across 54 blocks from 19 districts under the 10K FPO Scheme of the Ministry
of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India. These FPCs collectively have a




  312
                           Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



shareholder base of 40,440 Mahila Kisans. All 59 FPCs have commenced both input and
output business operations, with 47 FPCs obtaining Seed Licenses from the Department of
Agriculture. Additionally, all 59 FPCs have collectively received a Matching Equity Grant
amounting to ₹2.68 crores, and 49 FPCs have recorded a total turnover of Rs. 84.81Lakhs-
till date.

   Apart from this, ASRLM has also promoted an additional 20 all-women Farmer Producer
Companies in four districts of Assam, supported through HDFC Parivartan (HDFC Bank's
CSR initiative) in partnership with Sesta Development Services (SDS), as part of its
convergence efforts.

III) Integrated Farming Cluster (IFC):

    An Integrated Farming Cluster (IFC) is a cluster-based approach under NRLM that
brings together 250–300 SHG households from 2–3 nearby villages to promote diversified
and sustainable livelihoods, covering more than 1.05 Lakhs Households. Each household
adopts 3–4 high-potential farm and non-farm activities with a focus on improving
productivity, enabling value addition, and strengthening market linkages, aiming to
enhance household income through integrated and collective efforts.

    ASRLM is implementing a total of 350 Integrated Farming Clusters (IFC) across 34
districts, covering a total of 105,400 SHG households. Further, under the IFC-NRETP
project, a total 20 nos. of community-owned Livelihood Service Centre (LSCs)-Custom
Hiring Centres have also been established.

IV) Organic Farming:

    Organic farming, promoted under NRLM, is a sustainable practice that avoids synthetic
fertilizers and pesticides. It is encouraged to ensure safe food, reduce input costs, and
enhance the livelihoods of SHG members. Certification is done through PGS-India under
the Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare. Under NRETP Organic Village Clusters, more
than 20,000 SHG members have been federated under 696 Local Groups, which have
already received Organic Certification under the Participatory Guarantee System (PGS).
The NRLM Organic Project Phase-I (FY 2021-22), 20 blocks have been covered and in 40
clusters with 359 local groups formed, 10,784 Mahila Kisans have been covered. All 359
local groups have received PGS-India Organic certification and the first scope certificate.
In the phase II (FY 2023-24), the project covers 100 blocks and 200 clusters, with 1328
local groups formed, benefiting 50,682 Mahila Kisans. In the extended phase III (FY 2024-
25), the project covers 67 blocks and 134 clusters, with 896 local groups formed,
benefiting 33,545 MahilaKisans.

   ASRLM always envisages convergence with various line departments and other
organizations, institutes, etc., for the benefit of the SHG members. A summary of
convergence under the Farm Livelihoods sector has been given below:

NAMO Drone Didi scheme:

    NAMO Drone Didi Scheme was launched by Govt. of India on 30th of November 2023,
under the Ministry of Rural Development, to promote women-led development and
empower rural women through advanced technology in agriculture. This initiative aims to
integrate women Self-Help Group (SHG) members into the modern agri-tech landscape by
training and deploying them as Drone Didi and Drone Service Providers. The Lead Fertilizer

                                                                                    313
                             Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




Companies (LFCs) are the implementing agencies of the scheme. In Assam, two LFCs,
namely IFFCO and Brahmaputra Valley Fertilizers Corporation Limited (BVFCL), have
trained a total of 27 SHG members from 10 districts with the help of Guwahati-based RPTO
(Remote Pilot Training Organization), i.e., AMTRON, to obtain a DGCA license to fly and
use a drone as per the Drone Act 2021. Now, the Didis are providing drone services
(spraying fertilizers and pesticides) in the farmlands on a rental basis. Total cumulative
income: Rs. 7,90,616.

A-HELP (Accredited Agent for Health and Extension of Livestock Production):

   The A-HELP program is a collaborative initiative of the Department of Animal
Husbandry & Dairying (DAHD), Government of India, and the National Rural Livelihoods
Mission (NRLM) under the Ministry of Rural Development. It aims to strengthen veterinary
service delivery through trained SHG women at the village level. These women, known as
A-HELP workers, act as a crucial link between farmers and veterinary services. The Pashu
Sakhis promoted under ASRLM are engaged by the Department of Animal Husbandry and
Dairying for implementing various government schemes related to animal health,
breeding, and livestock development. As on March 2025, a total of 150 Pashu Sakhis from
12 Districts are engaged as trained A-Help Workers.

Amrit Sarovar:

    The Amrit Sarovar initiative, launched in April 2022 under the Ministry of Rural
Development, aims to rejuvenate 75 water bodies per district to promote water
conservation and sustainability through community participation. In Assam, Amrit
Sarovars located on government land are being handed over to Cluster Level Federations
(CLFs) under ASRLM for livelihood promotion. ASRLM has undertaken fishery-based
interventions in collaboration with CLFs to enhance rural incomes.

   So far, a total of 836 Amrit Sarovars have been successfully taken over by CLFs, out
of which 395 are currently utilized for fishery activities. Capacity building has been
conducted for 17,462 SHG members on sustainable aquaculture. Further, 256 Sarovars
have been harvested, generating an income of ₹13.85 lakh.

(B)Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana,(DDU-GKY)

    Deen Dayal Upadhaya Grameen Kaushal Yojana (DDU-GKY) aims to skill the rural poor
youth and provide them with jobs having regular monthly wages or above the minimum
wages. It is an initiative of the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India that
seeks to promote rural livelihoods and a part of the National Rural Livelihood Mission
(NRLM). DDU-GKY follows a 3-tier implementation model. The DDU-GKY National Unit at
MoRD functions as the policy-making, technical support and facilitation agency. The DDU-
GKY State Missions provide implementation support and the Project Implementing
Agencies implement the programme through skilling and placement projects. The course
curriculum and duration of the courses/trades is developed by the respective Sector Skill
Councils (SSCs) and the duration of the courses ranges from 3 months to 12 months. The
target age group is 18-35 years and the minimum educational qualification required is
Class V passed. The DDU-GKY programme started in the year 2015-16 in Assam. The
scheme is funded in the ratio 90:10 from Center and States respectively.

(C) Rural Self-employment training Institutes (RSETIs)

    Rural Self Employment and Training Institutes (RSETI) provide skilling for self-
employment. RSETI program is a three-way partnership between the Ministry of Rural
Development (MoRD), Govt of India, the State Government and the Sponsoring Banks.
MoRD provides grant-in-aid to the sponsoring Banks for reimbursement of training costs
of the rural poor and infrastructure support for each RSETI building. Banks are mandated
to open at least one RSETI in their lead District to provide training to rural youth to take
up self-employment entrepreneurship ventures. State Government provides land for
RSETI’s permanent infrastructure & reimbursement of training cost. Target group of RSETI
programme is rural poor youth in the age group of 18-50 years.
