CAPACITY BUILDING AND TRAINING FOR PRI’S, OFFICIALS AND OTHERS:

    The State Institute of Panchayat and Rural Development was established as one of the
core distinguished institution of Assam with the objective of becoming a premier training
institute in the field of conducting training programmes and rural development. The
Institute was registered under Societies Registration Act 1860 during the month of April,
1998 and thereafter, administrative and financial autonomy was conferred by the
Government. The Institute organizes various training programmes under the aegis of the
Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Ministry of Rural Development and Government of Assam for
the elected representatives of three tier Panchayati Raj Institutions, different courses for
officials of Rural Development, Panchayati Raj, front line workers of Line Department,
representatives of CBOs, NGOs, SHGs and rural people through its vast network of 2 (Two)
Head Quarter campuses at Guwahati, 1(One) no. State Panchayat Resource Centre, 12
(Twelve) nos. of Extension Training Centres and 11(Eleven) nos. of District Panchayat
Resource Centres located in different parts of Assam wherein SIPRD do not have any
Extension Training Centres.

    The mission of the State Institute of Panchayat and Rural Development is to focus on
the qualitative development in the ongoing rural development programmes and sensitize
the elected representatives of Panchayati Raj Institutions to be proactive through capacity
building activities. Capacity building is considered to be the fundamental part in the

                                                                                       315
                              Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




development efforts through which the delivery system can be made more effective. The
community and rural development plays an important role in the process of accelerating
the socio-economic development of rural areas with a view to increasing the income level
and quality of life of the rural people.

    As envisaged by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Government of India, the SIPRD,
Assam has given special thrust on localizing Sustainable Development Goals through
capacity building and training. The institute has been regularly organizing training
programmes on localizing SDGs in a decentralized manner on the 9 (nine) thematic areas
that have been identified by the Ministry. The institute has been organizing the training
programmes for the elected representatives of PRIs, officials, SHG members jointly on
localizing SDGs in a saturation mode. In each theme, the institute targeted to cover 5000
members of Gaon Panchayats in every year. During the year 2024-25, there were no
elected bodies in three tiers Panchayati Raj Institutions. So the Institute could not organize
any training for the Elected Representatives of PRI’s during the period. Focus has been
given on synchronizing GPDP with SDGs. GPDP is the entry point in the villages for
localising different thematic areas of SDGs. SIPRD has already been working in the field
to create the base for meaningful GPDP in the last couple of years and from this localising
SDGs will take off. The institute has already deputed the Faculties of SIPRD and its District
Centres to adopt at least five GPs so that they can provide the handhold support to the
GPs for attainment of SDGs in two to three identified themes in a phase manner. The
SIPRD, Assam since last couple of years has been organizing training on the following
Sustainable Development Goals:

        Theme 1: Poverty Free and Enhanced Livelihoods Village.

        Theme 2: Healthy Village.

        Theme 3: Child-Friendly Village.

        Theme 4: Water Sufficient Village.

        Theme 5: Clean and Green Village.

        Theme 6: Village with Self-sufficient Infrastructure

        Theme 7: Socially Just & Socially Secured Village

        Theme 8: Village with Good Governance.

        Theme 9: Women Friendly Village.

    The SIPRD has already signed MoU with Central University, Tezpur, Central Institute
of Technology, Kokrajhar. The institute has also tie up with Assam Agriculture University
and its colleges, KVKs, TISS, Guwahati. Different colleges have been coming up to sign
MoU with the SIPRD for various training programmes of their students.

    UNICEF, Assam field office has already set up a Resource Centre in the SIPRD for
development of women and children in the villages. The UNICEF has also been coordinating
with the institute for development of women and child friendly GPs in the state. The
Institute has taken up a planned approach towards building the capacity of the elected
representatives of panchayats in the light of devolution of functions, functionaries and
funds to Panchayati Raj Institutions in the State.

decentralization of the governance and for socio-economic development of the rural areas.
The Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Ministry of Rural Development, other Ministries and State

CHAPTER-XIX

                                    SOCIAL SECTOR


S
         ocial Sector Development is one of the most rewarding investments available to
         promote national development. With this view, the State Government has been
         making all possible efforts to develop social sector in the state, according to desired
priorities. Development of social activities like education, health, family welfare, safe
drinking water, sanitation, welfare programme for women, children, SC & ST sub sectors,
development of marginalized groups and backward regions etc. have assumed fairly
important. The Government is committed towards overall development of all sections of
society.
EDUCATION:


      Education is one of the key inputs for balanced social & economic development.
Education empowers people with skills & knowledge which ultimately help to boost
economic growth. A number of schemes have been initiated by the Government for
encouraging development of education among various sections of the population in the
State. Development in these sectors can build up strong edifice of a stimulating economy
in terms of rising income and employment opportunities, productivity, technology
advancement and finally enhanced quality of life in the State. Education may be both
formal and informal. Formal education consists of Pre-school, Primary, Upper Primary,
Secondary to Senior Secondary, Technical or non-technical or may be Vocational in form.
PRIMARY & UPPER PRIMARY EDUCATION:
      In Assam, the number of Government/Provincialized Schools/Institutes under
department of Elementary in Lower Primary schools is 33875 of which 32841 are in rural
areas and 1034 are in urban areas. Likewise, the total number of Upper Primary schools
is 6160 of which 5855 are in rural areas and 305 are in urban areas as per UDISE 2023-
24.
DROP-OUT RATE:


      As per, DISE 2023-24, the average annual Drop-out Rate in Lower Primary in the State
during 2023-24 is 6.90 against 8.49 in 2022-23, while this rate was 6.02 percent in 2021-
22. Likewise in the Upper Primary level, the drop-out rate is 9.27 in 2023-24 and it was
10.33 in 2022-23. The drop-out rate, registered highest 11.55 percent in West Karbi-
Anglong followed by 11.20 in South Salmara in the Lower Primary level while lowest is
2.78 in Jorhat. Similarly, in the upper Primary Level, this rate is highest 16.85 in Dhubri
followed by 16.36 in Nagaon and the lowest 0.36 in Dhemaji. During the period 2023-24.
The Transition Rate from primary to upper primary in the state is 84.1.

      The Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) or Student-Teacher Ratio is the number of students who
attend a school or university divided by the number of teachers in the institutions. The
Pupil-Teacher Ratio in the Lower Primary level of the State during the year 2024-25 has
been 20 as it was 21 during 2023-24. Similarly, in the Upper Primary level the PTR during

GROSS ENROLMENT RATIO (GER):
   The National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020) identified universal education as a key
priority, with several initiatives aimed at transforming the education sector and
empowering the nation’s youth. At the heart of the NEP vision to achieve 100% Gross
Enrolment Ratio (GER) till secondary level by 2030, it is necessary to measure GER.Gross
Enrolment Ratio or Gross Enrolment Index is a statistical measure used in the educational
sector and by the UN in its Education Index to determine the number of students enrolled
in school at several grade levels (like elementary, Secondary school and Senior Secondary
school).

Samagra Shikha:
   Under Samagra Shikha Abhiyan the different activities undertaken by the
government for elementary and secondary level are as follows-
Elementary Level:

INCLUSIVE EDUCATION:
    Under Inclusive Education component of SSA, different activities are conducted where
all the field level functionaries play a vital role, to create public awareness, to provide


                                                                                                      321
                                Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




physical and academic support in school and home base situation and provide remedial
teaching programme etc.
   Samagra Shiksha - the Integrated Scheme on School Education envisages the ‘school
‘as a continuum from pre-school, primary, upper primary, secondary to Senior Secondary
levels. The Scheme covers all children with Special needs with one or more disabilities as
mentioned in the scheduled of disabilities of Right of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act,
2016 studying in Government, Government Aided and local body School. The vision of the
Scheme is to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education from pre-school to senior
secondary stage in accordance with the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) for
Education.
   Samagra Shiksha Assam focuses on increasing access to education, enrolment and
retention of all children in school as well as improving the quality of education.
Target Group/beneficiary of the scheme:
   The scheme covers all children from pre nursery to senior secondary stage studying in
Government, local body and government-aided schools, with one or more disabilities as
defined under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act (2016) namely:

   Gunotsav: Gunotsav is an initiative to bring qualitative improvement in schools
education system. It is a comprehensive census base evaluation covering four broad areas
viz. Scholastic (learning outcome), Co-scholastic & other areas, community participation
& contribution, availability & use of infrastructure. Children from classes I to IX of
Government /Provincialised, Tea Garden Model School, Adarsha Vidyalayas, KGBV and
Residential Schools were covered in Gunotsav. Schools have been graded on the basis of
performance as ‘A+’.’A’,’B’,’C’,’D’ with weightage of grading of school –Scholastic 90%,
Co-Scholastic and other areas 5%,Community participation & Contributions 5%. Notably
7846 schools achieved A+ for two consecutive years i.e. Gunotsav 2024 & 2025.

Gunotsav Integration: The Assam Government has made Gunotsav a regular part of the

SECONDARY LEVEL:
   The activities undertaken in the secondary level of schools during 2023-24 by the
government are—
Capacity Building of Members of School Management Committee (SMDC):
   The importance of effective science teacher training in Indian schools cannot be
overstated. Well-prepared teachers play a pivotal role in shaping the quality of science
education. Their ability to inspire students, nurture a profound understanding of scientific
principles, encourage critical thinking and problem solving skills is paramount. To address
this need, Samagra Shiksha, Assam has taken significant steps by signing MoU with two
esteemed institutions viz-IIT-Guwahati and Dibrugarh University.
   Under these agreements, a five-day, in-service residential science teacher training
program has been initiated. This program was conducted in multiple batches to
accommodate a total of 1400 science teachers at the secondary level. The program was
hosted at IIT, Guwahati for 1000 teachers, while another 400 teachers are benefiting from
training at Dibrugarh University. The training was provided by faculties of different
departments of IIT-Guwahati and Dibrugarh University on teaching methodology of
Chemistry, Physics, Biology, Mathematics and general English. These initiatives aim to
enhance the capabilities of science teachers, ultimately ensuring a brighter future for
students and the nation as a whole.




  326
                               Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



Pre-Primary Education:
   With the amendment to the Indian Constitution which made primary education a
fundamental right for every child. The launch of Samagra Siksha Abhiyan (SSA) by the
Govt. Of India aimed at universalization of the primary education in India.
There are primarily three learning goals highlighted in the NIPUN Bharat guidelines as
well as the NCERT Preschool Curriculum which correspond to the various domains of
development -
Goal 1:– Children maintain good health and well-being corresponds to physical
development (gross and fine motor skills) creative and aesthetic development as well as
social and emotional development.
Goal   2 :– Children are effective communicators
Goal 3:– Children become involved learners and connect to their immediate
environment.

HIGHER EDUCATION:
The Higher Education Department in Government of Assam has been playing an important
role for expansion and quality development of Higher Education sector through the
Universities and Colleges. The State Government has been providing adequate fund for
infrastructure development of these institutions as well as establishing new Universities,
Colleges and introducing additional streams to existing colleges to enhance access to
Higher Education. Govt. has also launched some new schemes under Higher Education in
the interest and benefits of the students in the state.

     TECHNICAL EDUCATION:
        Technical education in Assam started with the establishment of Prince of Wales
     Institute of Engineering and Technology at Jorhat before independence in 1927. It was
     followed by Assam Engineering Institute and Assam Engineering College in Guwahati in
     1948 and 1956 respectively. At present, there are 7 Govt. Engineering Colleges and 26
     Polytechnic Institutions in Assam. Besides the state-run technical institutes, there are two
     national level institutes, the National Institute of Technology (NIT), Silchar and Indian
     Institute of Technology (IIT), Guwahati.

HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE:
   Health care performance in Assam exhibits sustained improvements over the years.
These improvements are the outcomes of concentred and continued efforts of the
Government towards establishing an efficient system of health care and family welfare
through    effective   planning,     financing,     human      and    resources        management,    and
infrastructure and supply chain management. The State Government has taken consistent
initiatives to reduce prevailing regional disparities and gaps in the access to safe drinking
water,    sanitation   facilities,   public   and    private    health     care    infrastructure    rural
infrastructure, and access to preventive and medical care, public hygiene, information
system on health care and nutrition and skilled manpower.
   The TFR has reduced from 2.9 in 2005 to 2.2 in 2018. As per NFHS 5 report, the total
unmet need in the State is reported as 11%, while the unmet need for spacing is 4.1%
(NFHS 5). Kamrup district reported the highest total unmet need (17.6%), while Biswanath




  342
                            Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



reported the lowest (5.3%). Approximately 60.8% of married women reported to avail any
modern method of family planning in the State (NFHS 5); with sterilization acceptance
being 9% among females and 0.1% among males.
NATIONAL HEALTH MISSION (NHM)
    Government of India launched the National Health Mission (NHM) to carry out
necessary architectural correction in the basic health care, delivery system. The Mission’s
approach is relating health to determinants of good health viz. segments of nutrition,
sanitation, hygiene and safe drinking water. It also aims at mainstreaming the Indian
systems of medicine to facilitate health care. Various measures were taken by National
Health Mission (NHM) for child and mother’s health.
    The National Health Mission encompasses its two Sub- Missions, The Nation Rural
Health Mission and the National Urban Health Mission. The main Programmatic
components include health systems strengthening in rural and urban areas, Reproductive
–Maternal-   Neonatal   Child   and   Adolescent   health   and   communicable and    non-
communicable diseases. The core public health mandate of the National Health Mission is
to provide equitable, affordable and quality health care services to the people of Assam.
    The State Government along with National Health Mission has taken up schemes to
strengthen existing health facilities and also to build new public health infrastructure in
Rural, Hilly, Char, and Tribal and Tea Garden areas to reduce Infant Mortality Rate (IMR),
Maternal Mortality Rate (MMR) and Crude Birth Rate (CBR) in the state.

inhabitants in 2021. Similarly, Crude Death Rate has also shown a declining trend from
6.7 deaths in 2016 to 6.2 in 2020 to 6.6 deaths per 1000 inhabitants in 2021. Likewise,
Infant Mortality Rate of the state is falling significantly due to various health related
measures taken up by Government of Assam. The IMR of the state in 2021 is 34 deaths
per 1000 live births, while it was 44 in 2016 and 40 in 2019. In India, IMR in 2021 is 27
deaths per 1000 live births. Similarly, the Total fertility Rate has come down from 2.3 in
2016 to 2.0 in 2021, which is below the replacement level of 2.1.

LIFE EXPECTANCY:
   The World Health Organisation (WHO) defined life expectancy as the average number
of years that a person expects to live in full health. Life expectancy varies by geographical
area and by era. Life Expectancy of a person or population group depends on several
variables such as their life style, access to health care, diet, economic status and the
relevant mortality and morbidity data. However, as life expectancy is calculated based on
averages, a person may live for many years more or less than expected. According to the
latest data published in 2019-2023 life Expectancy in India is: Male 68.5, Female 72.5 and
total Life Expectancy is 70.3.In the same way Life expectancy in Assam is Male 66.9,
Female 70.7 and total 68.1



           Table 19.16 for life expectancy of Birth in India & Assam

   The above graph depicts that there is an overall decline of the Maternal Mortality Rate
(MMR) during the period from 2016 to 2023. However, the rate is still very high in Assam
in comparison to All India rate due to some major factors like infections and anaemia
during childbirth especially among rural women. There is a downfall of MMR at the All-
India level from 113 in 2016-18 to 88 in 2021-23. Likewise, at the state level, downfall in
the MMR was from 215 to 110. During 2017-19 the MMR of the state is 205 from while it
was 215 during 2016-18 against the all-India level the rate is 97 in 2018-20 and 103 in
2017-19. Factors responsible for downfall in MMR includes increase in institutional
deliveries, involving private doctors to provide free health check-ups to the pregnant
women at government hospitals, decline in child marriage, reduction in teenage
pregnancies etc. Moreover, a facility in public hospitals and health centres, free drugs and
diagnostics among other incentives to pregnant women has led to the increase in
admission for delivery in Government hospital.
PUBLIC HEALTH (SANITATION & DRINKING WATER):
        The Ministry of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Government of India, is the Nodal
Ministry for the overall policy, planning, funding and coordination of two flagship
programmes of the Government of India, namely, the National Rural Drinking Water




  348
                            Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



Programme (NRDWP) for rural drinking water supply and the Swachh Bharat Mission
(Gramin) [SBM (G)] for sanitation in the country.
1) Swachh Bharat Mission:
   In Assam, SWACHH BHARAT MISSION (G) has aimed at to provide Individual House
   Hold Latrin (IHHL) facility to every household in Assam. More than 32 lakh Individual
   Household Latrines (IHHL) have been constructed and almost 4 lakh dysfunctional
   toilets have been converted to functional toilets. In the year 2024-25, the physical
   target and achievement in case of household toilet was 76285 target and 5915
   constructed respectively.
   Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM):
   JJM is envisioned to provide safe and adequate drinking water through individual
   household tap connections by 2025 to all households in rural India. The programme
   will also implement source sustainability measures as mandatory elements; The Jal
   Jeevan Mission will be based on a community approach to water and will include
   extensive Information, Education and communication as a key component of the
   mission. JJM looks to create a Jan Andolan for water, thereby making it everyone’s
   priority. With the launch of JJM, Rural Water Supply and Sanitation Project for low-
   income states (RWSS-LIS) stands subsumed into JJM.

SOCIAL WELFARE:
   The Social Welfare Department, Govt. of Assam has been divided into two separate
departments namely Women and Child development and Directorate of Social Justice and
Empowerment. The contribution of women and child developments implementing various
schemes for the welfare of the Persons with Disabilities so as to bring them equally to the
mainstream of the society to live with honour and dignity. In pursuance of the Persons
with Disability Act, 1995 (now RPwD Act,2016) and through various welfare measures,
necessary efforts have been made to give them an empowerment in the fields, such as,
Health, Education, Employment, Self-employment, Sports and other all activities. The
schemes are as follows:


Women and Child Development:
   The Women and Child Development, Government of Assam aims at improving the
nutritional status of women adolescent girls and child in the age group of 0-6 years and
provides pre-school education to children of 3-6 years of age. The department also works

State..

POSHAN 2.0 ,(II) Mission Shakti and (iii) Mission Vatsalya. The schemes are as
follows:
Saksham Anganwadi & Mission POSHAN 2.0
   A) Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) Scheme:
       Integrated Child Development Services is World’s largest community-based
programme and is centrally –sponsored scheme and will provide the following six services
to the beneficiaries.
        1. Suplementary Nutrition (SNP)
        2. Health & Nutrition Check-up
        3. Immunization
        4. Non-Formal Education for Children in Pre-School
        5. Health & Nutrition Education
        6. Referral Services
        This services are provided from Anganwadi Centres and staffed with frontline
Anganwadi workers & helpers. The Scheme is implemented through 62,142 nos.
Anganwadi Centres (AWC) In the State. It is funded by Central and State Government in
the ratio 90:10 for general assistance and 90:10 for supplementary nutrition for all states
of NE region.

CHAPTER-XX

          SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT GOALS (SDG)
1. Introduction

1.1 Overview of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and India’s
Commitment

    The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), adopted by all United Nations Member
States in 2015 under the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, represent a universal
call to action to end poverty, protect the planet, and ensure peace and prosperity for all
by 2030. The 17 Goals and 169 associated targets embody an integrated vision of
economic growth, social inclusion, and environmental sustainability.

    India has demonstrated strong national commitment to the SDGs by aligning its policy
architecture and development priorities with the global framework. The NITI Aayog serves
as the nodal agency for coordinating and monitoring SDG implementation across States
and Union Territories, advancing the principles of cooperative and competitive federalism.
The launch of the SDG India Index in 2018 marked a major milestone in this journey,
enabling States to measure and benchmark their progress across the 17 Goals through a
data-driven and comparable framework. Over successive editions, the Index has become
a central tool for evidence-based policy making and inter-State learning.

    Recognising the unique developmental context of the North-Eastern Region (NER),
NITI Aayog, in collaboration with the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region
(MDoNER) introduced the North Eastern Region District SDG Index in 2021. This initiative
localised SDG monitoring to the district level, ensuring that progress is captured at the
most granular administrative unit. It also encouraged States to integrate SDG priorities
into their planning frameworks, fostering bottom-up development and local ownership of
the 2030 Agenda.

    Within this national and regional framework, Assam has emerged as an early adopter
and proactive leader in SDG localisation. The State’s institutional readiness, strong
monitoring mechanisms, and integration of SDGs into its development planning have
positioned it as a key contributor to India’s collective SDG progress. Transformation and
Development Department, functions as the nodal department for research, policy
guidance, and interdepartmental coordination on SDGs. The subsequent formulation of
Assam Vision 2030, Assam Agenda 2030, and the State and District Indicator Frameworks
underscores the State’s sustained commitment to translating the global goals into
actionable local strategies.

2. NER District SDG Index: Framework and Methodology

2.1 Genesis and Scope

    The North Eastern Region (NER) District SDG Index was jointly developed by NITI
Aayog, the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER), and the United
Nations Development Programme (UNDP). It is the first regional-level tool for tracking
SDG progress across all eight North Eastern States.




                                                                                   355
                              Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26




    The first edition of the NER District SDG Index (2021–22) covered 103 of the 120
districts across the region and established a baseline for future assessments. The second
edition (2023–24) expanded coverage to 121 out of 131 districts, reflecting improved
data availability and institutional collaboration across the States.

    The Index is modelled on the NITI Aayog’s SDG India Index, ensuring methodological
consistency, comparability, and analytical robustness. It provides granular, district-level
insights into the pace of SDG achievement in the region, enabling targeted policy actions
and resource prioritization.

2.2 Methodology and Data Framework

     The NER District SDG Index 2023–24 assesses the performance of 121 districts
across the eight NER States against 84 indicators covering 15 SDGs (excluding Goals 12
and 14 due to data constraints).

      Data Sources: 41 indicators are sourced from central ministries/departments, and
43 from state-level sources, ensuring both national comparability and local relevance.

     Normalization: Indicator values are standardized using the min–max normalization
method, rescaling data to a 0–100 range.

     Computation: District-level SDG scores are derived as the arithmetic mean of
normalized indicator scores under each Goal, which are then aggregated into an overall
composite score.

      Classification: Based on the composite scores, districts are categorized into four
tiers:

o             Aspirant: 0–49

o             Performer: 50–64

o             Front Runner: 65–99

o             Achiever: 100

This framework provides a uniform and data-driven mechanism to evaluate district
performance, identify developmental gaps, and promote inter-district learning.

3. Coverage Expansion and Data Improvements

The second edition of the Index (2023–24) represents significant progress in both
coverage and data quality:

   District Coverage: Expanded from 103 of 120 (86%) districts in the first edition to 121
of 131 (92%) districts in the second edition.

    Data Strength: Enhanced district-level data reporting and validation mechanisms have
led to improved accuracy and completeness across the region.

   Assam’s Participation: Assam achieved full inclusion of 33 districts, with verified data
for 64 out of 84 indicators, reflecting strengthened data governance and institutional
readiness.




    356
                             Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



4. Assam’s Performance and Key Outcomes

   Assam has demonstrated notable advancement in the 2023–24 edition, emerging as
one of the Front Runner States in the North Eastern Region. The State’s composite score
improved from around 68 in 2021–22 to 75.2 in 2023–24, marking a rise of over 7 points
and a visible shift from the “Performer” to the “Front Runner” category.

4.1 Positive Trends and Key Achievements

   Assam, with the highest number of assessed districts (33) in the Northeast, shows
substantial improvement in the 2023–24 Index compared to 2021:

• Overall Progress: 31 districts are now classified as Front Runners; the remaining 2 are
Performers. This is a significant increase from 2021 (23 Front Runners, 4 Performers, 6
un-scored)




• Data Contribution: Assam submitted validated data for 64 out of 84 indicators, enabling
scoring for all 33 districts, reflecting enhanced data governance.

• Scale & Complexity: This progress is notable given Assam's size, population (~3.1 crore),
and diverse developmental challenges compared to smaller NE states.

• Ranking of Districts: Three Assam districts lie in the 0–25 rank band, eight fall between
26–50, eleven sit in 51–75, another eight occupy 76–100, and two are positioned above
the 100-rank mark. This distribution signals steady state-wide progress while clearly
highlighting where targeted administrative support can be most effective.

5. Goal-wise Progress: Assam’s Sectoral Advancements

Assam’s improvement reflects coordinated interventions across multiple SDG dimensions,
integrating social protection, economic empowerment, and environmental resilience.

SDG 1 & SDG 8 – No Poverty / Decent Work and Economic Growth

      Orunodoi 3.0: Covers over 37 lakh women-led households, strengthening income
security.
      Mukhyamantri Mahila Udyamita Abhiyan (MMUA): Empowers 40 lakh rural women
through entrepreneurship grants.
      Chief Minister’s Atmanirbhar Asom Abhiyan (CMAAA 2.0): Promotes self-
employment and youth livelihoods.

SDG 2 – Zero Hunger

      Enhanced MSP for paddy (₹2,300/quintal) and incentives for maize and mustard
benefiting 40,000+ farmers.
      Procurement of 11,102 MT mustard ensures remunerative returns and strengthens
agri-economy.

SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being

     ₹4,257 crore redevelopment of GMCH and upgrade of district hospitals under the
Assam Health Infrastructure Development Project (AHIDP).
     Expansion of Ayushman Assam and Chief Minister’s Free Diagnostic Programme
improved health access.

SDG 4 – Quality Education

      Mukhya Mantrir Nijut Moina Scheme: Direct transfers to 4 lakh girl students to
reduce dropout rates.
      ASAP (World Bank Project): Strengthens early education, teacher capacity, and
STEM learning infrastructure.

SDG 5 – Gender Equality

       Procurement of 11 lakh Gamosas from 5.64 lakh women weavers enhances cultural
identity and women’s income.
       Gender Budgeting Units institutionalized across key departments to ensure
inclusive policy planning.

SDG 6 & 7 – Clean Water, Sanitation, and Energy

     95% tap connection coverage under Jal Jeevan Mission.
     Rapid LPG coverage expansion and solar rooftop installations under Assam Solar
Energy Policy (2023).

SDG 9 – Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure

     Implementation of Industrial and Investment Policy of Assam (2023) and Ease of
Doing Business reforms.




  360
                           Economic Survey, Assam, 2025-26



     Development of Bamboo Park, Plastic Park, and Tea Park clusters to strengthen
MSME competitiveness.
     Expansion of road infrastructure under Asom Malaand PM Gati Shakti for
seamless connectivity to industrial zones and economic corridors.
     Construction of major flyovers and bridges, including the Guwahati–North
Guwahati Bridge, Dispur–Khanapara Flyover, and the Bogibeel and Dhubri–
Phulbari bridges, enhancing urban mobility and inter-district connectivity.
     Upgradation of LGBI Airport (Guwahati), development of Rupsi Airport,
modernization of river ports at Pandu and Dhubri, and improvement of railway
connectivity to boost regional trade and logistics efficiency.

SDG 11–15 – Environment, Urban Resilience, and Ecosystems

      Mission Basundhara 2.0 digitized over one crore land records.
      Smart City initiatives and solid waste management systems in Guwahati and
Dibrugarh.
      Kaziranga Landscape Restoration Project and Assam Green Mission reinforce
climate and biodiversity goals.

SDG 16–17 – Governance and Partnerships

      Mission Sadbhavana improved citizen service delivery through time-bound
grievance redressal.
      SDG Coordination Cell, Assam, facilitates inter-departmental data monitoring
aligned with NITI Aayog frameworks.

6. Key Insights and Way Forward

      Balanced Progress: Assam demonstrates steady advancement across social,
economic, and environmental dimensions, with reduced inter-district disparities.
      Data Strengthening: Expansion from 28 to 33 districts with validated data reflects
improved monitoring capacity.
      Convergence of Schemes: Flagship programmes— Orunodoi, MMUA, CMAAA 2.0,
Nijut Moina—drive measurable SDG-linked outcomes.
      Targeted Attention Needed: Focused support is required for South Salmara-
Mankachar, West Karbi-Anglong, and Baksa to achieve uniform progress.
      Vision 2047 Alignment: Continued synchronization between the SDG Index and
Assam Vision 2047 will ensure sustained, inclusive growth.

7. Conclusion

The NER District SDG Index 2023–24 positions Assam as a data-driven, reform-oriented,
and socially inclusive state in the North East. The steady rise in Assam’s composite score
and near-universal district coverage highlight significant strides in governance, welfare
delivery, and institutional coordination. Going forward, Assam’s emphasis on equitable
regional development, climate resilience, and gender empowerment will be pivotal to
achieving the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals and realizing the broader vision of
Viksit Assam @ 2047.
